## NH Hunt 5 — 2026-08-21: Newbury holds every unit the Census names, and a green suite was hiding eight deleted tests

**03255 holds 48 of 48 government units, up from 28.** `pnpm twig:pair`
reconciles: 48 in the Census denominator, 48 held, 0 un-held. That is the
headline, and the reason the other twenty were un-held is the finding under it.

### Six of the seven towns were dark because the Census recorded a dead URL

Not because the towns publish nothing. Every one of them publishes a full
boards index.

| Town | The URL the Census of Governments records | What is actually there, 2026-08-21 |
|---|---|---|
| Acworth | `http://www.acworth.cc` | DNS does not resolve, and the Internet Archive has NEVER captured that host |
| Newport | `http://WWW.NEWPORTNH.NET` | answers 200 — a parked domain whose sitemap holds one Cyrillic "uncategorised" category |
| Grantham | `http://www.granthamnh.net` | redirects to the live `granthamnh.gov`; merely stale |
| Croydon | (none) | `townofcroydon.com` is a Squarespace "Coming Soon" page, and has been since 2024-12-19 |
| Windsor | (none) | `windsornh.gov` is a GoDaddy parking lander — a `.gov` that is not the town |
| Lempster | (none) | — |

A hunt that trusted the denominator's own URLs would have recorded five towns
as publishing nothing. **The Census of Governments is the right denominator for
WHICH governments exist and is not a source for where they publish.**

### The routes that worked, each now a branch in the playbook

`docs/zip-playbook.md` §8 records all of them with what each reached. The
highest-yield three share one shape: **the body publishes nothing, and somebody
else with a statutory or associational reason to enumerate it publishes
everything.** New Hampshire's village-district register (91 districts, 87 with
a phone) is the only publisher that names the Eastman Village District at all.
One read of SAU 34's school-boards page named three separate Census units. The
NH Association of Conservation Districts publishes the Sullivan County
Conservation District's address and *when its board meets*, which the county's
own 81-URL sitemap does not.

The other three: the `.gov` sibling; the Virtual Town Hall Drupal-7 `/boards`
index, where **Windsor's front page renders zero links to a plain client and its
`/boards` index renders ten**; and the Internet Archive at rung 11 for Croydon,
whose site is down to a plain client AND to a real browser — recorded as an
archive read with its snapshot date, never restamped as fresh.

### The structural blocker, and the narrow fix

The committed TIGER geometry is clipped to one county per state —
`public/geo/*.geojson` says `clippedTo 04019/34027/33013` on its own face — and
03255's first-rung circle crosses three counties. So six whole towns had no
DIVISION, and `scripts/build-registry.ts` refuses a curated body whose division
does not exist. Every board this session enumerated for them bounced.

`lib/registry/curated-divisions.ts` supplies the identifier, label, tier, parent
and real Census/NCES GEOID **without geometry**, because a registry division
carries none — geometry lives in `public/geo` and is served separately. RULING
57 says a body is NAMED FIRST and hunted second, and a body that cannot be named
because a map file was clipped is the opposite of that. Widening the clip is the
other honest answer and is the author's decision (`NH44`): `countyFips` is
singular per state, it names the ballot files too, and re-fetching TIGER changes
every served polygon.

The map cannot draw those six. `tests/municipal-layer.test.ts` was an equality
and is now a **reconciling pair** — drawn plus held-without-geometry equals held
— with every undrawable division required to state why in its own provenance.

### Two corrections this session made to its own work, both caught by guards

**Lempster was filed as `goshen_lempster_school_district`**, on the
reasonable-looking grounds that SAU 71 runs the schools as the Goshen-Lempster
Cooperative. NCES lists Lempster (3303303) and Goshen (3303304) as two
districts. Filing one under the other's joint name would have dropped a
government from the denominator.

**The shared body-name matcher bound `SULLIVAN COUNTY CONSERVATION DISTRICT` to
`Sullivan County Board of Commissioners`.** Its own doc block had called that
failure mode theoretical; it fired the same afternoon. Stripping ` BOARD OF
COMMISSIONERS` leaves `SULLIVAN COUNTY`, which the unit name starts with. Every
county in the country has both bodies, so it was a rule that would bind two
unrelated governments wherever it was pointed — and a false positive removes a
government from the hunt queue silently. The permissive direction is gone.

### NH31: a refresh that commits only when every source is healthy never commits

Run 32485680324, 13:12Z: 11 sources attempted, **10 read, 330 rows WRITTEN**,
one job-failed on an eventless VCALENDAR, and nothing committed. The ingest
signalled that with the same exit code it uses for "nothing was written at
all", so the workflow could not tell them apart and stopped before its commit.

At eleven sources that reads as flakiness. The per-source rate implied by 14
failed runs of 37 over eight days is 0.042, and a run that commits only when no
source fails commits with probability `(1-p)^n`: 62% at n=11, **`3e-94` at
n=5000**. Three outcomes now carry three codes (`lib/meetings/refresh-exit.ts`);
code 2 means the snapshot is on disk, so the workflow commits it and fails the
job in a final `always()` step. RULING 12 is untouched — the run is still red
and the source still named.

Nine reader-facing coverage statements deleted in the first pass. Then the same
defect one layer down, inside the document RULING 59 makes load-bearing: the gap
ledger printed *"2 of these govern part of this zip and are not in the
registry"* **without ever doing a lookup** — both were in it.

Then a section the source sweep could not see. The production capture at 85701
showed a heading reading **"NOT HERE YET"** over *"Pima County offices, City of
Tucson offices, and school-district (TUSD, Vail Unified) contests are not
curated yet."* `walk:all` passed 371 of 371, the RULING 59 guard passed, and the

to all three because the heading was three ordinary words in JSX, and the
sentence that made it a coverage claim lived in `data/states/az/ballot/az-pima-2026.json`
and never appeared under `app/`. **The guard now sweeps `.json`, because
reader-facing prose in this product lives in data as often as in code.**

Second session running in which a human reading a capture found what nothing
automated could.

### NH31, proven on the scheduler itself — addendum, 2026-08-21

Two dispatch-only runs, and the second is the whole fix in one job.

**Run 32543393133.** The ingest exited 2, the workflow CAPTURED that instead
of dying on it, and every step NH31 promised would now run, ran: the diff, the
browser install, the gate. The final `always()` step failed the job. Then the
gate itself refused — on `docs/tracker.md` stating 170 open rows against a
store of 177, because `pnpm tracker:add` had written the CSVs and crashed on a
workbook Excel was holding open.

That is a **red suite on `main`**, put there by this session's own close-out
commit and found by a scheduled job rather than by the session. It is also the
argument for fixing it in one sentence: **the refresh gate is the only
scheduled job that runs `pnpm test` on Linux**, so a spreadsheet open on
somebody's desktop could stop a governed artifact from ever committing, and
the reason would appear nowhere near the spreadsheet. `modeViews` now writes
the two markdown views first and attempts the workbook after, reporting a
failure rather than throwing through it (fourth merge, `99e48c5`).

**Run 32543652154**, after that fix:

| Step | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Refresh the snapshot | success — exit 2 captured, not fatal |
| Diff the governed artifact | success |
| Validate before committing | success |
| **Commit** | **success — `3a9068a`, 415 rows (353 fresh + 62 carried)** |
| A source failed for a JOB reason | **failure — the run goes red LAST** |

Under the old code those 415 rows were written to disk and thrown away.
RULING 12 is intact: the run is red, the failure is named, and a human is
told. What changed is that the good data survived the bad source.

# NJ HUNT 3 — 07866, 2026-08-22

## What was wrong when this session opened

`main`'s tip was red and production had not published since 10:17. NJ Hunt 2's
two close-out commits — `6fb14e4` and `be40ad9` — carried
`scripts/shoot-nj-hunt2-0822.mts` with five `TS18046` sites, build checks #196
and #197 both failed, and Netlify refused both deploys at 'building site'.

**How it reached `main` green, with the evidence.** The script did not exist
when the gates ran. It was added in `6fb14e4`, a CLOSE-OUT commit written after
the merge `78b0c10` and after build check #195 passed. The local and CI
type-check scopes are IDENTICAL and nothing needed changing: `tsconfig.json`'s
include carries `**/*.mts`, `next build` type-checks the same config, and the
gates job and both build modes reported the same five errors at the same five
line:column pairs. `scripts/` stays type-checked — excluding it would clear the
red and remove type safety from the extraction toolkit, `twig:pair`,
`control-query`, the move script and the walk, in a directory that only grows.

**The class, which is what mattered.** `pnpm handoff --ship` calls itself the
single door everything merges through. For CODE it is. For close-out records it
never was — they are committed after the ship and pushed straight to `main`
through no gate at all, by every session in this repo's history, and the shape
has now put a red suite on `main` twice. RULING 75, in `docs/rulings.md`:
`pnpm closeout` is the gated door, `pnpm main:green` asks GITHUB what happened
to the tip rather than asking the working tree, and `pnpm handoff` now carries a
`main checks` line that FAILS on red. It fired four times this session and
caught a red `main` that a local gate could not have seen.

## The headline number, re-taken

Last session's "5 of 178 units auto-resolved — 2.8%" was void. **The pair at
07866 is 90 of 142 units held, 98 bodies**, and Newbury holds at **47 of 47**
with 409 bodies after this session's class sweep.

**The far more useful number: 52 of 52 unheld rows read "no division of its
own".** Not one is a body somebody looked for and could not find. The gap is
entirely a DIVISION gap, in two classes:

| class | count | why |
|---|---|---|
| SPECIAL_DISTRICT | 18 | no TIGER polygon exists at any vintage — fire districts, sewerage authorities, a power authority |
| GENERAL_PURPOSE + SCHOOL_DISTRICT | 34 | real polygons exist; they sit in Sussex, Passaic, Essex, Bergen and Warren, outside the one-county clip scope |

**And the denominator matters more than the fraction.** 142 is the count inside
the first-rung 25 km circle, not inside the zip. The nearest unheld unit is 6.44
km away and the furthest 24.7 km; every government whose territory actually
reaches inside 07866 IS held. Reporting 90 of 142 without that sentence
describes a coverage-WIDTH decision as though it were a hunt failure. `NJ07` and
`NJ08` carry the two classes.

**The honest national read, replacing 2.8%.** Enumeration is per-place work and
routes compound, and the thing that compounds here is not the hunt — it is the
GEOMETRY. Nothing at 07866 was blocked by a wall or by a source that would not
answer. What bounds coverage is which polygons are committed, and that is an
architecture decision with a stated ceiling: `scripts/fetch-districts.ts` says
national coverage across these types is 13,000+ features, which ends the
committed-GeoJSON approach and forces vector tiling. Five adjacent counties is
roughly 1,000 more features.

## RULING 71 — the pill, and what it is not

`lib/geo/zip-certainty.ts`. Certainty is MEASURED rather than hand-listed, and
the measurement was already in a committed file nobody was reading:
`zip-governments.json` records, per government, how many of a ZCTA's 0.01°
lattice points fell inside it. Covering every sample means governing everyone
there; covering some means the answer is a fact about the reader's street.

The zip's total is the sum of its COUNTY-layer samples — counties tile the
country with no gaps or overlaps — **checked across all 33,791 zips in the
national file before being relied on**, not assumed.

At 07866: Morris County 64 of 64 and Morris Hills Regional 64 of 64, no marker;
Rockaway Township 55, Rockaway Borough 6, Denville 3 and their three local
school districts, pilled. At 03255 Newbury is CERTAIN and carries nothing, which
is the check that stops the pill becoming decoration. **Three of the four pilot
zips cross; 184 of the 279 zips this repo has committed geometry for do.**

**The RULING 44 distinction is recorded and mechanically asserted.** A
completeness marker says *we did not find this* — about our data, next to a
named person, worn only by the least-covered card. This says *this is a fact
about your street that only you can settle*. `tests/could-govern-pill.test.ts`
holds the pill's sentence against the same lexicons the RULING 44 guard uses, so
a reword drifting toward *we don't know which one is yours* fails the build.

## RULING 74 — an address, once given

`lib/geo/session-address.ts`. The RESOLVED OUTCOME — contest ids plus the street
the reader typed — goes to `sessionStorage`. **The house number and the
coordinates do not**, and a contest list cannot be walked back to a house.
Nothing reaches the server, nothing reaches disk, no schema grew a column, and
the schemas-share-no-joinable-column claim is untouched because it never becomes
a row. Lifetime is the browser tab. An address given in 07866 does not answer
for 03255. Verified as an image: the ballot page opens already narrowed, with no
second prompt.

## Three defects the verification found that no assertion would have

1. **The pill was on the US Senate race.** A statewide division is absent from a
   lattice index — there is nothing sub-state for it to be partial about — so it
   fell through to UNKNOWN and UNKNOWN rendered the pill. Caught by a capture
   script that prints its DOM facts BY NAME before any image is opened. A
   screenshot would not have shown it either: the defect is a pill that is
   present and plausible.
2. **The pill lost its invitation at 430px.** A media query hid "add your address
   to confirm" to keep it on one line. The DOM reported the full sentence; the
   IMAGE showed half of it. Stripping the invitation leaves a bare uncertainty
   marker, which reads as the badge RULING 42 deleted.
3. **The map's "Who governs here" card was the second instance of `NJ01`, still
   live.** At 07866 it read *"4 bodies govern the area around 07866"* and listed
   Rockaway Township and not Rockaway Borough. Found by reading capture 6 as an
   image, after the DOM probe on that same capture reported the wrong thing.
   Fixed; it now reads 4 of 8 and lists both municipalities and both school
   districts. `NH56` is fixed and verified.

## And one the walk found before a reader did

Widening the map's divisions took the coverage payload at 85641 from **2 bodies
to 61**: 85641 is Vail, the City of Tucson's territory clips that ZCTA, and
Tucson carries 59 curated boards and commissions. A Vail reader would have been
handed Tucson's Design Review Board and its Outdoor Lighting Code Committee,
every one wearing a "Could govern you" pill. **That is worse than the defect it
was fixing.**

`pnpm walk:all` reported it as a NAMED REGRESSION — M135, shipped by g15 —
rather than as a coverage number nobody was reading. A body arriving ONLY
through the widening must now be `GOVERNING`; a body on a division the point
itself resolved is untouched, which is why 85701 still carries all 59. The
counts are recomputed off the kept array rather than carried over, and
`WIRED_STATUSES` is imported rather than retyped — the first draft hand-wrote
`["WIRED","PARTIAL"]` against a real set of `["LIVE","MANUAL"]`.

## The clerk filing, and a defect that would have crossed two towns' ballots

Re-pulled: **272 candidacies across 90 contests, byte-identical** — the clerk
has not republished since `082126`. (The brief's "91 contests" does not match
the committed file, which held 90 before and after.)

The rebuild came back with **87** contests and four orphaned candidacy ids. The
contest id is minted from jurisdiction + office + DIVISION and the carry map was
keyed on division + office alone, so a REGIONAL school district — whose seats
New Jersey allocates per constituent municipality — collapsed three genuinely
different contests onto one. Every Chester and Mendham reader would have been
shown Washington Township's candidates for a seat they do not vote on. Fixed by
bucketing: **362 ids carried, 0 minted, zero orphans.**

The filing is on a RULING 53 clock with a **one-day** window rather than seven —
this document is not a candidate field, it IS the ballot.
`.github/workflows/refresh-nj-filing.yml` runs daily and gates like every other
governed artifact; `pnpm nj:filing:check` states the clerk's published count
against what this repo renders and exits non-zero on divergence.

**42 seats a party filed nobody for**, as the clerk publishes them: 25
Democratic, 11 Republican, 6 school-board seats with no party. One of the 42 is
a parser artifact — `DI01`.

What did NOT happen is the REST OF THE MANIFEST per contest, which is what
"walked" means under RULING 61, so no contest is walked in that sense and
`VERIFIED_ABSENT` stays at 0.

**Say the shortfall plainly.** The brief asked for every field for every
candidate in every contest, and said there is no partial completion in it. This
session found 24 fields of 816.

**Say the shortfall plainly.** This session built the machinery and the branches
and did not get through the ballot. What it has instead of 816 fields is four
committed tools, three named branches, and a measurement of what each route
actually reaches — which is what the next session needs and did not have. That
is a real result and it is not the result that was asked for.

## What actually limited it, measured rather than guessed

**The search index rate-walled, twice, and it is the binding constraint.**

- DuckDuckGo's HTML endpoint answered at 09:0x and was serving HTTP 202 with an
  empty body by 09:1x — **six queries**.
- Bing and Yahoo both walled after roughly **170 queries**. From candidate 90 to
  candidate 100 the first full walk answered ZERO queries and failed thirty.
- Of **26 public SearXNG instances probed**, three were answering with results.

The first complete walk got through all 272 candidates before the wall closed:
**148 returned at least one classified URL, 124 returned none.** That 124 is a
fact about one IP's rate ledger on one afternoon and may never be read as an
absence about those people.

**And one loss that was mine.** The re-walk of the 124 had reached 50 when it was
stopped, and it wrote only at the end, so those 50 are gone. The flush-as-it-goes
fix is in `scripts/nj-hunt4-search.mts` now and arrived one run too late.

## The three branches, and what each reaches

**`search-index`, made mechanically walkable** (`pnpm nj:search`). It has been a
manifest route id since v1 and never had a script, which meant it was walked for
the candidates somebody had time for — the ranking the equal-effort rule forbids,
produced by tooling rather than by choice. Five engines as a TREE, unioned:
three SearXNG instances at **rung 5** (the instance queries the upstream engines
from ITS server, so our requests are not on the walled ledger at all), then Bing,
Yahoo, DuckDuckGo, Mojeek.

Three mechanical rules make it honest:

- **A walled engine is RESTED**, doubling from a minute, capped at fifteen.
- **When every engine is resting, the walk WAITS** rather than recording a miss.
  "All four are resting for another forty seconds" and "nothing on the internet
  knows about this person" are completely different statements.
- **A 200 whose rows never mention the surname is not a document.** Bing drops a
  quoted phrase silently when the query is thin: `"Melissa BURNSIDE" Rockaway
  NJ` returned ten pages about a shoe brand. That rule caught it, and it caught
  the ALL-CAPS trap underneath it.

**The New Jersey municipal-roster branch** (`pnpm nj:rosters`). The county
publishes an index of every municipality's official website and it is not at a
path anyone can guess — three guesses answered 404. It is in the county home
page's own `href`s. **30 of 33 municipalities indexed, 167 pages read, 2 walls
named, 18 candidates found on their own government's page.**

**Per-person extraction** (`pnpm nj:extract`). A directory naming twelve people
and carrying nine emails says nothing about whose is whose. The block around the
FULL NAME, and nothing outside it — anchoring on the surname alone attributed
*"Janet Cassidy, Superintendent of Recreation"* to WILLIAM Cassidy and a vote
tally reading *"CHIRDO, Mabey, Lewis"* to Sean Mabey.

## Two rungs that fell

**The JavaScript-concatenated `mailto`, at rung 8.** Butler Borough's council
page carries no `mailto:` at all. It carries `a = 'rverdonik'; b =
'butlerborough.com';` — the anti-harvesting idiom every CivicPlus-era municipal
site uses. A plain fetch records "no email published", which is a false miss
about a councilman whose address the borough publishes on its own page. It
reached **4 of the 9 official emails found**.

**The filename as portrait attribution.** Proximity is weak — half these vendors
put the face in one `<div>` and the name in the next. These municipalities name
the file after the person, and a surname in the URL of an image on that person's
own government's roster page is the publisher saying whose face it is.

**And it is not infallible, which is why a person still looked.** Kinnelon
publishes `thumb.Franks.jpg` on a page naming *Cynthia Frank*. FRANKS is not
FRANK. Any doubt about identity fails at every door — refused, and her portrait
stays owed.

### NJ ELEC — the wall was on a different host

`NH71` recorded it as *212 bytes to a plain client, a JavaScript application
shell, rung 6 owed*. **Both halves were wrong.** It is an Imperva/Incapsula
bot-management challenge, not an app shell — and the records are not on that
host at all. `elec.nj.gov` is the agency's brochure site; the filings live on
**`njelecefilesearch.com`**, which answers **rung 2** at HTTP 200 with 166 KB and
no challenge. It was reached by walking **rung 5** against the walled host and
then asking the host the rendering pointed at.

**1,215 location codes read from the page's own option list. Rockaway Township 8
filed entities, Rockaway Borough 11, control 0 rows.**

**RULING 68 caught a false hit here.** The first working request used
`CountyCode` — which populates the municipality dropdown and is not a filter on
the entity search. The API answered **HTTP 200, 47,737 bytes, `recordsTotal:
326271`**, first row a union PAC from 1995. The control returned **byte-identical
output**, which is what named it. Without the control it would have been recorded

## Item 3 — the Wikipedia parser

`lib/hunt/wikipedia.ts` · `pnpm wiki:muni`

**39 of 39 Morris municipalities reached. 898 official rows, 261 distinct
officials, 818 citations CONFIRMED (91.1%), 45 LEAD, 16 UNREACHABLE, 19
NO_CITATION, 751 distinct citation hosts.**

The officeholder templates are the prize: `{{NJ Morris County Commissioners}}`
carries **seven commissioners and the three constitutional officers** — Clerk,
Sheriff, Surrogate — in one footnoted list, fetched once and cached rather than
39 times.

**Form of government as twig enumerator (RULING 87), stated as a pair: 176 seats
PREDICTED across 29 municipalities, 171 NAMED.**

**Six parser seams found and fixed, each written into the playbook §8.** The one
worth repeating: **sentence splitting must mask `<ref>` bodies**, or the sentence
ends inside its own footnote and every extracted person comes back with zero
citations — a confirmation rate of 0 of N for reasons that have nothing to do
with Wikipedia.

**And a defect of my own, caught by a guard that already existed.** A `" "`
written into `lib/hunt/wikipedia.ts` came out as a **literal NUL byte**, so the
ref mask replaced footnotes with NULs, `\s` did not match them, and the sentence
splitter silently failed. `tests/nul-bytes.test.ts` would have failed the build.
Class sweep: 1,073 tracked files checked, 1 found, 1 fixed, 0 others.

**Two misses were the SEED LIST, not the parser.** `Chatham, New Jersey` is an
area article with no government section; `Mendham, New Jersey` is a redirect with
no headings. A parser miss and a universe-list miss look identical in the output,
which is what the returned `headings` array is for.

## Items 10 and 11 — the two the author added mid-session

### The government graph — crawl it, do not list it

`lib/hunt/wiki-graph.ts` · `pnpm wiki:graph`

**174 entities, 118 official sites → 70 after a correctness fix, depth 7, 15,718
edges recorded, 268 followed, 3,936 left unexpanded and NAMED.**

**171 governing bodies the graph found that the registry does not hold**, against
a registry holding 12: **14 executive departments** (Banking and Insurance,
Environmental Protection, Education, Transportation, Health, Human Services,
Community Affairs, Law and Public Safety, Treasury, Agriculture, Corrections,
Children and Families, Military and Veterans Affairs, Labor), **40 agencies,
boards and commissions** (the Turnpike Authority, the Cannabis Regulatory
Commission, the Meadowlands Commission, the Delaware River Basin Commission, the
Motor Vehicle Commission…), **6 courts**, **12 legislative bodies**, **80
legislative districts**, **14 congressional districts**, **4 school districts**.

**The priority frontier is the finding.** A plain breadth-first queue spent the
whole budget at depth 1 — 260 fetches, 48 entities, 4,769 links unexpanded —
because a municipality article carries 150–350 outbound links. Capping depth is
the thing this crawler exists NOT to do; ordering is the fix. Expanding
departments, commissions, boards and courts ahead of the next municipality took
it from **48 entities at depth 1 to 174 at depth 7 on the same budget**.

**A correctness fix that COST a number, stated as a pair.** `infoboxWebsite`
matched the first `|url=` anywhere in the article and put a `nytimes.com` story
forward as the Division of Criminal Justice's official site. Citation templates
are now cut before the search and the result must be an official host: **118
"official sites" → 70 real ones.** Calling a newspaper article a government's own
page is a provenance error, not a cosmetic one.

**`meetingSchedulesFound` is 0, and that is honest rather than disappointing.**
An encyclopedia links a department's home page, not its hearing calendar. The
second hop — walking each harvested official site for its schedule and wiring it
into the meetings composite — is `DI02`.

## `VF02`: the instrument was breaking the thing it was measuring

**The basemap was never broken for a reader. It was broken for US, in every
capture and every walk this repo has ever taken.**

Playwright's `extraHTTPHeaders` applies to EVERY request a context makes, third
parties included. MapTiler's CORS preflight does not allow
`x-wtp-synthetic-run`:

```
Access to fetch at 'https://api.maptiler.com/maps/.../style.json'
has been blocked by CORS policy: Request header field
x-wtp-synthetic-run is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers
```

So the style request was refused, the map fell to the plain ground colour, and
the notice fired. **No reader ever sent that header.** That is why NJ Hunt 5's
photographs and its 371 walk checks disagreed: both were honest, and they were
looking at different pages. It was also handing our run identifier to every
third-party host the page touched.

**WALL or JOB: a JOB, and ours.** Fixed at the shared path in
`scripts/browser.mts` — the marker goes to our origin and is stripped from every
cross-origin request.

Two more defects fell out of the same investigation, both real on their own:

- **The notice had no way down.** `setTilesFailed(true)` was the only writer, so
  one transient error latched *Basemap unavailable* for the rest of a session
  over a map that then drew perfectly. `onTilesRecovered` now fires on `idle`
  with a real style loaded.
- **It told a reader to edit `.env.local`.** The notice named
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPTILER_KEY` on a civic map. Rewritten to say what they can see,
  what still works, and that reloading often fixes it.

**The walk checks that now catch it — two per zip, because they are different
questions.** *The reader is not told the basemap is unavailable* is the claim on
screen; *the basemap style has real layers* is there because a silent fall to the
fallback shows no notice at all. **All eight pass on production, 54 layers at
every zip against the fallback's 1.**

## The strongest record in the New Jersey hunt

`pnpm nj:winners` reads the Morris County Clerk's certified *Winners of the
General Election*: **263 winners across three cycles, 242 with an email, 246 with

That is M62's rung, and it is what makes 98 party labels on this session's cards

the certified record does not reach him — silence, not a guess.

## The gate that refuses a partial roster, and why it is not RULING 26 suppression

A roster is a claim about **who sits on a body**. Four of six members is not an
under-stated field; it is a **false composition**, and the two it drops are
invisible rather than marked missing.

So wiring is gated on the member count reaching the seat count the
municipality's own form of government declares. **Every member found is still
held, still in the artifacts, still hunted on its RULING 53 clock**, and
`pnpm nj:wire --dry` names all 20 gated-out bodies with the reason. The nearest
wins: Boonton 7 of 8, Dover 5 of 8, Netcong 4 of 6, Long Hill 4 of 5.

And a body with no roster renders the honest named gap, read as an image:
**"We know this body governs here because its division exists. We haven't sourced
who sits on it."** — a fact about US, not an assertion about them.

## `NS06`: the new Census key is ALSO refused

`pnpm census:key` is now a committed tool so this is one command next time.

| | |
|---|---|
| ACS endpoint **with** the new key | HTTP 200, body is `<title>Invalid Key</title>` |
| The same endpoint **with no key** | HTTP 200, body is `<title>Missing Key</title>` |
| An endpoint needing **no key at all** | HTTP 200 **with real data** |

The third line is the control: the host is up, the endpoint is right, the request
is well-formed. **The credential is the only thing being refused**, and the key is
40 well-formed hex characters.

**Offered as a guess, and marked as one:** a Census API key must be ACTIVATED
from a link the Census emails when it is issued. An unactivated key presents
exactly like this.

**And the failure mode CHANGED** — NJ Hunt 5 saw `302` with
`X-DataWebAPI-KeyError: 1`; it is now `200` with an HTML error page and no such
header. A check written against either symptom would now read this dead
credential as healthy. The committed tool asks whether the response is the DATA
requested, which survives both. **`NS06` stays open.**

# 2026-08-23 — Discovery Conduct: eight rulings that ask a session what it found off the list, and one address form where there were two

**Code SHA `87868c9` → PR #160 → `main` at `764758f`.** Production is serving
`764758f`, deploy `6a8aaa348a8df100081af031`, confirmed on `/api/build`. Close-out
records follow as their own commits and are labelled as such.

Gates at the close: **test 1749 pass / 0 fail · lint 0 errors, 11 allowlisted ·
`pnpm build` clean, the same command Netlify runs · `pnpm main:green` GREEN ·
`pnpm walk:all` 377 passed, 0 regressions, 2 could not run.**

**Rows this run wrote to production, named:** 76 search-log GETs (every
`/api/meetings` GET writes one), 69 ask/log requests, of which **9 rows landed**
carrying run id `walk-all-local@2026-08-23T08:18:43.814Z`. No reaction was
tapped. Two earlier local runs carried
`measure-battlecards-0823@2026-08-23T07:5*` and `shoot-conduct-0823@...` and ran
against a LOCAL production build, so they wrote nothing to the sold store.

## Part 1 — the diagnosis, and why more principles were not going to fix it

**Sessions walk the routes the brief names and no others, and that is what the
system asks for.** Scope is a ceiling by rule, the branch manifest is a checklist
with a completion condition, and the discipline rules correctly make speculative
moves feel like confessable defects. What nothing had noticed is the missing
half: **no report contract has ever asked a session what it found that was NOT
on the list.** A session that walked eleven known routes and one that invented
three produced identically-shaped reports and were graded the same.

**RULINGS 88, 89, 94, 95, 96, 97, 98 and 99** are law, in `CLAUDE.md` under
*Discovery conduct* and in `docs/rulings.md` with their rationale attached. 88
and 89 were held open on 2026-08-22 so the author could claim them rather than
have `docs/rulings.md` renumber a ruling of his; he claimed them here, and the
paragraph explaining why they were held is left standing with a dated `CLAIMED`
line beneath it.

| The brief called it | It is law as | Its name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | RULING 88 | The expansion requirement |
| B | RULING 89 | Expansion is not a side quest |
| C | RULING 94 | The stuck protocol |
| D | RULING 95 | Credentials are proven, not assumed |
| E | RULING 96 | Sources have freshness |
| F | RULING 97 | A founder find is a class-wide defect |
| G | RULING 98 | Exploration holds a guaranteed position in item order |
| H | RULING 99 | The amendment procedure |

**`docs/report-contract.md` did not exist and that is the finding.** The brief
asked this session to AMEND the close-out contract template every hunt session
uses. There was no template: the contract has been rewritten by the chat in each
brief, every time — which is precisely why the one figure that would have caught
the discovery failure had never appeared in it. **A contract that is rewritten
every session cannot accumulate.** It is now a file, it carries the seven
required figures with their denominators, and a brief may add to it but not
subtract from it.

**`docs/credential-ledger.md` — 14 of 15 credentials PROVEN by calling.** The
bar is all four of: the call was made, the transport succeeded, the body carried
the **control fact** saying it is about the subject asked for, and a deliberately
bogus **control query** came back different. Three of the fifteen rows failed on
the first run and **all three were this generator's own bugs, not the
credential's** — `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPTILER_STYLE` holds a style NAME rather than a
URL, and `WTP_DB_ROLE` is a DECLARATION of what `DATABASE_URL` points at rather
than a Postgres role. Both are now proven through the app's own code path.

The one real failure is **`CENSUS_API_KEY`**, refused again on 2026-08-22 with
`302` to `invalid_key.html`. `NS06` already holds it and stays open; no new row
was minted, because duplication is worse than a gap.

Two things worth carrying forward. **`DATABASE_URL` authenticates now** — the
recorded belief that it could not (a role made on the production branch not
existing on a sibling) is stale. And **10 of the 15 had never been proven by a
call in any session's walk**: the three MapTiler variables, `PLURAL_API_KEY`,
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, all three connection strings, `WTP_DB_ROLE`, and
`LEGISCAN_API_KEY`, which runs daily in CI but had not been session-walked.

**`docs/sources.md` now carries a last-walked date on every entry** — 45 of 54
recovered from git history by `pnpm sources:freshness --seed`, 9 `UNKNOWN`, and
`UNKNOWN` reads as stale rather than fresh. **9 of 54 are past expiry, and every
one of them is an UNKNOWN**: no dated entry is out of window. The fifteen
credential rows point at the ledger's date rather than this file's, because a
date here that disagreed with the ledger would be the register guessing about a
measurement the ledger actually made.

**`docs/expansion-log.md`** is append-only and guarded. `tests/expansion-log.test.ts`
reads the newest session in `docs/log.md` and fails when no entry carries that
session id. **It was proven to fail before it was wired**: with `njhunt6` on top
and no entry, it failed by name with the full RULING 88 text in the message. The
non-hunt exemption is claimed by the marker `-nonhunt` IN THE SESSION ID and is
never inferred — a test that inferred exemption would excuse a hunt session whose
label happened to look like housekeeping.

**The pinned block, and what it cost.** `scripts/context-file.mjs` reads
`CLAUDE.md`'s *Discovery conduct* section verbatim and it is exempt from the
shrink cascade — asserted at a 16 KB cap in `tests/context-pinned-conduct.test.ts`,
because an exemption that has never been exercised is one nobody has tested.
`context.md` lands at **40,924 bytes of a 40 KB cap**, and the price is stated
rather than discovered: **the whole tracker-change section (10 of 10 rows) and
the P0 notes clipped from 130 to 90 characters**, both printed in the file
itself. `NS09` puts the trade in front of the author, because on 2026-08-17 he
ruled the opposite way — *raise the cap rather than cut rows* — on this same
section.

## Part 2 — the 8/22 build

**WGH-5 first, because everything else depended on it.** Two implementations of
the address feature shipped on the same screen and disagreed about the one thing
in it: the map's narrowing chip promised, verbatim, that *no house or apartment
number* was ever needed, while the ballot's form refused to submit without one.

There is now **one resolver, one component, one promise**, and the resolver
returns **three states rather than two**. The interesting part is how ambiguity
is measured. The old `CROSSES` case decided it by **how far apart the sampled
points were in kilometres** — a proxy, and a bad one: a long straight street
inside one township is spread out and perfectly unambiguous, and a short street
on a municipal line is compact and genuinely split. `lib/geo/address-resolution.ts`
asks the question ambiguity is actually about — **do the sampled points land in
the same divisions** — **per level, independently**. So a street unambiguous at
county and municipal level and split at the congressional level **confirms the
first two immediately** and hedges only the congressional row.

The house number is used for one geocode and dropped in a `finally`. Coordinates
reach the browser only as a STREET midpoint and only when the street is
unambiguous. The footer promise was rewritten to the keepable one, and the guard
that pinned the absolute version was **rewritten to the same strength rather
than deleted** — three guards where there was one.

**WGH-1, measured and read as an image.** At 07866 the who-governs card went from
six rows each carrying *"Could govern you — add your address to confirm"* to
**six asterisks and ONE pill** between the Local listing and the State listing.
The old pill was dead — clicking it did nothing. This one opens the prompt.

**BC-1 to BC-4 — the P1 of Part 2, and the measurement is the report.** Every
person on the ballot page now gets the same seven drop-downs: *What this office
does · Positions · Committees · Offices near you · Campaign money · Voting record
· Sources*. **26 of 26 people at 07866 are reachable**, and four cards were opened
and read: Cory Booker, **Veronica Fernandez**, Justin Murphy and Joanne
Kuniansky, each carrying **exactly seven**. Fernandez is the one the author said
had *no way in at all* — an independent with no voting history, therefore no
voting-record link, therefore nothing. Her card was captured at 430×932 and read
as an image.

**The reachability number was 26 of 26 before AND after, and that is stated
rather than smoothed.** The pill always rendered; what was wrong was what it
opened. Booker's card showed campaign finance because the record lived behind a
SECOND modal — *"See their voting record"* — inside the first. The record is now
IN the card, and `IncumbentRecord` and its door are gone.

**BC-2's two empty states.** An empty voting record on somebody who has never
held the office and an empty one on an incumbent we have not collected are
different facts. Rendering them as one sentence is a null becoming an assertion,
and it makes a challenger's card read as thinner than an incumbent's **because
of copy rather than data** — the information asymmetry the equal-effort rule
exists to catch, pointed the other way.

**DEF-1 to DEF-4 — the refusal copy is gone.** *"We haven't yet read the law that
defines what this body can decide, so we're not going to describe it"* does not
ship again. Two layers: a CLASS definition that always renders, and the
form-specific one beneath it. **15 of 15 citations were fetched and confirmed
against a control string** (`pnpm definitions:verify`), and getting there walked
the ladder: rung 2 got 403 from `constitution.congress.gov`, `law.justia.com` and
`codelibrary.amlegal.com`; **rung 3, the full browser header set, got the same
403**; **rung 4, curl with the identical User-Agent, got 200 from all three**.
Reporting that as a wall would have put *we could not read the U.S. Constitution*
in this repo.

The class definitions are **state-scoped wherever the class varies, which is
nearly always** — a New Jersey township is a municipal TYPE and not a form of
government, Connecticut and Rhode Island have no county government at all, and a
single national county definition is false in some of the four pilot states
before this scales anywhere. **School districts were classified from the Census's
own INDEPENDENT/DEPENDENT split**: 291 independent, 4 dependent, **219
unclassified**, 2 TIGER pseudo-entities skipped. An unclassified district
deliberately gets no class definition — guessing independent on a base rate would
be a claim about who governs a reader's schools.

**JUR-1 swept as a class.** Morris County rendered *"Governs your area"* and
*"Boundary not published"* at the same time. `badgeFor` was never the defect — it
returns exactly one value. A SECOND path built the `Governs` row straight off the
division label with no reference to whether a boundary existed. **1 found, 1
fixed at the shared path**, and a guard now refuses any other site that builds
one.

**The brief was wrong about one string and it is stated plainly:** *"boundary not
defined"* does not exist in this repo — `git grep -a --untracked` returns 0. The
string is *"Boundary not published"*.

**JUR-3: there is no current-Congress ZCTA-to-district crosswalk, and the Census
does not publish one.** Four directories walked on 2026-08-23: `rel2020/zcta520/`
holds six files and none is CD; `rel/` holds only the **111th Congress** file
with 2010 ZCTAs; `rel2022/` and `rel2024/` are Connecticut-only; `baf2020/`'s CD
file is dated **2020-12-11** and `baf/`'s **2011-01-21**. `PU05` records the
route that does work and it needs no new machinery: adding a `cd` layer to
`scripts/build-zip-governments.mts` gives per-zip district counts nationally by
the same 0.01° lattice the who-governs pill already trusts.

## The regression the live walk caught, and it was mine

`pnpm walk:all` printed one NAMED REGRESSION: **g3's five-point scale separators
at 85701**. It was not undone — BC-1 put the funding block inside a collapsed
`CardSection`, and **a collapsed section does not render its children at all**,
so `.scale-sep` was absent from the DOM rather than merely hidden. This is the
SECOND time this check has followed the funding block: item 12 moved it off the
row into the card, and BC-1 moved it one layer deeper. The check now opens the
Campaign money section, and finds **4 separators on card 16 of 20**.

## Read as images — 2 of 2

Both captures were opened and read, and both showed what they claimed.

| Capture | What it claimed | What it showed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `battlecard-fernandez.png` | Fernandez's card carrying the same seven every card carries | Confirmed — Candidate / Veronica Fernandez / Independent, all seven pills, and the page-level collection line at the foot |
| `who-governs-07866.png` | the card at 07866 with 6 row marks and 1 notice pill | Confirmed — asterisks on the six part-covering bodies, nothing on Morris County or Morris Hills Regional, one pill between Local and State, and the basemap rendering |

Captures live in `screenshots/`, which is gitignored: they are evidence a human
reads, and RULING 20 keeps binaries out of git. The first version of the shooter
wrote to `data/audit/`, which IS tracked, and `tests/no-new-binaries.test.ts`
refused the commit — correctly.

## Two instrument defects found while closing out

**`docs/log.md` sorted the newest session last.** A session that only OPENS rows
— every session that finds more than it finishes — had no date at all: rows
carry `Resolved on` and nothing else dated, `Opened by` is a bare label, and a
modern label has no ISO date to fall back on. `docs/tracker-opened.json` has
recorded the date all along and nothing read it. Fixed in the generator, ISO
values only, because 89 of the ledger's 111 entries record
`reconstructed-2026-08-21` and that string sorts above every real date.

**The lint-allowlist gate was refusing on a clean `main`.** Five unlisted
warnings, all unused imports, proven pre-existing by stashing every change in
this session. All five fixed. `RO02` is open for the shape rather than the fix:
this check is not in `build-check.yml`, so a gate sessions run by hand had been
red for an unknown number of runs with nothing reporting it.


## The coverage numbers the contract asks for, measured after the ship

`pnpm exec tsx scripts/measure-definitions-0823.mts`, over all **1,253 bodies**
the registry holds a division for:

| | |
|---|---|
| carrying a CLASS definition | **1,013 of 1,253** |
| carrying a FORM-SPECIFIC definition | **216 of 1,253** |
| carrying NEITHER | **214 of 1,253** — 202 unclassified school districts (`DI03`) and 12 counties, of which the New Hampshire ones are `DI04` |

**The first run of that measurement said 636, and the 377-body difference was a
real defect it found.** Census LSAD 43 is "Township", and **388 of the 1,011
place divisions carry it — including every New Hampshire town.** All of them
resolved to the `township` class key, found no `nh` township row, and returned
nothing, while a New Hampshire definition written about exactly those towns sat
one key away under `municipality`. A township is a REFINEMENT of a municipality
rather than a sibling of it — which is what the New Jersey row says in as many
words — so `township` now falls back to its state's municipality definition.
Found by measuring, not by reading.

**LBL-1, over all 2,267 divisions:** the "Who runs it" field renders on **1,549**
and is **SUPPRESSED on 718** — 441 congressional districts, 201 state house
districts and 76 state senate districts. Nobody runs a district and nobody runs a
Senate seat; the field is removed there rather than renamed, and the
representation the card already shows is the correct account of that
relationship.

**The measurement script got its own denominator wrong first**, and it is worth
recording because it is the shape this project keeps finding: it counted LBL-1
over BODIES and reported 0 of 1,253 suppressed, which reads as *the fix does
nothing*. A congressional district has no body row at all, so a body-shaped
denominator cannot contain the cards the rule is about. **A number that
reconciles is not a number that is correct.**

## Hunt 6 hardening and the 8/22 visual pass, 2026-08-23 — the captures were in the repo this time, and reading them found the fix

**Code SHA `d0f2831`, Netlify deploy `6a8acefd4394a100080cf1a9`, PR
[#161](https://github.com/SeanJ22/We-The-People/pull/161). `pnpm walk:all` — 377
passed, 0 regressions, 2 could not run. Tests 1816 passing, lint 0 errors with
12 warnings.**

### The one-sentence version

The 8/22 walkthrough captures moved from a Google Drive folder no session can
open into `docs/feedback/2026-08-22/`, **all 21 were read as images**, and the
reading is what produced the work: three of the fixes in this session exist
because a picture showed something no DOM assertion was ever going to.

### What the previous session could not reach, and why that was the brief's fault

The 8/22 brief pointed at a Drive folder. A session has a shell and a repo and
no Google credentials, so the input was unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION — and the
brief then said *if the folder is unreachable, proceed and report that*, which
is permission to skip. The session took it and honestly reported that it had not
tried. **`LBL-2` came back "0 found, could not reproduce, did not guess" while
the image showing it sat in a folder nobody had opened.**

That is RULING 104 now: an artifact he places in the repo is an input a session
must reach, and unreachable is a defect to report rather than a permitted
outcome. It extends RULING 94 to visual sessions, which were outside its stated
scope.

### The four guards, which are the durable half

**RULING 100 — a partial answer that adds up is still a wrong answer.** A
council page says *nine members*; the reader came back with five; every
instrument said healthy, because every instrument was asking *did anything come
back*. Extraction now carries a count assertion against what the SOURCE states,
`EXTRACTED` downgrades to `PARTIAL` when it falls short, and a document stating
no count records `NOT_ASSERTABLE` rather than passing silently. The second state
is the load-bearing half.

**RULING 101 — our own identifier never leaves our own origin.** `VF02` found
two things and fixed one. The strip existed as four lines inside a harness that
nothing could test and nothing would miss; it is
`lib/ops/origin-confinement.ts` now, walked across all **14 of 14** third-party
hosts these pages reach.

**RULING 102 — fixing a generator is not finished until its output is
regenerated and diffed.** Each generator's whole source closure is digested into
`tests/generator-digests.json`; a moved digest fails the build. The git sweep
found **2 of 10** artifacts behind their generator. `tier-directories.json` was
behind its own dedicated script and was regenerated — content byte-identical,
only the walk date moved. `directory-source.ts` is behind a date helper shared
by nine generators and was deliberately NOT regenerated, because re-running it
restamps a `collectedAt` of 2026-08-16 without re-reading the data. That is
`NH80`.

**RULING 103 — a class sweep covers duplicated implementations.** Three copies
of an initials function rendered *Thomas J. Haynes III* as **"TI"**, and
grepping a symptom cannot find a second implementation of the same logic.
`pnpm dupes` reads **2,114** declarations across 806 files and finds 26 groups.
**Its own first version read 241 and reported one** — a sweep announcing nothing
found without having looked, in the instrument. Four copies of the outbound
User-Agent and two of the person-name normaliser are now one each; the other 24
are a baseline that only shrinks (`NH79`).

### What reading the pictures actually caught

**`MTG-1`.** The jurisdiction pill painted over the meeting date in every row of
the 48-meetings list. A flex gap fixed the overlap — **and the capture then
showed the real problem**: the wider honest pill had squeezed the body name down
to *"Rockaway Tow…"*, which is worse than the overlap it replaced. The badge
left the metadata line entirely.

**`MTG-2`, three instances of one rule.** The row printed the body name and the
jurisdiction twice, reordered. The popup printed the body name under a headline
that already said it. And the group heading said **ROCKAWAY TOWNSHIP, NJ**
before nineteen rows repeated it, so the ellipsis fell on the one fact that
distinguished them. The rule is the same at every level of nesting: only what
the enclosing context has not already said.

**`JUR-4`.** Nineteen consecutive *Could govern you* pills became **one**, under
the group heading, where every row shares the answer.

### `JUR-2` — the card stops asserting jurisdiction from a zip

The Rockaway Township card read **"Governs your area"** with **"Your address is
inside the area this body governs"** underneath it, to a reader who had given
nothing but a zip. 07866 holds three municipalities; the card picked one.

The badge gains a fourth state that says what is actually known, and offers the
one address prompt. The partial-division set comes from the same lattice
measurement the ballot page's RULING 71 pill already reads, so the two surfaces
cannot disagree — and **Morris County still reads "Governs your area", because a
county covers the whole zip.** Wired through a context rather than a dozen
component signatures, because a surface that renders the pill must not be able
to forget to wire it: the last dead pill happened exactly that way.

### `LBL-2`, reopened under RULING 97 and found

The previous session read the STYLESHEET, found no `nowrap` and no ellipsis, and
stopped. That instrument answers *is there a rule to clip this* when the
question is *is this clipped*.

**The cause is a property of `letter-spacing`, not of one card.** It adds its
space AFTER the final glyph, so a `0.15em` run is about a seventh of a character
wider than its own characters and all of it sits past the last letter. Against a
clipping right edge — and `shrink-0` puts one there — the clip takes the space
and then bites the glyph. **6 sites across 4 files, found by sweeping the shape
rather than the symptom, all 6 compensated at the shared classes.**

### `OFF-1` — 7 of 7, and why 6 were missing

Seven Morris County commissioners, one portrait between them. The photo store
records, for six of the seven, *"door 2, rungs walked 2026-08-15 —
`…/Board-of-County-Commissioners`: 0 candidate image(s); `…/Board-of-County-
Commissioners`: 0 candidate image(s)"* — **the same URL twice, recorded as two
rungs, and it is the board's INDEX page.** The seventh was walked at his own page
and returned a portrait immediately. Every commissioner's own page URL was
already in the registry as `websiteUrl`.

**7 of 7 sourced, 7 of 7 read as images**, every one a clean solo portrait.
Nothing shipped: `NH78` is the review row and the decision keys to the asset.

The script discovers the member pages from the board index rather than building
them from names, because **this session's first attempt guessed and lost three
of seven to HTTP 404** — the county keeps the period after a middle initial.
Three absences entirely of the hunt's own making, which is the same shape one
level down.

### `NS09` — there are no caps anywhere

`context.md` was capped at 20 KB and dropped its whole tracker-change section;
the cap was raised to 40 KB; by today the same cascade was dropping the same
section again and walking P0 notes from 130 characters to 90. **A cap forces
silent trimming, and silent trimming is RULING 100's failure one floor up.**

The cascade is deleted rather than loosened. **`context.md` is 45.1 KB with its
tracker-change section whole at 10 of 10 rows and its notes at full length**, and
`docs/log.md` — which clipped its lists to twelve rows each with an *"and N
more"* line — grew from 156,520 to 181,347 bytes.

What replaces a cap: every section states where it came from, and any block
claimed verbatim is tested against its source. **That sweep immediately found a
real gap** — the pinned conduct block named its source only at the END, after
the whole thing.

### `NH64` — the session-side resolve, built and used

`pnpm tracker:resolve <ID> --session=<label> --evidence <file>` writes the
resolution and stamps the closer as a SESSION, so the RULING 37 gate keeps
refusing a Needs Sean row while allowing everything else. It also requires
evidence and refuses a row the author opened. **Honestly stated: `tracker:move
--resolve=` already set a resolution.** What was missing and is now there is the
evidence requirement, the session-record entry, the RULING 41 refusal, and a
refusal that fires BEFORE anything is written rather than after.

Exercised on `VF03`, `PU04`, `NH77` — and on two rows this session opened in
error from a stale scratch file, which were resolved rather than hidden, because
only he deletes.

### What this session did not reach, and it is named rather than implied

`LAY-1` and `LAY-2`, `ASK-1` and `NH-3`, every Arizona item, `JUR-3`'s national
crosswalk, `JUR-4` on the ballot page, and the DEF completion. Six rows carry

done. **The layout work in particular must be built against the post-Hunt-6

## State campaign money, 2026-08-24 — the drop-down that structurally could not fill

*Session `state-money-0824`. Branch `claude/state-money-0824`. Sean's ruling of
2026-08-24: campaign-finance data for state, county and local candidates is
collected and rendered now, with election counsel reviewing afterwards on `B05`.*

**Four rulings adopted: 124, 125, 126, 127.** `docs/rulings.md` carries all four;
124, 125 and 126 are written into `CLAUDE.md` as law.

### The gap, stated as a fact about a card

Every Campaign money surface in this product was FEC-fed, and the FEC is
federal-only. `app/ballot/page.tsx` read `money: federal ? <CandidateFunding/> :
null` — so a Morris County commissioner candidate, who files with the New Jersey
Election Law Enforcement Commission, had a section that **could not fill.** Not
"had no data yet": there was no code path. At 07866 that was 235 of 272
candidacies.

### NJ ELEC — the three-way split, with denominators

| | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Candidacies on the certified ballot | 272 |
| In ELEC's scope (a municipal or county location code) | **235** |
| Out of ELEC's scope (federal office, or unresolved) | 37 |
| **FILED — candidacies with money rendered** | **58 of 235** |
| …backed by committee records | 65 |
| **NO REPORTS ON FILE — sourced and dated** | **177 of 235** |
| **LEAD — does not render** | 1 |
| Unresolved | **0 of 235** |

37 locations walked, 429 committees read, **0 SHORT extractions** against ELEC's
own stated `recordsTotal`. 297 second-hop filing calls, 0 failures. Contests
walked 90 of 90 — the loop iterates the certified ballot, so equal effort is
enforced by the loop rather than by intention.

### THE FALSE ZERO, which would have shipped

ELEC's committee listing returns `TOT_CONT_AMT` on every row. **Every value is
zero.** Not for the current cycle — for every cycle: measured across three
locations and four election years, twelve location-years and 158 rows, including
cycles finished years ago whose candidates demonstrably raised six figures.

The first working version of this collector recorded **202 candidacies as FILED
with $0 raised.** That is not a missing figure; it is a false claim about 202
named people's campaigns, and every instrument in this repo would have called it
healthy, because the extraction returned a number.

The money is one hop further on, at `GetEntityFilingData` — the page's own
network call, ladder rung 7. Two further traps inside it, both found by reading
rather than summing:

- **Amendments are separate rows.** Ann Grossi's 2023 committee files `R-1`
  period 3 twice. A naive sum reports $237,109 and is wrong. Rows collapse to
  the highest `AMEND_NO` per `(form, period)`.
- **A `D-1` is a certificate of organization, not a financial report.** After
  the filing endpoint landed, 63 of 73 records still read $0 because their only
  filing was a registration. Five more candidacies moved out of `FILED` into a
  sourced absence.

*And the period-versus-cumulative question was settled by measurement rather than
assumption: DeGroot's `R-1` period 5 is $24,977.25 against period 3's $39,777.95,
and a cumulative series cannot decrease.*

### What renders — read as images, 2 of 2

`screenshots/state-money-07866-card.png` — Tayfun Selen, Morris County
commissioner: **Raised $225,026 · Spent $229,526 · 14 reports on file, most
recently 22 June 2026 · Filed with the New Jersey Election Law Enforcement
Commission — see this candidate's filings. Read 24 August 2026.**

`screenshots/state-money-07866-absence.png` — Dino F. Cappello: **"No reports on
file with the New Jersey Election Law Enforcement Commission as of 24 August
2026."** with the reason beneath it, and never `$0`.

**Reading the first capture caught a defect the DOM was happy about**: the report
line printed ELEC's own form codes and a raw ISO date — *"14 reports on file ·
72/24 HR, D-1, R-1, RQ-2024, RQ-2025 through 2026-06-22"*. `72/24 HR` is an
internal filing-form identifier and `2026-06-22` is a machine date. Both were
removed before the second capture. That is exactly what the screenshot rule
exists for; a DOM assertion would have passed.

### New Hampshire and Arizona — reached, not extracted, and the difference is stated

**Neither is an absence claim.** Both are walls with dates and rung histories.

- **`cfs.sos.nh.gov` ANSWERS** — Node `fetch` gets HTTP 200 and 65,928 bytes.
  The app is an Angular SPA whose data endpoints were not located. **Rung 6, the
  live browser, is REFUSED 403 by the edge**, and so is curl; only Node's fetch
  passes. That inverts an assumption this project has carried — the ladder
  describes rung 6 as the rung a wall falls to, and here it is the rung that
  trips the wall.
- **`seethemoney.az.gov/Reporting/GetNEWTableData` is LIVE** (HTTP 200) and its
  parameter shape is not determined. `GetDetailedTableData` is a 404, so the
  name is exact. `robots.txt` and the terms path are both 404 — recorded as
  measurements, never as permissions.

`NH122` and `AZ02` carry them forward with the next branches named.
`docs/arizona-source-enumeration.md` gains the walked door so the AZ hunt
inherits a route rather than a name.

### The RULING 97 accounting — why the FEC directory was never walked

**What procedure would have found this without Sean?** *Read the reference data
already in the tree.* The FEC Combined Federal/State Disclosure Directory has
been committed at `data/reference/` since 2026-08-22 — 349 offices across 56
jurisdictions, public domain, no terms.

**Why did it not run?** Because nothing ever asked. The manifest tells a session
which ROUTES to walk and `docs/sources.md` tells it which SOURCES exist; no
report contract, no gate and no rule asked a session what `data/reference/`
already held. It was committed as evidence for a different question and then sat
there.

**What changed so it runs?** `pnpm cf:agencies` exists and its output is a
registered reference dataset, so it is now in the row-count gate, the pairing
gate and the regeneration register — three guards that go red if it rots.

*And the brief's own premise was wrong in the same direction, which is worth
recording.* It proposed seeding the directory from CFI's `stateLinks` page.
`cfinst.org/state/stateLinks.aspx` answers **HTTP 404** and `www.cfinst.org`
does not complete a TLS handshake. The seed does not exist; the better source
was already here.

### The directory — 56 jurisdictions, link-verified

`data/reference/state-cf-agencies.csv`: **56 of 56 jurisdictions have a
campaign-finance office named. 43 agency URLs alive, 43 control-matched, 12 dead
or refused** — the twelve named individually, six of them 403/503 to a rapid
sequential sweep and recorded as refusals-with-a-date rather than as walls.

**And it caught a partial that added up.** The directory files its FEDERAL
offices under the jurisdiction `WASHINGTON`, meaning Washington DC — and
Washington State is also `WASHINGTON`. A first-match search gave Washington
State the **Federal Election Commission** as its campaign-finance authority,
shadowing the **Public Disclosure Commission**. It reported *56 of 56* and named
the wrong government for one state. RULING 100 in a single row.

### Credentials — the leak was nine, not one

The brief named the Census key. A sweep **by value** — not by pattern, because a
Census key is forty hex characters and so is every git SHA — found **nine
distinct credentials** in plaintext across the Drive mirror and the local
transcripts, including all three database connection strings and the
**production write** credential.

**Nobody pasted a key.** `curl -w '%{url_effective}'` printed the resolved URL
back, and several of these APIs carry the key as a query parameter. **The Census
rotation leaked by the same mechanism** — the replacement was in the same file,
twice.

Old key proven **DEAD** (HTTP 200 with an HTML page titled *Invalid Key* — RULING
95's exact case). New key proven **LIVE**. Drive mirror **scrubbed: 6 → 0**,
verified by re-read. Repository: **0, before and after.** Local transcripts hold
all nine and were deliberately not edited. `NS11` is the P1 — **rotation is the
fix; scrubbing is cleanup.**

### `NH121` — the product was right, and the instrument had a NaN in it

03255 states 201 meetings and its group headings sum to 200. Reproduced on the
local build: the panel renders **`Show 1 more (1 hidden)`**, so 200 + 1 = 201 and
the clip is stated. The product was correct throughout.

**THE CAUSE IS A REGEX ESCAPE EATEN BY A TEMPLATE LITERAL**, and it is worth
stating precisely because two diagnoses before it were wrong.

`walk:all` reads the clip with `/(([0-9]+) hidden)/` — written inside a
`page.evaluate` TEMPLATE LITERAL. A backslash before a parenthesis is not a
recognised escape there, so it collapses, and the page compiled the escaped
parens as a **capture group**. The regex still matched, so nothing threw and
nothing looked wrong — but the groups shifted by one, index 1 held `"1 hidden"`
rather than `"1"`, and `Number("1 hidden")` is **NaN**.

NaN then poisoned the check in two directions at once. `200 + NaN` is NaN, so
the equality failed. And **`NaN > 0` is FALSE**, so the report took the no-clip
branch and printed *"group counts sum 200 across 7 group(s)"* — as though the
panel had rendered no clip at all. That is what the previous session read as
"renders NO more-button, measured not assumed", and it is why the 200-row page
limit was ruled out on the strength of a button that was there the whole time.

**Two wrong diagnoses are recorded here rather than tidied away**, because the
pattern in them is the finding. The previous session's was *the page limit is
ruled out*. **Mine was a timing race** — that the header painted before the
footer, fixed by settling. It is a plausible story, I wrote `untilSettled` for
it, and it was **wrong**: measured nine times from 0ms to 9s after the door
click, the button is present at every single reading, including t=0. Both
diagnoses came from reasoning about the symptom instead of instrumenting the
instrument.

`untilSettled` stays — it is a real robustness improvement and it costs
nothing — but **it fixed nothing**, and this document says so rather than
letting a shipped helper imply it was the answer.

The fix is to stop putting a regex inside a template literal: `indexOf` plus a
digits-only strip cannot lose an escape. Proven on four inputs including the two
that matter, with the old extraction shown returning NaN on the same text.

Newly ruled out by measurement: not an empty-key group — 0 of 456 snapshot
meetings have a blank jurisdiction, across 19 distinct values.

### One process mistake this session made, named rather than smoothed

I ran `pnpm run build` **while a walk was in flight against the running
server**. `next start` serves `.next` from disk, so rebuilding under it
replaces the chunks the walk is mid-way through reading — the failure mode is a
server that 500s its own assets and a walk whose results mean nothing.

The run was **discarded rather than reported**, the server was killed, the build
was run to completion first, and the walk was re-run clean. It cost about twenty
minutes and no correctness. It is recorded because a walk result is only worth
what the conditions it ran under were worth, and a session that quietly kept a
contaminated run would have reported numbers it could not stand behind.

### Gates

`test 2087 of 2087` · `lint 0 errors` (13 pre-existing warnings, none in a file
this session wrote) · `tsc --noEmit` clean · `pnpm build` green ·
`pnpm regen` 15 of 15 current · `pnpm credentials` **15 of 15 proven**.

**`pnpm walk:all` against the LOCAL production build (RULING 125): 368 checks
ran, 0 NAMED REGRESSIONS, 11 declared COULD NOT RUN, 0 silent.**

Three of the eleven are new and are this session's doing, correctly: the
`/api/build` SHA, deploy-id and distinctness checks ask PRODUCTION-ONLY
questions, and a local build has no Netlify environment. Left as failures they
would have reported three NAMED REGRESSIONS on every local walk from now on —
an alarm created by this session's own ruling, wrong on every quiet day. They
report CANNOT RUN and name `pnpm deploy:live` as the way to ask.

`docs/walk-checks.txt` is deliberately NOT rewritten: the baseline records what
the PRODUCTION suite runs and a local walk cannot reach every check. The diff
still ran against the committed file, and the 11 unreachable checks are named
individually rather than counted.

**One flaky check, named rather than claimed as fixed.** *85701: north Tucson
renders crisp, not muted, at city zoom* failed on two earlier runs of this
session (delta 8.62 against a 2.5 bar) and PASSED on the clean one. Nothing in
this session touched that surface. It is recorded as flaky under a contaminated
build rather than as something this work repaired.

## Audit remediation, 2026-08-24 — every finding was reasoned, so every fix was reproduced first

Two external audits of `ae5b178` (code head `336a3eb`) — one for correctness,
one for performance — returned eight findings, two systemic patterns and six
performance items. **The auditor could not run code**, so nothing they reported
had been observed happening. That made the session's law simple and it is the
only reason this record is worth reading: **no fix shipped without its finding
first reproduced against the code as shipped.**

**Eight of eight correctness findings reproduced. None disputed. One correction
to an auditor's example, recorded rather than smoothed.**

The reproductions were not ceremony. Three of them changed what the fix had to
be:

- **A-005's example was one slug too wide.** The finding described two boards
  meeting at 7pm collapsing into one meeting. Read against the code that cannot
  happen — the id is namespaced by wiring row, so two boards produce two ids.
  The defect is real and one level in, WITHIN a row, where a town publishes
  "Zoning Board of Adjustment" and "Zoning Board of Adjustment Public Hearing"
  at the same start and both match the row's title filter. **A fix built for the
  example as written would have been a fix for nothing.**
- **A-002's stated invariant could not hold.** The brief wrote `produced +
  dropped + outOfWindow + unretrieved === input` and, two sentences later,
  required that document counts never be compared with event counts. Those
  cannot both be true: `unretrieved` counts DOCUMENTS. The first implementation
  added them anyway and `ical`'s own refusal fixtures failed with *1 more
  disposition than records* — the contract catching its author mixing two
  layers.
- **P-002's first attempt made the bundle BIGGER.** Converting the three
  components that resolve a typed zip moved the landing page from 2,955,835 to
  2,956,534 raw bytes, because one static importer remained in a hook. The
  change was worth exactly nothing until that moved too, and the measurement is
  the only thing that said so.

### What is measurably different

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Landing page initial JS (this machine, standalone) | 2,955,835 raw · 852,947 gzip · 14 chunks | **1,995,824 raw · 524,646 gzip · 13 chunks** |
| Exact polygon tests per division lookup | 2,291 | **14** |
| Resolver geometry | 26 files · 2,291 features · 118,533 coordinates | **25 · 1,850 · 38,418** |
| DOM writes on a 500→480 pin filter | 20 removes + 20 later creates | **20 visibility writes, 0 creates, 0 removes** |
| DOM writes to select one pin | 500 | **1** |
| Raw email addresses in a reader collection store | 1 | **0** |
| Search-log rows that are ours | 11,755 of 14,877 | **0 of 3,122** |

Every one of those is a measurement taken twice on the same instrument, which
is now law: **RULING 133 — a performance change ships with its measurement.**

### The three that were about our own instruments lying

**A-008.** `pnpm main:green` — the gate every session's close-out trusts under
RULING 75 — returned GREEN when a required check had completed having executed
zero steps. Its own test carried the comment *"That is not green"* above an
assertion that only checked it was not RED, which GREEN satisfies. The prose and
the assertion had disagreed since the day it was written and the prose lost
silently. Audited across the last 20 green readings on `main`: **0 were false**,
which is the honest number and not a comforting one — the defect was real and
had not yet fired.

**A-002.** `accountedNormalize` asked a boolean. 100 logical inputs, 0 output and
one recorded drop was branded as a fully-accounted result: **one drop laundering
ninety-nine disappearances.** RULING 43 asks whether a pass produced NOTHING and
is silent about a pass that produced SOME, which is RULING 100 one layer down.

**A-003.** Document validity depended on which transport rung happened to
succeed — the same bytes refused on rung 2 and accepted on rung 3. And the
branch was gated on `!options.fetchImpl`, so **no test in this repo could reach
it.** That is the chromium-pin shape: a production path nothing observes.

### A-001, which is the one that touched the constitution

`CLAUDE.md` says without qualification that no store carries a column that could
join to another. `feedback.reply_to` held a raw email address.
`questionnaire_invitations.email` holds a raw email address. One value space,
two tables, equality-joinable.

**The guard that was supposed to catch it checked column NAMES.** `reply_to`
does not contain the letters `email`, so it was added to a carefully-written
exception set and waved through — RULING 110's wrong-form search, living inside
a test.

The address moved to a contact-delivery store behind a handle minted with
`randomUUID`, never derived, because a shared deterministic hash is the same
join key relocated. Migration applied to production and **verified by reading
the catalog back** rather than by trusting `db:apply`'s own per-statement OK. 3
feedback rows exported to a dated backup outside the repo first; 1 carried an
address; 1 address in the delivery store afterwards; 0 handles resolving to
nothing.

Two things the work found on the way, both stated: the reply address was **never
readable** — `pnpm feedback:read` did not select it, so R41's field had been
collected and never surfaced since it shipped — and the delivery store IS joined
by that handle on that one author-only path, which is a deviation from the
brief's "joined to nothing" and is written down where the query is.

### What did not get done, and why

**P-005 stays OPEN.** `pnpm perf` ran against a local production build and
reported *hardware acceleration OFF or UNKNOWN* with `NaN` for every frame
metric. `docs/perf-baseline.md` was **not committed**, which is the harness
working rather than the work failing: a number describing a software rasterizer
in the place a reader's hardware belongs would be inherited by every budget set
from it afterwards.

**P-006 is measured, and measuring it found a defect in itself.** Across three
real build-check runs: the build legs went 73s to 51s and 65s to 53s with cache
hits confirmed in the log, while gates stayed at ~195s — because that job is 96s
of test, 24s of lint and 20s of types against a 3s install, and saying so is more
useful than a percentage. A merge is not faster; Actions minutes fall by about
34s a run, which is what RULING 78 is about.

The defect: the Playwright cache key read `node_modules/playwright-core`, which
pnpm does not hoist, so the version came back empty and the key resolved to the
bare prefix `playwright-Linux-`. Worse than a miss — the post-step would save
under a version-less key and restore a stale browser after every upgrade. The
step reads `playwright` now and EXITS NON-ZERO on an empty version rather than
composing a key out of nothing. **A step whose product is a string must be asked
whether it produced one**, which is the same sentence as RULING 113 and was
found by applying it.

**0 of 9 leaked credentials are rotated**, proven rather than assumed: the
by-value sweep still finds every current value in a leaked location. Only Sean
can rotate them. What this session could do it did — the Drive mirror was found
dirty AGAIN, with six occurrences of five live credentials, and the cause is now
named: `handoff` re-runs the transcript exporter, which rewrites the mirror out
of the local `.jsonl` files that are deliberately never scrubbed. **A hand-run
scrub was only ever true until the next handoff.** It scrubs at the output
channel now and re-reads to confirm.

### The walk, and one regression this session caused and one it did not

`pnpm walk:all` against the local production build (RULING 125): **366 checks
passed, 1 named regression, 12 declared could not run, 0 silent.**

**The one I caused, and fixed before the session ended.** Moving the marker
pool to hold every venue in the data is P-001's fix, and it left a hole at the
other end: `applyVisibility` writes only the keys whose visibility CHANGED, so
a marker created for a venue the current filter EXCLUDES was in neither loop —
never written, `data-hidden` unset, and **visible on the map**. Twenty pins
showing that should not have been. A new marker is created hidden now, and two
guards assert it. **The counters could not see this**, which is the lesson worth
keeping: they count WRITES, and the defect was the absence of one.

**The one I did not, attributed rather than assumed.** g9's fan check reads *4
pins in the stack; 4 fanned; every pair now clears 28px: false*. A worktree at
`ae5b178` — the head this session opened on, before any change here — was built,
served and walked, and **it fails the same check with byte-identical numbers.**
The previous session's zero-regression reading was taken against a different
day's snapshot, where fewer pins happened to collide. It is `NH144`, and the
likely cause is the fan radius against a stack of four rather than two.

**`docs/feedback/8.24/` was empty.** The session's first act was to be committing
sixteen captures unread; there were none, and git cannot track an empty
directory. The refinement it was meant to unblock is law anyway — RULING 135, a
fence bars acting on content and never registering the author's artifacts — so
the next batch lands without the collision.
