# 2026-08-27 — THE DETECTIVE SESSION: 85641

**Every government this session added was found somewhere the government does
not choose to publish.** Not one of the seven came from a directory.

## What a reader at 10723 S Bear Table Tank Drive, Vail AZ 85641 gets now

**7 governing and advisory bodies, from 2.** Verified against a local
production build, at a point two geocoders agree on to 8 metres.

| Body | How it was found | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pima County | already held | LIVE |
| **Regional Flood Control District** | A.R.S. 48-3603 + the district's own formation page | LIVE, Legistar |
| **Free Library District** | A.R.S. 48-3901(C) and 48-3903 | LIVE, Legistar |
| **Stadium District** | the county's own sitemap; A.R.S. 48-4202 | LIVE, Legistar |
| **Central Arizona Water Conservation District** | the county's LEVY RESOLUTION | LIVE, **new CivicClerk adapter** |
| Vail Unified | already held | LIVE |
| **Board of Adjustment District 4** | its own agenda's second column | KNOWN_UNCOVERED |

**And 23 ballot contests, from 18.** `/ballot?zip=85641` now renders
Proposition 425 (Pima County's $70,000,000 Permanent Base Adjustment),
Proposition 423 (the Vail override), Corporation Commissioner, the Vail
school-board cancellation as a cited authority absence, and the Proposition 427
coverage note. `/api/ballot/scope` at that address adds **State Senate and
House District 17**, which half of 85641 sits in and which the file did not
carry at all.

## The five things worth carrying to another state

**1. The county's LEVY RESOLUTION is the taxing universe.** A.R.S. §§ 42-17101
to 42-17110: one resolution each August for every entity that taxes property in
the county. A government can publish nothing, appear in no directory, own no
domain and sit on no boundary layer, and it still cannot avoid being in it,
because somebody has to collect its money. Pima's names **38 jurisdictions and
classes across 143 levy lines** — and it CORRECTS the county: the county's own
Community Facilities Districts page lists two, the levy names nine. `pnpm
az:levy`.

**2. The state education agency is a meeting source for every school district.**
A.R.S. § 15-905(C) compels a hearing notice, and `budgetsystem.azed.gov` posts
it: date, time, venue, street address, named agenda contact, plus the district's
tax rates. **Empire Elementary School District No. 37 operates no schools and
employs no staff** — a *transportation-only district*, a class this project did
not know existed — and two official enumerations record its website field as
BLANK, which that structure helps explain. Its board meeting came out of a
filing system instead. *(Corrected 2026-08-27: this said the district would
never have a website. The evidence supports the blank field and its likely
cause; it does not establish permanent absence, and a plausible explanation is
not a verified permanent fact.)*

**3. The canvass is not the ballot.** A certified canvass carries CONTESTED
races only; the election authority's OFFICIAL CANDIDATE LIST is the ballot
universe. Pima's canvass names 15 races and its candidate list 34 contests and
101 candidates. Building a ballot from the canvass drops every unopposed seat
silently, in the direction that looks like completeness.

**4. A district with no boundary layer still has a boundary — as a PLAT.** A
community facilities district is formed by a resolution that must recite its
land by recorded book and page, and the county maps its recorded plats for
unrelated reasons. `pnpm cfd:territory` joins them and point-tests the result.
It PROMOTED Rocking K South (25 of 25 plats inside ZCTA 85641) and KILLED
Wildflower (85757) in the same pass — a lead the project had carried as strong.

**5. When a portal ships as an EMBED, the tenant slug is in the page.** The
CAWCD's meetings page renders no meeting, and carries
`window.clerkEmbedProps = {"tenant": "capaz"}`. With that, CivicClerk's own
OData API answers a plain GET. New adapter, new `AgendaSourceType`.

## Two corrections this session made to itself

**An uncovered government correctly makes coverage look worse.** Adding the
CAWCD with no adapter moved both Pima pilot ZIPs from `NONE_SCHEDULED` to
`NO_SOURCE`. The available shortcut was to leave the district out and keep the
greener number; CLAUDE.md forbids exactly that. The district went in, then the
adapter did, and `tests/coverage.test.ts` records the arc rather than the
answer.

**All five district bodies were given the county's Legistar calendar, and one
of them does not meet there.** Four are the Board of Supervisors sitting as
them; the CAWCD is directly elected and holds its own meetings. Sending its
readers to the county calendar would have sent them to the wrong room. The
agenda source is now per row.

## Instruments

`pnpm cfd:territory`, `pnpm az:levy`, `lib/sources/civicclerk/`,
`pnpm method:learn-85641`. Method version **19 → 27**, routes **80 → 88**.

## The instrument finding that cost the most and matters most

**Three documents from one county, three different correct PDF extractors.**
The ballot candidate list needs `pdftotext -layout` for office attribution and
pdfjs for name spelling — two of three extractors agreed with each other and
were both wrong, welding a form's rule glyph onto a state senator's surname.
The levy resolution needs pdfjs, because `-layout` offsets its label column one
row from its numbers and would publish the Flood Control District's tax rate
beside Debt Service. The Board of Adjustment agenda needs `-layout`, because
pdfjs interleaves its two columns and makes the Executive Secretary a board
member.

**There is no right extractor, only a right one per document.** The check that
makes it safe is to read a row whose answer you already know before trusting
the run. That check caught a $146,498,365 school levy filed under HEALTH
DISTRICTS during development.

# 2026-08-27 — THE COVERAGE-TRUTH SESSION

**Every defect this session repaired was invisible to a count, and every one of
them was visible the moment two layers were asked the same question separately.**

The session was gated behind two preflights and both were larger than the briefs
that described them. It spent itself on those, on the four red controls the
author's visual review produced, and on the three instruments the brief asked
for. Ten commits, seven of seven gates green on each.

## The five integrity defects, and what each one actually was

**NH232 — the registry had four writers, not two.** `pnpm registry:build`
regenerates `lib/registry/registry.json` whole; `adjudicate-leads.mts` and
`census-gap-walk.mts` each appended promoted bodies to it in place; and
`normalize-census-placeholders.mts` rewrote labels inside it. A generated output
was three other scripts' canonical store, so running the generator deleted 731
verified bodies — the promoted population that IS the coverage numerator the
governance snapshot reports — and nothing went red. `lib/registry/promoted-bodies.json`
is now the canonical INPUT, `appendPromotedBodies()` its only write path, and
the generator merges it. Reconciled independently of the registry: 674 distinct
`BODY_PROMOTED` bodyIds in canonical work state against 674 DESCENT rows, zero
stranded either way.

**A geographic key was being used where a seat key was required.** Ballot
incumbency asked `seatHoldersForDivision(contest.ocdId)` — *who holds something
in this division* — and read the answer as *who holds this seat*. For the AZ
Governor contest that call returns **Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego**, so the
sitting Governor was labelled **Challenger** on the ballot while her own map
card said Incumbent. Sixteen division keys in the pilot ballots host more than
one elected office. `lib/officials/office-identity.ts` gives an office a
canonical identity — built from the 52 distinct contest titles on the four pilot
ballots, classifying all 141 contests with zero unclassified — and the join is
now `(division, office)`.

**A body was taking its members from its geography.** 74 of 1,998 registry
bodies rendered named people through `governingRosterHoldersForDivision` and
through nothing else: CAWCD showed the five Pima County Supervisors over a
popularly elected 15-member board, and 58 appointed Tucson commissions each
showed the Mayor and Council. Deleting the fallback alone would have replaced
false claims with false absences, because some of those bodies really are
another government sitting as a board — so `data/states/az/officials/body-compositions.json`
models the relationship explicitly and every alias carries the document that
makes it lawful. **CAWCD and the flood control district hang off the same
division and now give different answers**, which no geographic fallback could
do.

**A meeting was taking its body from its geography too.** 364 of 460 meetings
would render on a body that did not hold them. `Meeting.bodyId` now travels from
the wiring row that produced the meeting, across all 13 construction sites; 460
of 460 carry one.

**And a body's own schedule was rendering as its absence.** CAWCD's card read
"0 upcoming" while the board's published 2026 schedule listed meetings on
3 September, 1 October, 5 November and 3 December. The wiring was correct and the
snapshot predated it — `civicclerk` did not appear in the snapshot's own list of
sources at all, which made "returned nothing" and "was never asked"
indistinguishable from the file.

## Two claims corrected, and one government un-stranded

**NH233.** The Rocking K South Community Facilities District is a taxing
subdivision of 85641 that reached nobody, because the smallest division
containing it is `county:pima` — 9,200 square miles against 2,047 acres — so its
`ocdId` was correctly null and it was stranded. Worse, with a null `ocdId` the
card said *"Boundary not published"*, which is false: the county recorder
publishes it, as a recorded plat. The geometry was being fetched all along and
discarded. It is now emitted and point-tested with the same even-odd
implementation that decides every other government, and the answer is exact in
both directions — a reader inside a Rocking K plat is governed by it; the Vail
address at 10723 S Bear Table Tank Drive is not.

**The Empire permanent-absence claim.** Four documents said the district *will
never have a website*. The evidence — transportation-only, no schools, no staff,
two official enumerations recording a blank website field — is real and narrower
than the sentence. A permanent absence retires the recheck, which is how a
plausible cause becomes a fact nobody looks at again.

## Three instruments

`pnpm coverage` compares four layers that do not share a source. Its two Census
enumerators disagree by construction — the ZIP crosswalk resolves 0 of 39,555
special districts nationally — and the disagreement is preserved rather than
resolved. Across four pilots: **0 integrity defects over 20 measured surfaces,
9 coverage gaps, and 16 surfaces named as unmeasurable with what is missing for
each.**

`pnpm run doctor` reports 15 capabilities with a remediation on every non-PASS,
and never calls a credentialed endpoint. `pnpm corpus:check` measures seven
artifact classes against a provenance contract: 4 conform, 1 supports change
detection, and `public/geo/*.geojson` cannot say when it was retrieved — which
is the gap that made a generator assert a retrieval that never happened.

## What the instruments found about themselves

Each of the three reported a false result before it reported a true one, and
each failure is recorded where it happened rather than smoothed away:

- `pnpm coverage` called 10 Newbury committees integrity defects for having
  nothing scheduled. "Wired and silent" is two states and only one is a defect.
- `pnpm verify:composition` reported three cards NOT REACHED that were one click
  away, and printed "still showing inherited members" over cards it had never
  opened.
- `pnpm run doctor` reported that pnpm was not on PATH, on a machine running the
  check through pnpm. And its sentinel-leak test passed with redaction disabled,
  because nothing in doctor handled a value on a printing path.

**A zero from an instrument nobody has seen fire is not a measurement.** Every
guard this session shipped carries a control that replays the defect and
requires it to still be caught.

## The adversarial challenge

Every reader-positive claim the author flagged was taken to a primary source,
and the sources disagreed with the app four times out of four. Confirmed: the
Tucson PHA really is the Mayor and Council — *plus a Resident Appointee* the
seven-person roster dropped. Contradicted: CAWCD's board. Classified from its
own page rather than from a search result: the Pima County Regional Affordable
Housing Commission is advisory — *"to make recommendations to the Board"* — and
is not a substitute for the Tucson PHA. And the supplied search summary claiming
South Tucson's housing authority extends to Vail was **rejected**: the
authority's own page says all its housing is within South Tucson's 1.2 square
miles.

## What is owed

Eleven rows, each carrying what was measured rather than a restatement of the
task: NH235–NH239 and NH244–NH245 from this session's own findings, and the
remainder of Job 1's scope, which `pnpm coverage` prints as its own unmeasurable
list on every run. The largest two: **the CAWCD board's four Pima seats are on
the 2026 ballot and the ballot corpus holds no CAWCD contest at all**, and
**58 Tucson commissions now correctly show no members**, whose real rosters the
City Clerk publishes on a tenant this repository already fetches meetings from.

# The ask-entity session — 2026-08-27

**A tester asked what was on the Vail school district agenda and was told about
Sunnyside Unified.** A different government, about thirty miles away, named
nowhere in the question, with no statement that Vail had not been found and
none that a default was in use. The reader had no way to know the answer was
about somewhere else.

The one-line proof of the mechanism, now an assertion in
`tests/ask-entity-binding.test.ts`: **with the word "Vail" deleted, the question
produced a byte-identical answer.** The name contributed nothing.

## Where the named entity was lost — four places, none of them a bug

Nothing in the pipeline ever read the name, and each layer had a defensible
reason:

- `matchTopic` matched `schools-policy` off the words "school district".
- `resolveRouting` asked `bodiesFor` for the school boards in the READER'S
  coverage, which at a Tucson zip is Sunnyside.
- `matchExactName` compares the WHOLE input against a WHOLE name **by design**
  — its own header argues that a name inside a sentence belongs to the
  destination and topic layers — so a name inside a sentence never matched.
- The Level 1 Claude classifier is asked for one topic id out of a closed enum
  and nothing else, and is told not to answer the question. The entity never
  survived that call either, and for the tester's question the classifier was
  never consulted at all: it runs only when the keyword matcher REFUSES, and
  the keyword matcher routed this one confidently.

**How the paid Claude API was being used, and what it was not doing.** It is a
topic labeller over a closed list, with a JSON-schema-constrained enum and a
second check against the same list on return. Its input is the scrubbed
question text alone; it receives no entity, no coverage, no candidate list, and
returns no entity. So the answer to "was wrong context injected before the
model" is that **no context reached the model at all, and no model output
reached retrieval** — the substitution was entirely in the deterministic layer
underneath. Retrieval was unconstrained across entities because nothing had ever
told it which entity to constrain to.

## The repair — a named government binds before the reader's ZIP

`lib/routing/named-entity.ts` resolves the government a reader named against
what this product holds and returns one of four verdicts: `NONE`, `BOUND`,
`AMBIGUOUS`, `UNRESOLVED`. It never picks a government; where the evidence does
not decide it says so, and the caller renders that instead of an answer.

Matching is on the tokens of a name that IDENTIFY rather than CLASSIFY. Strip
the civic vocabulary every district in the country shares and *Vail Unified
District* reduces to `vail`, which is why *Vail school district*, *Vail
Unified*, *Vail Unified School District* and *the Vail school board* all reach
the same government. The generic tokens are then used for exactly one thing —
breaking ties the distinctive tokens could not, using the reader's own class
phrase and the registry's own division type, which is why *the Vail school
board* resolves to the district rather than to the place called Vail. Where
that evidence does not separate them the answer is `AMBIGUOUS` and the reader
is asked.

`resolveRouting` takes the binding and constrains retrieval **by identity, never
by label** — two governments can share a name, and a label match is how the
substitution would come back through a different door. `/api/ask/agenda` binds
the same way, and a named body REPLACES the geographic scope rather than
narrowing it.

**Both directions are pinned, because pinning one is how this comes back.** A
question that names NO government still gets the reader's own district. A repair
that simply stopped answering would have passed half the file and broken the
product.

### The rung's own two failure modes, kept as controls

A matcher able to override the default is able to override it wrongly, and both
of these shipped in the first implementation:

- A body genuinely called **"Agenda Committee"** has `agenda` as its whole
  identifying vocabulary, so it captured every question containing the word —
  including the one this module was written for. A government whose entire
  identifying vocabulary is ordinary question vocabulary can no longer be bound
  at all.
- `normalizeName` turns "what's" into "what s", which put a government called
  **"s"** directly in front of "school district" in the commonest phrasing
  there is; and walking back past "my"/"on"/"is" in *"who is on my school
  board"* reached **"who"**.

## Verified on the reader path, not only in a function

`pnpm verify:ask-entity` drives the real Ask box in a real browser against a
local production build at 85706 — the tester's own context. Vail is
`UNRESOLVED` and Sunnyside is not named; a question naming nobody is `NONE` and
still gets Sunnyside. The panel now carries `data-ask-entity` on every path,
because the substitution was invisible partly because nothing on the page said
which entity had been resolved.

## Zero defects on a partial subset is not zero defects

`pnpm coverage` reported, truthfully, `INTEGRITY DEFECTS 0` beside `SURFACES NOT
MEASURABLE 16`, and said in prose on every run that the zero describes the
surfaces it measures and nothing else. The previous session's report compressed
that to "0 integrity defects". Within a day a tester found a reader-visible
defect on Ask — one of the sixteen.

`lib/ops/integrity-claim.ts` derives the verdict instead: unmeasured surfaces
decide FIRST, so a clean run with one blind spot is `NOT_ESTABLISHED` rather
than "clean with a caveat". A standing sweep runs the guard over every document
that would be committed. Two of its own false starts are recorded in it: the
word "integrity" is required in the pattern, because without it the sweep
matched *the 0,0 defect* — the NAME of a bug — and the sweep reads
`filesThatWouldBeCommitted` rather than tracked files only, because a session
record written but not yet staged is exactly the document most likely to carry
a fresh compressed claim.

**Ask is now a measured surface**, probed at all four pilots through the same
function the reader's surface calls. Measured surfaces went 20 → 24.

### The probe was vacuous first, and that is recorded too

Its first version asked *"What's on the Vail Unified District agenda?"*, which
carries no topic keyword — so nothing routed, no body was ever named, and it
scored itself green. **Disabling the repair did not make it fire.** It now
carries the words that route; a probe that fails to route is reported as a
substitution rather than counted as a pass; and a standing control re-runs the
pre-repair path on every run and requires it to still name the reader's own
district.

## CAWCD: fifteen sourced people, released from an unrelated unknown

The board that taxes every parcel in Pima County rendered **nobody**. First the
five Pima County Supervisors, by a geographic fallback; then, once that was
removed, an honest emptiness — and then it stayed empty because the board's
PARTISANSHIP had not been sourced.

Those are independent facts, and `CLAUDE.md` is explicit that collection state
never governs display. Membership is wired with its provenance; partisanship
stays `UNDETERMINED`, renders nothing, and remains open. The county split the
district's own pages give is **Maricopa 10, Pima 4, Pinal 1** — exactly the
board's statutory composition, an independent check that fifteen pages were read
correctly. That corrects a note recording only three confirmed Pima members; the
fourth is **Justin Manuel**.

**The guard that blocked it was a completion measurement frozen into a
permanent bar.** `tests/party.test.ts` asserted no roster is ever `UNDETERMINED`
— true of the twelve M62 walked, and a rule that no roster whose partisanship is
still open may ever be added. What it was really protecting is preserved and
sharpened: an open roster must be DECLARED, so it costs a line in a diff. Two
composition controls were amended the same way; both asserted CAWCD renders
NOTHING, which was true of the interim state and is not the invariant, and the
fallback control now compares by DISJOINTNESS rather than by a count that loses
its meaning once the board has its own members.

## NH244: what is established about the 2026 election, and what is blocked

Four Pima seats DO fall vacant on 2026-12-31 <!-- expected-future: the end of the CAWCD Pima directors' six-year terms, read off the district's own member pages -->, read off the district's own member
pages. Two documents were read in full and **neither settles the ballot
question**: the Secretary of State's 2026 PARTISAN filing carries no CAWCD
contest, which is expected if the office is nonpartisan and proves nothing; and
Pima County's Official Candidate List for the July 21 PRIMARY carries none
either, though it does carry nonpartisan municipal offices — and CAWCD directors
appear on the GENERAL ballot, not the primary.

The deciding source, the Secretary of State's candidate listing portal for the
November 3 general, is **`BLOCKED_CURRENTLY`**: HTTP 403 to curl, to a bare
node fetch with a browser user agent, and to a real Playwright browser. Its
`robots.txt` is 403 too, so permission is `CANNOT_TELL` and is **not** a
disallow. Bypassing bot detection is prohibited, so this needs another route.

**Nothing was written into the ballot corpus in either direction.** Not a
contest on the strength of the expiring terms, and not an absence — the corpus
is silent on CAWCD because nobody has read the deciding document, which is a
fact about us and not about the election.

## An old snapshot can no longer restore the misattribution class

`Meeting.bodyId` is what stopped 364 of 460 meetings rendering on bodies that did
not hold them. The snapshot is regenerated by a scheduled job and committed, so
an older one arrives by entirely ordinary routes — a merge, a rebase, a revert,
a cron run from an older ref — and it parses, validates, has meetings in it, and
silently attributes them to the wrong governments. A session resolved exactly
that conflict by hand yesterday. **A safety property that depends on a future
merge being judged correctly is not a safety property**, so `validateSnapshot`
now refuses it, at the boundary both the reader and the writer run through, on
the SHAPE rather than on a version number or a commit id.

## The remote gate that was red, and why it was red locally-green

`tests/doctor-secrets.test.ts` asserted doctor still reports credentials by
count — which only holds when `.env.local` exists. CI has none, so the branch
never ran and the assertion was unreachable. It now drives the sentinel through
a **constructed** `.env.local`, which is the credential-reading path no run was
ever exercising: a developer's real file has values no test knows, and CI has no
file at all. Both were blind.

## What is owed

Eight new rows carry it, including the tester's UX findings preserved as the
tester stated them and a **P2 / NEEDS SEAN** privacy row. Inspecting the product
changed what that row says: the information is not missing — `/transparency` is
470 lines across nine sections, linked from five surfaces. The defect is
DISCOVERABILITY, and on the entry screen that link is the smallest text on the
page. The row carries a seven-line draft summary, every line checked against
`lib/db/schema.ts` and the geocode route rather than against what a privacy page
usually says, plus placement notes and three open questions. **No privacy copy
is reader-visible and no live page was created.**

Ask still cannot answer *what is on a NAMED body's agenda* — the agenda rung has
no vocabulary for that shape, so the question that started this never reaches
the corpus, which holds 11 Vail meetings and 9 readable agendas. The binding
inventory is area-scoped, so a government we hold but that is far away reports
`UNRESOLVED` where `BOUND` is available. Both are rows.

`MethodRoute.effort` now captures what a scale forecast needs — what repeats and
how often, whether a machine can walk it unattended, whether the route was new
invention or reuse, and whether it was reader-integrity repair rather than
collection. As CLASSES, not durations, because a class can be recorded
truthfully and a duration reconstructed from commit timestamps cannot. **An
absent effort is a stated unknown and never a zero**, or the project would
report itself cheaper the less it had measured.

## The ask-entity session, continued — after the first close-out

Everything above was written before the branch was merged with `main` and
before four further defects were found. The later work is recorded here rather
than by editing the account above it.

### The binder was asking the reader to choose between a thing and itself

The search index mints `body:<venue key>` and labels a body with
`meeting.bodyName`; coverage carries the registry's own `bodyId`. Merging both
put one government into the inventory twice under two ids — and distinct ids
are the tie test, correctly so, because two real governments can share a name.
So *"what is Sunnyside discussing"* returned `AMBIGUOUS` between **Sunnyside
Unified District** and **Sunnyside Unified District**.

A question carrying a class phrase hid it, because the class tie-break picked
the coverage row and the answer came out right. Only a question with NO class
phrase exposed it, which is the shape a reader actually types. Dedupe now runs
ACROSS the two inventories and never WITHIN coverage — two genuinely distinct
governments sharing a name still return `AMBIGUOUS`, and both halves are pinned.

**And a second path in the same class, found by counting it rather than by a
report.** `everydayContactsFor` is keyed on the reader's ZIP alone. Suppressing
the wrong BODY while still printing the reader's own city service number under
a question about a district thirty miles away answers it wrongly in a smaller
font.

### The route answered and the client threw it away

`/api/ask/agenda` now answers a named government's own docket — the question
this session opened on, which had never reached the agenda corpus at all. The
reader still saw nothing: the client's handler read `body.topic ? body : null`,
and a body-agenda answer carries no topic. **Building a rung and shipping a rung
are two different things, and only the browser shows which one happened.**

### A calendar page attached to twenty meetings is not twenty agendas

Asking Vail its own question found the next defect. Its next sitting's "agenda
document" is 1,652 characters of Highbond portal navigation. **56 of the
corpus's 198 agenda documents share a URL with another meeting** — 27 on one New
Hampshire town calendar, 14 on another, 9 on Vail's portal root, 6 on Tucson
Unified's board page. One page cannot be the agenda of two different meetings,
so it is now its own state with its own sentence. The collection defect behind
it is NH255 and is not fixed.

### CAWCD, closed by law — and the law then reopened the ballot question

M62's own rule says partisanship is settled BY LAW FIRST, and the project had
been reading canvasses because canvass-reading was the skill it had built.
**A.R.S. § 48-3709(B)** requires CAWCD candidates on the county general ballot
*"without party designation"* — NONPARTISAN, from statute, cited, and the
declared-open list is empty again. **§ 48-3708(A)** sizes each county's
delegation by population and independently reproduces the Maricopa 10 / Pima 4 /
Pinal 1 split read off fifteen member pages.

Then **§ 16-410** reconciled the disagreement between CAWCD's own pages and
Pima's certified 2020 canvass: a county board may cancel an uncontested Title 15
or 48 election, appoint the filers *"as if elected"*, and *"canceled elections
shall not appear on any ballot"*. Both sources were telling the truth.

**It also disproved NH244's own opening claim.** An expiring term implies a
POSITION TO BE FILLED and never a BALLOT CONTEST — and the corollary bites the
other way too, because an absence now requires knowing an election was
cancelled rather than merely not finding one. Nothing was written into the
ballot corpus in either direction.

Every machine route to the 2026 answer is now closed and named on NH244: the
state portal behind bot protection at three client classes, Maricopa's and
Pima's archives behind a robots-Disallowed `/api/`, the 2020 state canvass
scanned with no local OCR binary. What remains is a public-records request,
recorded as `HUMAN_ONLY` rather than pretended to be automatable.

### No successful command may silently erase learned knowledge

`pnpm method:ingest` rebuilt the method store from the legacy manifest and wrote
it over whatever was there — 88 routes at version 27 down to 62 at version 0,
printing `routes ingested 62` and `method:check PASSED` while doing it. Its own
header promised the opposite, and a dead `void readFileSync` marked where
reading the store had been intended and never written. Worse than an ordinary
overwrite, because the method version is what convergence records are stamped
with: resetting it to 0 silently re-validates every prior `CONVERGED_AS_OF`
claim. **NH254, closed** — it now refuses and names exactly what would go.

### The scale measurement had a type and no write path

`MethodRoute.effort` was declared and nothing could write it, so it could only
ever have attached to routes learned in the future — and the ones worth
measuring are the ones already walked. `learnBatch` now carries it and FILLS an
absent value on a route it already knows, while never overwriting a recorded
one. **3 of 91 routes measured, 88 honestly unmeasured**, which is the number a
forecast has to state rather than round away.

### What the merge decided, and what decided it

`main` advanced by one job-watch commit touching only the tracker files; all
four conflicts were resolved as UNIONS, and the generated views regenerated
rather than hand-merged. The meetings snapshot was decided MECHANICALLY: main's
cron file carries 460 meetings with **zero** `bodyId`, because main does not yet
have this branch's attribution code, and run through this branch's own guard it
is REFUSED while the branch's is ACCEPTED. The invariant chose the file. That is
the guard written one commit earlier doing exactly the job it was written for.

### One portal page, three layers, and the guard that had been red for a session

Following the landing-page finding to its source turned up the same defect at
three depths, and only the first was visible from where it was found.

**The reader was being handed another government's document under their own
government's name.** Of the 56 shared documents, ONE spans two DIFFERENT
governments: `bradfordnh.gov/pages/calendar`, on 27 meetings — 14 Newbury's and
13 Bradford's. Read in full it is unmistakably Bradford's: Bradford Town Hall,
`bradfordnh.org` addresses, Bradford's own board schedules, and the word Newbury
nowhere in it. Some of those rows carry `sourceOrg: "Town of Newbury"`. That is
the class that put 364 meetings on bodies which did not hold them, surviving in
the agenda layer — and a *harder* fact than a same-body landing page, because
one page cannot be two governments' agenda under any circumstances.

**The wiring was already correct, and the data still said otherwise.** Newbury's
fifteen wiring rows carry no notice URL at all, so nothing would fetch Bradford's
calendar for them again. The document survived because the store is seeded from
the previous snapshot — which is what makes append-only semantics hold across
refreshes, and also meant a document attached under a wiring error was
re-appended by every later run, unexamined, forever. **Correcting the wiring
could not correct the data, and nothing said so.**

**And the adapter kept producing the class.** The measurement settles it: of 198
agenda documents, 56 share a URL with another meeting and **not one yields a
single agenda item**, while 67 of the 142 on their own URL — 47% — do. Two
producers, one destination: an adapter setting `agendaUrl` to a portal ROOT, and
the division-wide notice-URL fallback in `documentUrlFor`.

All three are closed. The serving path no longer attributes such a document or
returns its items; the carry-forward refuses one attached to more than one
government; and the ingest refuses to store one that BOTH yields no item AND is
already stored elsewhere — sharing alone is not enough, because two bodies
meeting jointly under one real agenda yield items and must be kept.

**Every control asserts the MEASUREMENT rather than the conclusion.** Exactly one
cross-government URL today; zero shared documents yielding items today. If either
number moves the control fails and says so, instead of passing quietly at a new
value. A guard that would accept a changed world without mentioning it is the
failure mode this whole session kept finding.

### The standing net had been red on `main` since PR #210, and the product was right

`walk:all`'s g8 check asserts no internal adapter id reaches a reader surface. It
greps the raw response, so `\bcivicplus\b` matched inside
`content.civicplus.com` and `\blegistar\b` inside a `pima.legistar.com` link —
both CITATIONS, carried because the ballot corpus's absences must cite the record
that settled them. Strip URLs and not one adapter id remains on any surface at
any zip. **The guard was reporting the transparency rules working.**

Attributed before it was touched, because the instinct on a red walk is to
assume you broke it: `git log -S` puts the citation in `9e75bea`, PR #210's
merged handoff, and `merge-base` confirms that commit predates this session's
start SHA. This branch made no commit touching the Pima ballot corpus.

Repaired by stripping URLs before scanning, with a `PLANTED` control that runs on
every walk and asserts BOTH halves — an id in reader TEXT still caught, the same
id in a source URL not — and says THE GUARD IS BLIND if the first half ever stops
firing. **369 passed, 0 regressions, 11 could not run.**

That is the third instrument this session caught reporting a fact about itself as
a fact about the world, after the Newbury coverage false positive and the doctor
PATH report. The pattern is worth naming: **the false-positive direction of a
guard is the one nobody measures**, and a guard that cries wolf gets tolerated,
worked around, and eventually switched off.

### Nine defects, and not one was visible to a passing test

The last thread of this session was an audit of the copy the session itself had
written, and it found three sentences that were not true. Recorded together
because the pattern is the finding.

**"We don't have a government recorded under 'vail'."** Written this morning as
part of the entity-binding repair, rendered at a Tucson zip, and false: the
product holds Vail Unified District with eleven meetings and nine documents.
What the binder actually did was search the reader's OWN AREA — the search index
for what is in view, plus their covered bodies — and it never looks further,
because from the client it cannot. A local lookup had produced a statement about
the whole corpus. The sentence is now scoped to what was searched: *"We haven't
matched 'vail' to a government near you."* The server had resolved Vail three
lines before returning `{topic: null}` and discarding the verdict; it now travels
on the reply the route was already making.

**"Choose one and we'll answer for it."** The ambiguous verdict listed the
candidate governments and told the reader to choose. They render as prose — no
buttons, no links, nothing clickable. A reader following that instruction finds
nothing to follow. That is a claim about the PRODUCT rather than about a
government, and false the same way. It now asks for what the binder actually
does — the class of government, read out of the reader's own words — and the
test ties the instruction to the behaviour, so copy and binder cannot drift into
promising different things.

**And the check written for exactly this passed while the defect was on screen.**
`verify:ask-entity` asserted the DOM attribute and reported 5 of 5 green. The
attribute was RIGHT: it reports the client's binding, and `UNRESOLVED` was the
correct value for a client that only searches the reader's area. The prose beside
it was wrong. Asserting on the attribute alone could never have caught it, and
the rendered TEXT is asserted now — at the routing layer too, because the browser
check needs a production build and nobody walks it on every change.

**The tally, because it is the point.** Across this session: three instruments
fired wrongly — the Newbury coverage false positive, the doctor PATH report, and
the g8 source-id guard that had been red on `main` since PR #210 while the
product was correct. Two passed wrongly — `verify:composition`, which asserted
only absences and would have gone on reporting "clean" through the entire period
CAWCD rendered nobody, and this session's own `verify:ask-entity`. And three
sentences claimed more than was true — Sunnyside standing in for Vail, "we don't
have Vail", and "choose one".

**Not one of the nine was visible to a passing test.** Every one needed somebody
to read the actual output — a rendered sentence, a canvass page, a document's
text — and ask whether it was true. A green suite is evidence that the things
somebody thought to check are holding, and it is not evidence of anything else.

# The grounded-Ask session — 2026-08-27

**Claude was in this product, and it was picking one label out of sixteen.**

The whole model surface was `lib/routing/classifier.ts`: a system prompt
containing the topic list and nothing else, answering with one topic id or
`NONE`. It had never been told what governments exist, where the reader is, or
what today's date is.

That matters because it was mis-diagnosed once. When *"What's on the Vail
school district agenda?"* returned Sunnyside, the paid model did not receive
the wrong context and choose wrongly. **It received essentially no civic
context and correctly answered the only question it was asked.** The
substitution happened downstream, in deterministic routing that asked for
boards in the reader's own coverage.

## The pipeline that replaced it

```
question
   ↓  Claude, given the entity inventory and today's date
INTERPRETATION      intent · entity mentions · tense · referent   A HYPOTHESIS
   ↓  the registry's own binder, unchanged
RESOLUTION          BOUND · AMBIGUOUS · UNRESOLVED · NONE
   ↓  deterministic, scoped to the resolved id AND the resolved tense
RETRIEVAL           only records belonging to that exact subject
   ↓
EVIDENCE PACK       records + per-record provenance + NAMED GAPS + denominators
   ↓  Claude, given the pack and nothing else
SYNTHESIS
   ↓
VALIDATION          invented URL · substituted subject · advice · tense
   ↓
READER
```

`lib/ask/` and `app/api/ask/grounded`. The synthesis rung has no corpus, no
tools and no network: its inability to look anything up is structural rather
than instructed.

**The one rule that carries the most weight** is in `lib/ask/resolve.ts`: a
government the reader NAMED that matches nothing resolves `UNRESOLVED`, never
`NONE`. `NONE` means "no government was named", which licenses the reader's own
ZIP to decide — and that is exactly how Vail became Sunnyside. Returning it
here would have restored the defect with a model's endorsement on top.

## A tensed question was answered with the wrong meeting

`bodyAgendaAnswer` read `upcoming[0] ?? past[0]` for every question. So *"What
did Vail discuss at its LAST meeting?"* was answered with the agenda of a
meeting that has not happened yet. The government was right, the attribution
was right, the source link was right, the retrieval timestamp was right.

**It was a wrong answer wearing a complete provenance record**, which is the
most expensive kind this product can produce: nothing on the surface of it
looks like a defect.

Now the tense is a retrieval instruction, and a tensed question does not fall
back to the other tense — a `LAST` question against a body with only future
sittings returns `NO_PAST_MEETING_HELD`, because answering it with the next
agenda would state that a discussion has already happened when it has not.

The selection lives in `lib/ask/select.ts` because the first version of its
guard RE-IMPLEMENTED the rule and would have passed forever whatever the routes
did. Proven by mutation: restoring the old expression fails two tests.

## What the reader actually sees, read rather than asserted

Against a real production build, with real model calls:

| question | resolved | selected | mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| What's on the Vail school district agenda? | Vail Unified District | 2026-09-09 | GROUNDED_CLAUDE | <!-- expected-future: Vail Unified District Governing Board sitting, read off the committed meetings snapshot (apptegy:vail:60703698) on 2026-08-27; it is the NEXT-meeting control this session verified -->
| What did Vail discuss at its last meeting? | Vail Unified District | 2026-08-26 | GROUNDED_CLAUDE |
| When does Vail meet next? | Vail Unified District | 2026-09-09 | GROUNDED_CLAUDE | <!-- expected-future: Vail Unified District Governing Board sitting, read off the committed meetings snapshot (apptegy:vail:60703698) on 2026-08-27; it is the NEXT-meeting control this session verified -->
| What did Katie Hobbs do in the last 12 months? | Katie Hobbs, Governor | — | GROUNDED_CLAUDE |
| What is the Nonexistent Fake District discussing? | — | — | UNRESOLVED |

Two different, correctly ordered sittings for the two tenses. The generated
prose converted `2026-09-09T02:00Z` to "September 8, 2026, 7:00 p.m. Arizona <!-- expected-future: Vail Unified District Governing Board sitting, read off the committed meetings snapshot (apptegy:vail:60703698) on 2026-08-27; it is the NEXT-meeting control this session verified -->
time" and called it a Tuesday; both were checked by hand and both are right.

The Hobbs answer is thin and honestly so: the corpus holds **who an
officeholder is** and nothing about **what they have done**. There is no store
of vetoes, executive orders or bill actions for any governor — `lib/votes/` is
congressional only. That gap is **AZ03**, and it was found by asking, not by
reading a manifest.

## Ask reaches the ballot, on the same engine

It was absent entirely: `AskBox` mounts only inside `PillCluster`, constructed
only in `map-entry.tsx`. `components/ask/ballot-ask.tsx` posts to the same
`/api/ask/grounded`. It is not a second `AskBox` — that component reads
`useShellData()` and `useUi()`, provided only inside the map shell, so mounting
it would mean standing the whole map up behind a page with no map. One widget
forced is not one engine.

**Three defects, all found by reading the rendered sentence rather than the
DOM**, and every check in place at the time passed:

1. A `NO_EVIDENCE` reply rendered **nothing** — the reader got the empty form
   back. Panel present, mode attribute correct, request and reply both fine.
   Only the sentence was missing.
2. A sitting governor came back `UNRESOLVED` on the ballot. `personEntities`
   pre-filtered divisions to the bare state id before calling
   `statewideExecutivesFor`, discarding every county, place and district id.
   Invisible on the map, where the reader's list happens to include the bare
   state. `statewideExecutivesFor` already derives the state by PREFIX, exactly
   as `senatorsFor` does — re-deriving it more strictly was a second answer to
   a question that already had one.
3. The unresolved sentence said "a government" for a **person**.

**And the instrument was false first too.** The capture script asserted
visibility BEFORE scrolling and reported the desktop panel invisible. It was
not: the ballot page is ~20,000px tall at 1280, and the pre-existing
`[data-collection-note]` measured 0×0 in exactly the same way — which is what
proved the check wrong rather than the product.

## The Vail agenda hunt, which the product itself opened

All nine of Vail's agenda documents in the snapshot are the **same
1,652-character portal landing page**, shared across nine sittings. That is why
the honest answer above says the agenda is not held — and that honest answer
was the lead.

- **Highbond is DISALLOWED.** `robots.txt` read twice, two client classes, both
  HTTP 200: 486 agent blocks, exactly one `User-agent: *` carrying
  `Disallow: /`, zero `Allow:` directives. A read RULE, not a transport
  failure — RULING 182's `CANNOT_TELL` does not apply. **NH229 proposed
  building an adapter for this host; it may not be crawled at all.**
- **A second disallowed portal, found in the link TEXT.** The district's own
  event HTML reads `href="…highbond.com/Portal/"` with the visible words
  `https://go.boarddocs.com/az/vail/Board.nsf/Public`. Different vendors,
  different tenants — and an href-harvesting crawler sees only one of them.
  BoardDocs also disallows. The **detection** is the portable part.
- **The district's own site is permitted and does not hold the agendas.**
  `Allow: /`, `Disallow: /api/`, sitemap 194 URLs. It publishes the MEETING and
  links the AGENDA out. An argued ZERO for that source — never a claim that
  Vail publishes no agenda, because it demonstrably does.
- **NovusAGENDA is the one permitted route left, and is not yet readable.**
  `robots.txt` 404, so no restriction is published. A bare viewstate POST
  returned 200 with zero rows and the date window **reset to the portal's own
  defaults** rather than the one sent — so the search never ran. **RULING 100:
  a FAILED extraction, not an empty portal.**

Four routes persisted; method version 30 → 34, 91 → 95 routes.

## Two guards that were green because they never looked

- `method:check` never validated `effort`'s three closed sets. This session
  wrote `PER_SOURCE`, `AUTOMATED` and `KNOWN_METHOD`; all four routes landed in
  the canonical store while `method:check` reported PASSED, and `tsc` caught it
  minutes later for an unrelated reason. Store repaired, whole store swept
  clean, `validateKnowledge` now checks all three — proven by planting the
  exact values back.
- `tests/db-schema.test.ts` compared column NAMES, while RULING 132 says the
  n-stores rule is proven over **value spaces**. It now compares declared enum
  values, and still refuses a single-value overlap.

## What is NOT running

`ripcord.askSignalCapture` **ships PULLED**. The Ask interaction store — one
row carrying the scrubbed question, the answer, the resolved civic subject and
the zip cohort — is built, classified in `lib/db/identity-domains.ts`, and
writes nothing. The data-privacy policy requires **honest disclosure at the
box** before a reader's typed question may enter a store whose aggregates may
reach campaigns, and that copy is **NH246's and unapproved**. Nothing
reader-visible was changed: no component or page outside `app/api` was touched.

Location is two axes, not one enum — what the place IS to the reader, and how
well it is EVIDENCED. `zipCohortOnly()` is the mechanical gate between
"readers who identified 85641 as their home ZIP" and "address-validated
residents of Vail Unified District". 85641 crosses school, fire and legislative
lines, so the second needs evidence the first is not.

# The grounded-Ask INTEGRATION session (2026-08-28)

**The engine existed and the product did not use it.**

PR #212 built a grounded Ask pipeline — interpret, canonical resolve, retrieve,
evidence pack, synthesise, validate — and shipped it beside a map Ask box that
went on calling `/api/ask/classify` and `/api/ask/agenda`. The new engine was
tested, answered the Vail question correctly through a harness, and the
product's primary Ask surface routed around it. The repository held **two
definitions of what an Ask answer is**, and which one a reader met depended on
which page they were standing on: the ballot got the grounded pipeline, the map
got the classifier. A defect fixed in one was not fixed for the reader.

That is worse than not building it, and it is the shape this session was for.

## The four blockers, and what each one actually was

**1 — The map Ask box now posts to `/api/ask/grounded`,** awaited on every
submission that is not an exact-name navigation. The search half of the unified
input is untouched: an exact name still navigates, still lands in the search log
and still writes no question row. The topic-agenda sweep is retained, because
*"is there a data centre coming?"* is a different question with a different
denominator — and it is called with `scope: "TOPIC_ONLY"`, under which the route
**refuses** to answer a named body's docket. The ownership boundary is enforced
in the server rather than promised in a component.

**2 — Identity precedence was inverted, and no binder correctness could fix
it.** `resolveInterpretation` tried `MODEL_EXPANSION` first and returned the
first `BOUND`. If a reader names Katie Hobbs and the model normalises it to
Adrian Fontes, **both bind** — the binder is not wrong about either, and the
ORDER decided it. It is now explicit reader wording, then model normalisation,
then soft page context. An expansion may NARROW an ambiguity only from inside
the set the reader's own words fit; an explicit `UNRESOLVED` stands rather than
being repaired into a different government.

**3 — `referent` was generated and read by nobody.** `interpretQuestion` had
returned it since the pipeline shipped, a comment claimed *"what has she done?"*
resolved through page context, and a repository search found the word only in
the intent layer. A comment stronger than its code reads as covered and is not.
It is consumed now, canonical-bound, refused when uncorroborated by what the
surface said is on screen, and it CLARIFIES where two people fit.

**4 — The ballot's own records were not entities.** The canonical inventory was
meeting bodies plus statewide executives. Katie Hobbs answered on the ballot by
coincidence — she is a sitting executive — and **Andy Biggs, on the same
governor line, did not exist to this product at all**, nor did any contest or
any of the fifteen propositions the same page renders. `lib/ask/ballot-inventory.ts`
builds them from the committed ballot set the page itself renders from, keyed
exactly as the page keys them.

## What proving the above found

- **Every Vail sitting printed its UTC date, one day after the meeting.** The
  corpus stores 02:00Z; Arizona is UTC-7, so that is 7:00 p.m. the previous
  evening — which is when Vail's board actually sits, on the second and fourth
  Tuesday. The record read `starting 2026-09-09T02:00:00.000Z`, an identifier on <!-- expected-future: 2026-09-09 is the UTC INSTANT the corpus stores for a meeting held on the 8th in Arizona, quoted here as the defect itself -->
  a reader surface printing a Wednesday for a Tuesday meeting.
- **The deterministic tense fallback returned `NONE` for "what's on the
  agenda"**, so the degraded path still ran `upcoming[0] ?? past[0]` — the ASK02
  defect, alive on the branch that runs whenever a model is unreachable.
- **One human arrived as two entities, twice.** A sitting officeholder who is
  also a candidate; a filing row and a general-lineup row for the same person.
  Both produced a FALSE `CLARIFY` on the product's flagship question — the
  product telling a reader their question was unclear over a distinction that
  exists only in our storage.
- **Reading the panel found two dilution defects no API assertion could.** Every
  answer carried the reader's state senator whatever was asked, including one
  about a Vail budget override whose decision-makers are Vail's own board; and
  the school-board cancellation absence was cited under a question about the
  Governor. A contact with no relationship to the subject dilutes the ones that
  have one.

## The Vail red control, through the reader's own input

Local production build, the real map Ask box, desktop and phone:

> **Vail Unified District** — The next Vail Unified District Governing Board
> meeting we have on record is Tuesday, September 8, 2026 at 7:00 PM. We can't
> tell you the items on it: the link we hold for that meeting is the district's
> agenda portal rather than the agenda itself…

with Allison Pratt (president), Callie Tippett (clerk), Jen Anderson, Ed Buster,
Chris King and Superintendent John Carruth, each read off a sourced roster row.
The same question in the past tense selects **Tuesday, August 25, 2026** — a
different, correct sitting.

## 85641 — the Novus branch is walked, and the portal is understood

The date text boxes on `MeetingsResponsive.aspx` carry `disabled`, and
`hfFromDate`/`hfToDate` are OUTPUTS of a `ddlDateRange` select rather than
inputs to the search. That is why last session's hand-built POST always got the
server's default window back: it set a value the server recomputes. A browser
finds it in one step because it refuses to click a disabled element and says so.

Driven through the real control, all eight preset windows echoed their dates
exactly, and **Custom Date Range** over 2010–2027 returns **30 meetings and 30
agenda items, newest 2017-02-28**. The 2024–2026 window returns *"No records to
display"* — a MEASURED zero, echoed window, minutes after the same selectors
read thirty rows.

So `vailschools.novusagenda.com` is a **historical archive with a measured
boundary**. NH229's pre-2017 claim moves from UNVERIFIED to VERIFIED. It does
not hold the current agenda, which stays walled behind Highbond's published
disallow — unchanged, and not circumvented. Five candidate control tenants
proved NOTHING and are recorded as proving nothing.

## CAWCD — the inference is struck

NH244 read *"terms expiring 12-31-2026, so they are on the 2026 general
ballot"*. A term ending is a fact about a seat; a ballot is a fact about a
filing. Pima County's November general still publishes two documents and no
candidate list. The July primary's four published lists were parsed and contain
zero water-conservation matches — which is **not evidence either way**, because
that list is the partisan primary and CAWCD is nonpartisan, the same shape the
school-board races have. `RECHECK_DUE`.

## The signal taxonomy, written down

`lib/signal/taxonomy.ts` classifies every live collection point across all four
stores by what the reader's ACT means, with

```
ATTENTION  !=  SENTIMENT
```

as a function rather than a convention. Opening a person's card and reacting to
them can never be counted in one number. What the product does **not** collect —
contact clicks, source opens, meeting joins — is named, because an omission
reads as coverage.

## Two more guards that were green because they never looked

`outcome.outcome` had the identical hole `effort` was repaired for: three routes
carrying `WORKED` landed in the canonical method store while `method:check`
reported PASSED. Both closed sets are validated now and both have a planted
test — and the `effort` one was proved live by disabling the validator and
watching the test fail.

The handoff's mirror guard scanned the last sixty revisions **of main**. A
session writes the mirror on its BRANCH and the branch is squash-merged, so the
version the mirror holds is committed on a ref that is not an ancestor of main
and `git rev-list HEAD` cannot see it. It asked a question whose answer is
always no. `--all`, no cap, and a refusal that NAMES the divergent lines.

## What is NOT running

`ripcord.askSignalCapture` **ships PULLED**, and it now gates something real:
`captureAskInteraction` had **no production caller** until this session, so
raising the flag would have changed nothing. `app/api/ask/grounded/route.ts`
calls it after the delivered answer is known, on every outcome including
CLARIFY and UNRESOLVED.

**The gating basis is corrected.** The previous text cited the data-privacy
policy as requiring it, quoting *"honest disclosure at the box"*. That clause is
RULING 141's and RULING 141 governs the Speak Your Mind store. The real basis is
an **operator decision** — the author has instructed that new Ask/privacy copy
does not ship and that NH246 stays P2 / NEEDS SEAN — which is precedence 1 and
needs no invented law.

**Activation is three things, not one:** the disclosure copy, the flag, and
minting the Ask continuity key. The surfaces deliberately READ that key and
never mint one while capture is off, so no identifier is placed on a device for
a switched-off capability; and `captureAskInteraction` REFUSES a row with no
continuity key rather than digesting the empty string, which would give every
reader the same hash and report one distinct reader forever. Doing two of the
three writes nothing.

# 2026-08-28 — Most of what the walkthrough reported was not the defect it looked like

The Aug 28 reader sweep. Branch `claude/aug28-class-sweep-0828`, PR #214, on
top of #213 (merged as `dcdaac41`).

**The baseline was verified before anything was touched.** #213 is merged, head
`5fe2792a` as the brief stated, all three required checks green on that exact
main SHA. The screenshots are timestamped 08:58–09:23 local and #213 merged at
10:59 local, so several of them predate it. Every control below was re-measured
against current code rather than inherited from the brief, from #213's report,
or from the images.

## The pattern, stated once because it governs the whole session

Four of the reported defects were not defects, and three more were the opposite
of what they looked like. The cheap discriminator — read the denominators, then
ask the primary source the same question the adapter asks — settled several of
them before a line of code was opened, and it is now a recorded route
(`reconcile-the-adapter-before-suspecting-it`).

## What was actually wrong, and what the class was

**DATA-1.** A CAWCD meeting's "what this meeting is about" held 9,007
characters of the CAP website's menu tree. Two naive extractors existed, months
apart, neither aware of the other: `extractHtmlText` preferred `<main>` and
fell back to THE ENTIRE DOCUMENT, and `scripts/fetch-corpus.mts` had no region
preference at all — which is why `data/corpus/statements.json` holds a
candidate "statement" opening *"Juan Ciscomani for Congress DONATE DONATE 635ms
0vh 0 Skip to Content…"*. That corpus feeds candidate positions.

Measured before designing: `www.cap-az.com` declares zero `<main>`, zero
`<nav>`, zero `<header>`, zero ARIA roles. A landmark-only repair would have
passed its own test and changed nothing for the reader who reported it. So
`lib/extract/html-content.ts` layers three mechanisms, weakest assumption last
— landmarks and roles, a named platform chrome vocabulary, and link density,
which is vendor-neutral and the reason it generalises. Both callers share it.
39,524 characters to 937.

Two guards were learned by getting it wrong first: the first draft cut the
document to ZERO because it matched the whole attribute blob (a `<link>` named
`widget-nav-menu-css`, a `title="Skip to content"`) and because it let the
vocabulary reach `<body>`, which on that page classes itself
`elementor_header_footer`. The link-density pass also cuts only the INNERMOST
qualifying block, because a menu makes every ancestor containing it measure
dense too.

**MAP-5.** Local/State/Federal filtered meetings and left every civic boundary
drawn. The overlay-to-level mapping already existed as a `tier` field on
`DISTRICT_LAYERS` — inside the MapLibre layer builder, which nothing outside
the map can import cheaply, so nothing outside the map ever asked it. It moved
to `lib/ocd/district-tiers.ts` and both consumers read it.

Putting the predicate in `deriveActiveDistrictTypes` rather than beside the map
is what makes it a class repair: `map-canvas` reads that one list for the
layers it draws, the app-owned labels on them, and `districtsAt` HIT-TESTING.
A hidden level is therefore unclickable by construction rather than by a second
predicate, and no synchronising callback exists to fall out of step.

**DATA-3.** `data/states/az/officials/body-compositions.json` was correct and was being asked
about the wrong body. `bodyFor(meeting.ocdId)` matched a coverage body by
DIVISION, and the only thing that result is ever used for is
`membersOfBody(...)` — so a division match was a membership claim derived from
shared ground. Six coverage bodies sit on `county:pima`; the match returned the
first, `#governing`, so every CAWCD sitting rendered the five Pima County
Supervisors under Representation.

Measured before changing, over the 462-meeting snapshot: every meeting carries
a `bodyId`, 14 rendered another body's members, and NOTHING loses an honest
roster by matching on identity. The division fallback was not a safety net; it
was the defect.

The unnamed control turned out stronger than expected. The Board of Adjustment
District 4 sits on the SAME `county:pima` division and publishes its own
roster, so three bodies share one division and there are three different right
answers — a direct roster, a statutory alias, and a different direct roster.

**WGH-12/13/14.** `lib/geo/session-address.ts` has stored the reader's
confirmed divisions since RULING 74 landed on 2026-08-22 and was READ BY
NOTHING; the component that writes it was its only consumer. `onResolved`
reaches the map shell as `onNarrowApplied`, which ignores its argument
entirely. And only `onPoint` moves anything, while the resolve route withholds
the point whenever the street is ambiguous.

The server was never wrong: asked at the address's own point, `/api/meetings`
returns `sldl:17`. The ZIP-area widening is what adds `place:tucson` to a point
whose own divisions are `place:tucson_ccd` and `place:vail` — and Tucson CCD is
a Census county division, a statistical shape with no government.

The repair is client-side ON PURPOSE. Sending confirmed divisions to the server
would put them in access logs, which `session-address.ts` explicitly forbids.
The client already holds both halves, so `lib/state/resolved-location.ts` is a
pure function over them.

**A regression caught in the act, and it is why only CONFIRMED retires the
mark.** Clearing it from `ELSEWHERE_IN_ZIP` too was the tempting rule — but an
unmarked row on that card reads as *this governs you*, so it would have
upgraded the City of Tucson from a hedged claim to a confident wrong one. A
weaker hedge is worth keeping until there is stronger COPY to replace it with,
not merely stronger evidence.

**ASK-14.** The office-function corpus was never missing. `office-blurbs.ts`
holds twenty-six sourced definitions including `governor`. The trace said where
it stopped: intent CIVICS correct, `resolution.state` NONE, because
`lib/ask/resolve.ts` binds ENTITY mentions and "the governor" names an OFFICE.
No binding, no subject, no retrieval, and the answer one lookup away.

**BAL-29 and MAP-4.** Measures had no ordering rule at all. A string sort would
have been the wrong repair and it is worth saying so — `"Proposition 100" <
"Proposition 20"` — so the number is parsed as a number, and a published
`ballotOrder` beats it. MAP-4 is one CSS rule met once: an element setting only
`overflow-y` has its `overflow-x` computed from `visible` to AUTO. Sixteen
rules in `globals.css` did that, two of them on surfaces in the reader's own
screenshots.

## The four things that were reported and were not defects

- **MTG-12.** The modal says 60 and groups them 1 + 48 + 8 + 3, which is
  exactly 60. Nothing is miscounted. What is open is one number — the venue
  counter — filed P3 with its denominator measured (147 served, 61 placeless,
  15 distinct venues).
- **MTG-13.** Nothing is dropped. `fetched 16 → normalized 16`, and the
  Legistar public API over 2026-08-01 to 2026-11-01 returns seven events, <!-- expected-future: 2026-11-01, the end of the query window this session asked Legistar for -->
  newest 2026-08-25, none in September, inside a 60-day forward horizon. The
  September 8 and 22 sittings are real and are published by the county as a
  RULE — *"2nd and 4th Tuesdays"* — not as events. They are NOT synthesised: a
  recurring schedule is a different record from an agenda, and cancellations
  override it. Vail is the control that makes this publishing practice rather
  than code.
- **OPS-1.** The five "stale" refresh workflows are `workflow_dispatch` only by
  RULING 124, which folded their schedules into `refresh-daily`. Their
  timestamps in the Actions list are hand dispatches, not missed runs.
- **OPS-2.** Already satisfied. `09:11 UTC` is `02:11` America/Phoenix, inside
  the requested 2–3am window. Moving it would take it out.

**BAL-27 is a third of this kind.** The incumbency join is sound — exact
candidacy → office → officeholder, INCUMBENT / CHALLENGER / UNKNOWN, fails
closed. It returned UNKNOWN because `statewide-executives.ts` holds THREE
officeholders in total, the three governors, so Arizona holds 1 of its 9
statewide elected offices. The sentence the reader saw is correct and the work
is acquisition.

## The detective result, and the doctrine it demonstrates

The corpus recorded Arizona's signed-bill and veto class as unreachable because
`apps.azleg.gov` publishes `Disallow: /`. **`www.azleg.gov` is a different host
and it is permitted** — a specific path list, `Crawl-delay: 120`, and a sitemap
it advertises.

The sitemap is STALE and `SessionLaws.asp` returns 404, which is where a walk
normally stops. But the 404 is served by the live site and is 78 KB of current
navigation: 82 links, including the two that are the fact class. Both were
walked at the published crawl-delay:

```
/governors-letters/   151 letters, 57leg/2r, 83 HB + 68 SB
                      /govlettr/57leg/2r/hb2003.pdf
/sessionlaws/         264 chapters, 1–264
                      /legtext/57Leg/2R/laws/0001.pdf
```

The page describes itself in the legislature's own words: *"…a brief
explanation as to why the Governor has vetoed or signed the bill."* Neither
`/govlettr/` nor `/legtext/` is disallowed. No search, no form, no session
token, born-digital PDFs.

**A signed or vetoed bill produces a transmittal document, and a transmittal
document has to be published somewhere the other branch can read it.** When an
executive's site is thin or the bill-status app is walled, ask the RECEIVING
body for the same act.

NOT INGESTED. 151 letters at 120 seconds apart is about five hours for one

## 2026-08-28 — finish-aug28: the engineering-team law, and MTG-13 corrected

**The session ran as nine workstreams, eight of them in parallel git worktrees
with delegated engineers, and that is now project law rather than a preference.**

**RULING 190** (meta-governance) makes safe parallel execution the DEFAULT when
two or more authorized executable workstreams are materially independent, and
makes serializing them a process defect that must name the dependency it was
avoiding. **RULING 191** (shipping-ci) is where the work returns: one
integration owner for the shared stores, a branch changes canonical INPUTS while
the owner regenerates OUTPUT once, and branch-local green is never sufficient.
Both carry `author_explicit` provenance from the session brief.

The guard is `classifyOrchestration` / `pnpm orchestration:check` over
`data/workstate/orchestration/`. **It measures the SEMANTIC, never a branch
count** — a count rewards fragmentation, and three branches rewriting one module
is worse than one branch. A dependency is PROVEN only by an owned-domain overlap
or a produces/consumes handoff; an edge backed by prose alone is reported
UNPROVEN rather than accepted or overruled. PR size, branch simplicity, conflict
avoidance, convenience, unspecified caution, P0 and the absence of subagents are
refused BY NAME. Wall-clock concurrency is not observable in this repository and
the law says so rather than pretending otherwise.

### MTG-13 — the conclusion was false, and the mechanism is proven

PR #214 recorded that Pima publishes no individual September sittings and that
the 9/8 and 9/22 meetings exist only as a recurrence rule. The measurement it
rested on reproduces; the inference was wrong.

**`webapi /events` returns only sittings whose InSite meeting-detail page is
PUBLICLY VIEWABLE.** Not an agenda-status filter and not missing data: the
unreturned event ids 404 on the item endpoint, the two routes use disjoint id
spaces, and Mesa settles it — 15 grid rows, 12 flagged `meeting_NotViewable`,
and the API returns exactly the other three. Phoenix: 8 of 8 missing. **This is
a CLASS behaviour of Legistar**, and every wired tenant was silently losing its
unpublished future meetings.

`lib/sources/legistar-insite/` drives the Calendar.aspx postback the public UI
itself uses. Identity is `(bodyId, localDate, localTime)`, never the vendor id,
because the routes do not share one. Measured on the integrated head, the three
sittings reach the reader API: `legistar-insite:pima:1381575` 09-08 13:00 Study
Session, `:1381576` 09-08 17:00, `:1381577` 09-22 17:00 — with no duplicate
against the August `/events` rows.

Three corrections to the plan came from live measurement: the range control is a
Telerik combo whose `_ClientState` must also carry the selection or the postback
is a silent 200 no-op; the `Feed.ashx` ID/GUID pair is minted per tenant AND per
range; and the grid pages at 100 while publishing its true total, so a row count
would have reported 100 and a clean 200.

**The false method is superseded, not edited.** A dated sub-branch withdraws one
word from the old conclusion: the seven events confirmed the snapshot
UNTRUNCATED, never "complete for the window". Reconciling proves nothing was
DROPPED; it never proves enough was ASKED FOR.

`pima.granicus.com` is `Disallow: /` and was not fetched. It is recorded as a
permission wall with `claimAboutContent: null`, and a test asserts that null.

### The P0 that arrived mid-session, and was not allowed to freeze the team

Intake tripwire run 33211710028 confirmed production schema drift while nine
workstreams were already integrated. **It was fanned out as a TENTH workstream
rather than serialising the session** — which is RULING 190 doing its job on the
day it was adopted: a priority starts work immediately and never freezes
independent engineers.

**Production was two migrations behind merged code**, missing `0021` and `0022`,
both Ask-interaction migrations. The precondition was verified rather than
assumed: `0021` creates `ask_interactions` and three indexes, `0022` adds five
defaulted columns to that same brand-new table, and between them there is no
DROP, TRUNCATE, DELETE, rename or type change, and no pre-existing table is
touched at all. Dry-run first, write target confirmed to be the same production
host the read-only check reads, then applied — 9 statements, both journalled.

**And the drift was wider than the report.** `walk:all` kept failing after
production was repaired, and reading the failure rather than assuming it stale
showed it named a DIFFERENT database: the DEVELOPMENT branch
(`ep-weathered-cherry`) was also two behind. Both are now IN SYNC at
`0022_adorable_hemingway`, 23 of 23.

**How it happened, measured rather than guessed.** `git log -S` over the whole
history finds ZERO commits ever adding `db:apply`, `drizzle-kit migrate` or
`apply-migrations` to `.github/` or `netlify.toml`. **Nothing in this repository
has ever applied a migration automatically.** It has always been a person at a
terminal, and nothing reminded them. The two migrations landed in squash merges
gated by `build-check`, which runs test, lint, tsc and two builds and asks
nothing about the schema.

**Detection was never the gap.** `walk:all` already carried the check and it
caught this, as a named regression. What was missing was a gate where it can
BLOCK, so the repair reuses `compareSchemaState` — the identical function behind
`db:check`, the schema route and that walk check — rather than adding a second
detector.

The gate is separate from `db:check` for a specific reason: **`db:check` fails on
any missing migration, which is right for a daily sweep and wrong for a merge
gate**, because a CONTRACT migration is supposed to be missing until its code is
live. Phase is derived from each migration's own SQL, not asserted beside it,
and a test fails when the two disagree.

**The shape that made it invisible, and it is the reason this is a class:** every
insert naming a column those migrations add failed, the route CAUGHT it, and the
page was still served. A reader saw a working site while Ask interactions were
dropped. A repair that only makes the failure louder after deployment does not
touch that — the ordering is the defect.

Restoring `actions: read` to the seven workflows that ran `diagnose` without it
then exposed a second defect underneath: the primary path SUCCEEDS and returns a
ZIP, which was being read as UTF-8 and diagnosed as mojibake. Invisible only
because the 403 meant the fallback always ran. Both fixed, and
`schema-out-of-sync` is now a named failure class.

The daily schema tripwire is untouched. It failed closed and found this.

**Reader-visible proof on the repaired head:** `walk:all` 390 checks ran, **0
FAIL, 0 silent**, 14 declared COULD NOT RUN with reasons, no named regressions.

Mesa is why the rule is the union rather than a preference: its WebAPI carries

**RULING 192 — method knowledge is typed by claim class.** The false Pima entry
was not a bad route; it was a VALID route whose existence and outcome were both
correct, carrying a false conclusion in the same paragraph at the same
authority. With one blob per route the only moves are rewrite the paragraph or
delete the route — and a deleted route is one a later session rediscovers as
new. So each assertion carries its own record and its own retraction, structured
provenance is REQUIRED for coverage claims and derived conclusions, dependence
is DECLARED BY ID rather than inferred from text, and a withdrawn assertion
whose dependents still teach is a validator failure. Applied to the canonical
store: version 55 to 55 and routes 116 to 116, because an amendment adds no
