## 2026-08-28 — the pre-control-plane cleanroom

**FOUR SUBSYSTEMS WERE RESTING A VERDICT ON AN INPUT THEY HAD NOT CHECKED, AND
NOTHING CONNECTED THEM UNTIL AN INDEPENDENT AUDIT LOOKED AT ALL FOUR IN ONE
DAY.** That is the whole session. An outside audit of PR #215 filed nine
findings; eight were confirmed, one had the right defect and the wrong root
cause, and four of the nine turned out to be the same mistake wearing four
costumes.

Nine workstreams ran in parallel — eight engineering, one integration owner —
with **zero serializations**, 36 independent pairs, and no dependency edge
declared between any of them.

### The class, and why it is a class

    ORCHESTRATION   independence was computed over the DECLARED dependency
                    graph, after every edge had been proven separately. An edge
                    that FAILED its own proof still suppressed the finding it
                    was supposed to earn.
    BALLOT          a candidate universe was complete when the rendered COUNT
                    equalled the certified COUNT.
    MEETINGS        SUPERSEDED_BY_RICHER_ROUTE was assigned as a FALLBACK — on
                    the one branch where no richer record had been observed.
    LOCATION        a division was declared not to govern a reader because a
                    DIFFERENT division at the same OCD level was confirmed, at
                    every level, including levels that do not partition.

Four unrelated modules, four authors, one shape: **a guard that reads a
declared value and reports a verdict derived from it has not checked anything —
it has restated the declaration in a stronger voice.** RULING 193 names it.
Evidence is the checked kind or it is not evidence; a denominator is not a
membership proof; unknown semantics fails closed.

### What each of the four actually cost

**The orchestration guard could be switched off by the thing it guarded
against.** `dependsOn` was walked raw before any edge was proven, so a
workstream could serialize independent executable work, keep `findings` empty
and still return `TEAM`, by writing one sentence that dodged six regexes. The
negative control is now a real prose string, asserted at test time to match none
of them.

**The candidate universe passed `4 === 4` on two different sets of people.**
Arizona's 6th congressional district: the certified canvass names Mendoza,
Ciscomani, Peters and **Gary Swing**; the filed-candidate record renders
Mendoza, Ciscomani, Peters and **Iman Bah**. Both lists have four names, the
gate passed, and three `NOT_INCUMBENT` labels were produced — one of them about
a person the certified universe does not place in that contest at all. It did
not reach the ballot page, because that page renders `lineup ? certified :
filed` and those branches are mutually exclusive. **It was accidentally safe,
not designed safe**, and one corpus change ends the accident.

**A first-party route publishing a sitting we did not produce read as
"accounted for".** Pima cannot expose it — its grid carries all fourteen — so
the branch was unreachable on the only corpus anyone had read. On the Mesa
control the union is 9, eight instances are unique to a single route, and the
one the grid never carried now carries `PUBLISHED_BUT_UNPLACED_BY_US` with the
exact missing fields named and a `PartialScopeFailure` so it reaches the run
report as owed work rather than as silence.

**And `levelKeyOf` put the City of Tucson and the Tucson CCD in the same
bucket.** Both end in a `place` segment. So confirming a reader inside the
CCD — a statistical shape with no government, as this file already said —
licensed the card to tell them the City of Tucson *does not govern you*. That
one WAS reader-facing and it shipped.

Exclusivity is now measured rather than argued, per level key:

    cd  sldl  sldu  county  state       0 double-containment    PARTITION
    place                75/113 AZ interior points in two       OVERLAPPING
                        364/477 NJ
    school_district      39/104                                 OVERLAPPING
    everything else                                             UNKNOWN — fails closed

The fallback is structural, not remembered: the contract's value type makes
`UNKNOWN_SEMANTICS` unwritable into the table, so it is reachable only by
absence. A new division type cannot inherit the strong sentence by silence.

### The denominator that had stopped describing the session

The Aug 28 plan declared **ten** workstreams. Twelve `ws/*` refs existed. The
final report said **twelve** — and twelve was the *branch count*, which is the
one substitution RULING 190 forbids. It was an honest error: the canonical
denominator no longer described the session, so the artifacts were the only
number left that was true about anything.

Reconstructed from preserved refs rather than asserted — each of
`ws/mtg13union`, `ws/methodint` and `ws/incum` is one commit off the integration
branch at `5349710`, and every non-test file in all three is byte-identical to
the merged `origin/main`:

    13 LOGICAL WORKSTREAMS on 12 EXECUTION ARTIFACTS
    10 declared when it ran · 1 appended mid-session · 3 declared post hoc

**The two numbers diverge in both directions at once**, which is exactly why
neither can stand in for the other: `governance-orchestration` ran on the
integration branch and owns no `ws/*` ref, while nine workstreams own two
artifacts each. RULING 194 makes the plan append-safe and reconciles it at
closeout; a backfill has to say that it is one, and a count that cannot be
reconstructed is recorded as a typed discrepancy rather than fixed by inventing
a mapping.

### A correction the read path never read

RULING 192 typed the method claims and gave a false conclusion a way to stop
teaching. The consumer interface was never changed, so `method:prove` and the
descent handoff kept handing workers `applicability.note` and route prose out of
the struct next door — including two Pima sentences that had been formally
withdrawn the same day. **A correction the read path does not read is not a
correction.** RULING 195: one typed projection is the consumer surface, and for
the 112 unclassified legacy entries the safe projection is exactly *the route is
known; its substantive prose is not inherited as a conclusion*.

    routes 116 · classified 4 · unclassified legacy 112
    substantive INHERITED 3 · WITHHELD 2

And `pnpm method:learn-schedule-vs-events` was still executable, still carrying
all three false sentences. Its defence was that `learnRoute` refuses a duplicate
id — a statement about *one store's current contents*, not about the writer.
Against an empty, migrated, replayed or imported store it would have written
them as current knowledge. It now refuses and names
`pnpm method:learn-legistar-insite` instead, proven by a regression that runs
the real script against a fresh store.

### Two guards that fail in opposite directions

An established migration was mutable. The gate joined production on a
*timestamp*, so a rewritten already-applied migration reported APPLIED and IN
SYNC from four separate instruments while the committed SQL was no longer what
production ran. RULING 196 makes the merge-base guard refuse modification,
deletion and rename — built on merge-base trees rather than dates, because CI
clones shallowly here and per-file `git log` returns the tip date for every file
with no error at all.

The second half was already written and dark. `apply-migrations.mts` has
recorded a sha256 of every migration's raw bytes since the Aug 28 drift
incident, and `applied-migrations.ts` selected `created_at` alone — so the only
record of what production *actually executed* was written on every apply and
read by nothing. It is read now. **The merge-base guard sees every rewrite from
now on and is blind to one that landed before it existed; the checksum sees a
disagreement whenever it happened and is blind to a migration production never
applied.** Neither covers the other's hole, and only one of them was running.

### An adapter row is not a body

The audit said Mesa's governing body existed nowhere but the tenant file. It was
wrong: the body is in `registry.json`, derived from division type. The real
defect was worse in a quieter way — Mesa was **serving ten live meetings** while
the registry said `coverageStatus: NOT_ATTEMPTED`, `agendaSourceType: NONE`, and
no source wiring named it at all. Two adapters predating `SOURCE_WIRING` keep
private tenant tables (`make: () => …`, no arguments) and reach production
without passing any registry check; the composite capability gate turns on for
the whole `LEGISTAR` type, so Pima's row let Mesa in behind it.

RULING 197 and a repo-wide guard: **126 serving tenants across three tables, 126
bound, 0 faulted.** Mesa's row now reads `LIVE / LEGISTAR /
mesa.legistar.com/Calendar.aspx`, and its `name` stays **null** — which is the
law rather than an omission, since all thirteen `DERIVED_FROM_DIVISION_TYPE`
bodies carry a null name and the oracle test asserts it. The reader-facing name
lives on the tenant, quoted from the city's own page.

### What the integrated head caught that no branch could

The build refused: `/api/meetings` traces every `.ts` file in `lib/registry/`
into its serving bundle, so the new tenant-binding guard — imported by nothing
but its own test — began shipping to production and took that route's trace
cardinality from 220 to **221**, one past the committed ceiling. The budget file
permits re-measuring a baseline when a growth is understood, and doing that
would have made the build green while leaving test-only code in the deploy. The
postbuild check already asserts `tests/ traced 0`; the rule exists, the file was
simply outside the directory the rule can see. Moved to `lib/ops/`, which traces
zero files into that route.

That is RULING 191 earning its keep: branch-local green is necessary and never
sufficient, and this was only visible where the branches met.

### The Git cleanroom

**143 remote branches** classified, and the squash-merge trap was real rather
than theoretical: **all twelve `ws/*` refs are non-ancestors of `main` and all
twelve are fully shipped.** `git branch --merged` would have been actively
misleading, and PR metadata alone would also have missed them — none of the
twelve has a PR of its own. It took integration-ancestry against `c01f4a6`, the
head PR #215 squashed.

    SAFE_DELETE 135 · KEEP_ACTIVE 6 · REVIEW_REQUIRED 1 · OWNER_BRANCH 1

The two survivors are the point. `claude/g17-aud03-measure` holds one commit of
genuinely unshipped work, so it is not deleted — **ambiguity is never resolved
toward deletion**. `sean/captures-0826` is provably content-shipped and is still
not deleted, because nothing in this repository permits a session to retire an
author's branch and a sweep does not invent permissions.

## 2026-08-28 — the fixture credential hotfix

**The deploy that failed had nothing wrong with it.** PR #216 compiled, bundled,
traced and passed every one of GitHub's required checks. Netlify then scanned
7,901 files and stopped it on one line of one test fixture:

    1 instance(s) of likely secrets
    "AIza***" detected as a likely secret
    tests/fixtures/legistar-insite-pima-clerk-schedule.html, line 667

Nobody pasted a credential. `scripts/learn-legistar-horizon.mts --record`
retrieved Pima County's Clerk of the Board schedule page and wrote the bytes to
disk, and **the page's own bootstrap JSON carries a Google Maps browser key**.
The repository became a durable mirror of a third party's live credential
because a `writeFileSync` did exactly what it was asked to do.

So the class is not carelessness. It is acquisition:

> PUBLIC WEB CAPTURE -> TEST FIXTURE MUST REMOVE CREDENTIAL-LIKE MATERIAL THAT
> IS IRRELEVANT TO THE TESTED RECORD, WHILE PRESERVING PROVENANCE AND PARSER
> SEMANTICS.

### Netlify reported one. The class scan found three, in two files.

Running the new sweep over all 1,908 committed text files before touching
anything is what made this more than a one-line fix:

    tests/fixtures/legistar-insite-pima-clerk-schedule.html
      google_api_key   fp=0475203d7298  1 occurrence
      jwt              fp=7c636da75860  5 occurrences
    tests/fixtures/schedulepage/newlondon-calendar-2026-08.html
      google_api_key   fp=c0243981d0e9  1 occurrence

The JWT is the one Netlify never mentioned. It is `window.hcmsClientToken`, a
CivicPlus HCMS bearer token issued 2026-08-28 and **live for thirty days**
<!-- expected-future: the captured token's own exp claim, 2026-09-27 -->, sitting
in the repository five times over. The New London capture is a *different*
Google key in a `maps.googleapis.com` script tag, recorded nine days earlier by
a different session through a different code path.

**And Netlify does not flag that one at all**, which is the more useful half of
the finding and was checked rather than assumed. The New London key has been on
`main` since `f1d9337` and was present in `cb0f9af8`, `a44559ea`, `dcdaac41`,
`e937958d` and `c5cd4a21` — **five deploys Netlify passed as `ready`**. Only the
Pima occurrence turns the scan red. So this is not a case of getting there before
the vendor did: for that second key, the vendor's scanner is not a net at all,
and the repository's own guard is the only thing that will ever catch it.

That also corrects the deploy history. Two merges were red, not one: `d2c5dc56`
(PR #215) introduced the Pima fixture and failed with the same exit 2, and
`52844f7f` (PR #216) inherited it. The `49b907b7` failure between them is
unrelated — "Canceled build due to no content change", a docs-only commit.

### Why this scanner is pattern-based when `secret-redaction.ts` refuses to be

`lib/ops/secret-redaction.ts` argues at length that a secret sweep must run BY
VALUE, from `.env.local`, because a shape scanner finds every git SHA and misses
every credential of another shape. **That argument is correct and this does not
contradict it.** The two modules answer different questions: that one looks for
OUR credentials, whose values we hold; this one looks for a PUBLISHER'S, whose
values were unknowable before the page was fetched. By-value is not merely worse
here — it is not a thing that can be done.

The false-positive problem is answered instead by **class-awareness in two
stages**. Stage one is a literal anchor: `AIza`, `AKIA`, three base64url JWT
segments, `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----`. Stage two asks whether the match is a
credential at all, and the two live cases in this repository are why it exists:

- The Pima token decodes to `exp`, `nbf`, `iss`, `iat`, `jti`, `client_id`,
  `scope` — RFC 7519 registered authentication claims. **A credential.**
- `https://lnks.gd/l/eyJ…` in `data/states/nj/hunt/nj-campaign-sites-*.json` decodes to
  `{bulletin_link_id, uri, bulletin_id, url}`, a GovDelivery signed link whose
  entire payload is a public justice.gov URL. **A public record identifier**,
  and redacting it would have destroyed the provenance of a source link the
  hunt genuinely found, to protect nothing.

Registered-claims-or-`Bearer`-position separates those perfectly and is grounded
in the standard rather than in a guessed vocabulary. The same discipline retired
the first draft's other false positives: `docs/deploy-key-setup.md` names a PEM
header in a sentence and `tests/deploy-key-ssh.test.ts` stubs one with a body of
sixty-four `x`s. Requiring a real base64 body with genuine alphabet diversity
excludes both **on the evidence**, which is the only exclusion that stays correct
when somebody edits those files.

**Nothing is set aside silently.** An unconfirmed match is still returned,
counted, printed, and carries the reason it was not treated as a credential.

### What the repair actually changed

Seven substrings across two files, and nothing else:

    pima      6 replaced (885×5 + 39)   1,164,526B -> 1,160,242B
    newlondon 1 replaced (39)              56,565B ->    56,556B

The sanitized text was reconstructed against the original and matched
byte-for-byte outside the seven redacted spans. Line counts identical, `<script>`
counts identical, **every `<table>` block byte-identical** — which is the only
part `parseClerkSchedule` reads. MTG-13 is unmoved: fourteen future Pima
sittings, fourteen Clerk rows, horizon through 2026-12-15 <!-- expected-future: the Pima Board's published schedule horizon -->
and route composition unchanged, 26/26 union tests and 16/16 schedule-page tests
green.

### The line-ending trap, caught by the drift check it caused

The New London capture is stored LF, because `.gitattributes` marks
`tests/fixtures/** -text` — recorded evidence is never converted. A working copy
carrying CRLF was hashed partway through the repair, so the `rawSha256` first
written described 57,697 bytes that were not the captured bytes, and the commit
would have rewritten 1,132 line endings of evidence to redact one value. Caught
by reading `git diff --stat` and disbelieving a 2,264-line diff for a one-value
change. The tree was reset and the repair redone from a clean checkout; the
committed diff is now **4 insertions, 4 deletions**. A hash-agreement test now
makes that class fail loudly instead of silently.

I could not attribute what wrote the CRLF copy — it predates every write this
session made, and the scan was verified read-only. That is stated rather than
guessed at.

### Where the gate now sits

`tests/fixture-credentials.test.ts` runs in `pnpm test`, which is CI's required
`gates` job, so **the class fails in GitHub minutes after a fixture is written
rather than at the Netlify deploy**. Seventeen tests, and the positive controls
are **synthesized at runtime from fragments** — committing a Google-shaped key to
prove the guard catches Google-shaped keys would trip the very scanner this
exists to satisfy.

The negative controls are the half that keeps it usable: CivicPlus container
GUIDs, Legistar meeting and body ids, pagination parameters, dates, times,
analytics ids, a git SHA, a sha256 and an ordinary UUID are all asserted NOT to
be flagged. A redactor that eats the public record is worse than the leak.

`writeCapturedFixture` in `lib/ops/fixture-captures.ts` is now the one door a
captured page enters through, and a structural guard refuses any bare
`writeFileSync` into `tests/fixtures/`. It caught the sanitizer's own write the
first time it ran, so the sweep goes through the same door rather than being
exempted from it. Three recorders were rewired.

Provenance lives in two halves that cannot drift apart: the DECLARED half
(`SANITIZED_CAPTURES` — source URL, capture date, what captured it, what it
proves) is hand-authored, and the DERIVED half (`data/fixtures/sanitization.json`
— raw and sanitized SHA-256, classes, counts, fingerprints) is generated. **The
raw bytes are not committed anywhere.** `rawSha256` is the entire memory of them,
which is the point: this repository stops being a mirror of a live third-party
credential, and a hash is reproducible by anyone who re-captures the page.

    3 credentials removed · 2 classes · 2 files · 7 substrings
    1,908 text files scanned · 1,179 skipped (binary), counted and named
    2 shape-matched and excluded on the evidence, with reasons printed
    17 new tests · 1 workstream · SINGLE_WORKSTREAM, dependency-proven

    Netlify deploy 6a92603cebd657000809464d · READY · secret scan passed

Netlify's scanner found one instance of one class in one file. It was right, and
it was reading the shallowest layer of the problem: the credential it named was
not the live one, the file it named was not the only file, the second file it
never flagged at all across five green deploys, and the write that put them all
there was still in the tree.

## 2026-08-28 — the overnight control-plane build

**The repository already had most of the architecture's semantics and almost
none of its runtime.** That sentence is the whole finding of Stage 0, and it
changed what this session built. The hardened game plan asks for a work graph, a
method registry, atomic route dispositions, permission/transport separation,
coverage denominators and a political-neutrality invariant — and every one of
those already exists here, tested, and governed by a numbered ruling. What did
not exist was the layer underneath them: a durable unit of route work that
outlives the worker walking it, a lease, an attempt record, an evidence vault, a
shared host budget, a cost ledger.

So the control plane was built to **supply that layer and call the existing
semantics unchanged**, not to restate them. The clearest case is the disposition
vocabulary. The plan names five dispositions; `lib/workstate/types.ts` already
carries eleven under RULING 184, and the eleven are strictly better because
three of them — `BLOCKED_CURRENTLY`, `REQUIRES_NEW_ADAPTER`,
`RECORDS_REQUEST_PENDING` — are open states wearing a finished face. The plan's
five are now recorded as a *reading* of the governed eleven, in
`DESIGN_DOC_DISPOSITION_READING`, so a later session cannot reconcile the two by
minting a second enum. `FAILED` deliberately gets no mapping at all: it is three
different facts (a transport failure, which belongs to the Attempt and is not a
disposition; a capability gap; a wall), and collapsing them into one word is how
a wall became an emptiness.

### The three prerequisites

**`claude/g17-aud03-measure` is retired.** The prior audit finding was re-proven
before deletion rather than trusted: one measurement-only commit, one file
changed, 463 commits behind `main`, and all eight of its `dynamic()` boundaries
already present in current `main` at lines 98–126 of `components/map/map-entry.tsx`
under the same names, with `docs/aud-03-prereg.md` and both AUD-03 decision
commits on `main` too. Its SHA was recorded before the ref was removed. `main`
is now the only remote branch.

**NH272 is still yours, and the value was never the blocker.** The read-only
production URL exists in the local authorized environment and is proven — role
`readonly` on `neondb`, credential-ledger row 33. What this session declined to
do is copy a production credential into GitHub Actions, which widens what a
compromised workflow can reach. The consequence is smaller than it looks,
because the reading itself was taken **locally, against production, this
session, and it is green**: 23 of 23 committed migrations applied, head
`0022_adorable_hemingway`, all 23 content checksums matching the SQL committed
here, one `SELECT`, nothing applied. The mechanism is proven. What the secret
buys is CI taking that same reading unattended.

**NH273 shipped, and it does not roll anything back.** The author's decision was
explicit: a red post-deploy integrity reading marks production DEGRADED in
durable machine-readable state and mechanically blocks the next
production-changing release, rather than reverting the deploy — because the
database may already have advanced, and rolling code back underneath an advanced
schema manufactures a second incompatibility on top of the first.

The design turned on one measurement. The plan recommends a `deployment_status`
workflow; `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/deployments` returns **0**. Netlify creates
no GitHub Deployment for this repository, so that event has never fired here and
a workflow listening for it would never run — a gate that never executes reports
nothing and reads as covered. The freeze therefore went into the **existing
`gates` job**, which is the required context and the repository's existing
shipping truth. A tenth workflow would have been a second verdict and would have
broken two count assertions; the workflow count and the action-pin count are
untouched.

Five states, and the two that earn their keep are the two that are not green.
`CREDENTIAL_MISSING` exists so an absent secret cannot print like a pass.
`STALE_HEALTHY` exists so a green answer about an earlier commit cannot be read
as an answer about this one — the record carries the SHA it was taken against,
and without that field a green record is green forever. Both live controls were
run against a planted DEGRADED record: a production-changing change is refused
with exit 1 and a named remedy, and a non-shipping change is permitted **while
the state still reads DEGRADED**, because paperwork is not a production release
and merging it thaws nothing.

### What the control plane refuses

One deterministic evaluator answers whether an obligation may end. It is pure,
total, and refuses by default: an input it was not given is a reason to refuse,
never a reason to proceed. Thirteen named refusal codes, and the first is the
one the whole architecture exists for.

**The inherited route floor is computed, never typed.** Preflight asks two
authorities and unions the answers — the method store through `projectMethodFor`
(RULING 195 makes the typed projection the only inheritance interface) and the
source adapter's own declared first-party surfaces. Neither is a superset of the
other. A floor built from one of them is how fourteen Pima sittings became
three.

To make that mechanical, `horizon.ts` gained a value-level `FIRST_PARTY_ROUTES`
and now derives `FirstPartyRoute` from it. It had been a bare type union, which
cannot be enumerated at runtime, so any consumer wanting all of them had to
retype the list — and a retyped floor is the forgot-the-API defect wearing a
different hat.

### Pima, attached in shadow

MTG-13 is attached as a real obligation reading the committed method store off
disk, bound to the registered body id, and changing no reader truth: the InSite
adapter and `tests/legistar-insite-union.test.ts` remain the acceptance
authority for the fourteen.

The proof walks seven of the eight first-party routes and quietly omits
`/EventDates`. Completion is refused, and **the refusal names that route** rather
than reporting a count. The omitted route is precisely the one measured at zero
future sittings, which is exactly why forgetting it felt safe.

Two more that would be easy to get backwards. The Granicus `Disallow: /` keeps
the obligation **open** rather than counting as walked-and-empty — we are not
allowed to look, and that says nothing whatever about what is there. And a
denominator that was never established refuses the close, because completeness
measured against our own output is not completeness.

### The evidence plane

There is no evidence vault today, and Stage 0 found why that was easy to miss:
acquired bytes are hashed, extracted, accounted, attributed and rung-stamped —
and then discarded. The only durable copies of publisher bytes in this project
are 73 sanitized test fixtures, an external content-addressed asset store, and
untracked local scratch.

Three artifact tiers, and the middle one is the point. A public page can itself
emit a live third-party credential — PR #216 was stopped by exactly that — and
that does not make the public record disposable, nor the credential safe to
propagate. The exact bytes become a `RESTRICTED_RAW` artifact; parsers and
ordinary workers get a provenance-linked `SANITIZED_DERIVED` one carrying both
hashes, the sanitizer version and the redaction counts, and never a value. The
shipped PR #217 scanner does the work; no second sanitizer exists.

`ParserInput` is branded with a module-private symbol, and its sole constructor
verifies the bytes hash to the artifact's recorded `contentHash`. The brand
alone would still have allowed a worker to fetch a page live and attach the
metadata; the hash check closes that.

One correction to the plan, found by building it: `writeCapturedFixture` is the
single acquisition boundary for fixtures, but it sanitizes **and discards the
raw** in one step, returning only the sanitized hash. It cannot be reused as-is
for a vault that needs both hashes and the exact raw bytes.

### Capabilities, budgets, cost

Least privilege where the **absences** are the content. A parser holds no
network capability at all and cannot read restricted raw. Production write,
external communication and records requests are granted to no role. The
adversarial auditor *does* get public network read, because an auditor that
cannot independently acquire first-party evidence is a stamp rather than an
auditor. `authorize()` denies by default, and neutrality is an invariant with no
disable path.

Budgets are shared, and the test proves the thing that actually matters: twelve
workers against one publisher with `maxConcurrent: 3` get three grants, while
twelve **private** ledgers would grant twelve. Per-worker politeness multiplies;
that is the whole reason the budget cannot live in the worker.

Cost never touches truth. An unmeasured value is `null`, never zero — a rollup
of `[null, 5]` reports total 5, measured 1, unmeasured 1 — and `withinBudget`
separates *within* from *enforceable*, so an unmeasured spend neither halts the
system nor silently counts as free. A source sweep asserts that no exported
function in the cost module is shaped like a claim about correctness, with a
positive control proving the detector fires.

### The guards caught four things, and every one was real

The full suite found six failures on this session's own code, and not one of
them wanted the guard loosened.

RULING 103 caught the git reader written out identically in both NH273 scripts —
two places for the null handling to drift, in a mechanism that turns entirely on
the difference between *the answer is no* and *there was no answer*. RULING 159
caught a bare changed-path count with no denominator floor; flooring it improved
the output, which now reports how many changed paths are production-bearing
rather than printing a naked total. RULING 107 caught a clock-stamped freshness
date with no declaration that the stamp sits in the reading path — it does, and
now it says so, along with what would make the declaration false. RULING 14
caught a backslash repo path in a test where the backslashes were the *subject*
of the test, and was still right: such a literal can only ever match on Windows.

The remaining two were one mistake twice: NH273 was marked resolved and left in
the working store, so the section census counted 356 against a store of 357.

### Campaign finance follows the filing authority

The discovery question is not *which API covers this level*. It is **who is the
filing authority for this contest, committee and period** — and the authority's
level need not match the office's. Arizona answers it by statute: A.R.S. § 16-928,
read from the state's own site on 2026-08-26 and quoted here rather than
paraphrased, sends statewide and legislative filings to the Secretary of State,
county **and school-district** and community-college and special-taxing-district
filings to the county officer in charge of elections, and city and town filings
to the clerk. A school-board contest routing to a county officer is the test
that proves the levels come apart.

`resolveFilingAuthority` has no fall-through to the state. An unwalked county
returns OPEN with a null authority and names the route, because guessing the
custodian is the same error as guessing the filing. The federal authority's
`statutoryBasis` is **null on purpose**: this repository has read Arizona's
statute and can quote it, and has never read whichever federal provision names
the FEC as filing officer. A plausible citation in the one field whose job is
being checkable would be a fabrication, so it carries a named open question.

RULING 126 constrains the whole domain and the constraint is honoured — no
Drizzle table, no migration, types and committed-JSON semantics only — and the
firewall's own wall-1 sweep is re-run over the new modules and still finds
nothing.

Two obligations, both **open**. The federal one is AZ-06, reading per-candidate
coverage out of the committed FEC snapshot rather than transcribing it, so a
refresh cannot leave a stale number behind; Schedule E is `BLOCKED_CURRENTLY`
behind counsel review and the reporting calendar is `UNWALKED`. The local one is
the Vail Unified School District budget override, resolved by the statute to the
Pima County officer in charge of elections, with all seven routes open —
including the `seethemoney` SPA wall, the live-browser rung 6 still recorded as
NOT YET WALKED, and the EasyVote tenant-list question unanswered since
2026-08-26.

An independent expenditure is not money received. The types are structurally
distinct, and that guard was verified **by breaking it**: adding a
receiving-committee field produces three compile errors, one of them inside the
library.

### What this session did not do

It did not add the `WTP_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL_READONLY` secret, and NH272 is
still open for that reason alone.

It did not promote anything to reader truth. Every attachment is SHADOW; the
InSite adapter and its union test remain the acceptance authority for Pima's
fourteen sittings, and no reader surface changed.

It did not choose a durable workflow provider or an object-storage provider.
Both are owner decisions with billing attached, both are isolated behind
interfaces, and the in-memory evidence store says in its own type that it is not
production durability.

It did not build the Control Center. The plan puts it at Stage H and the plan is
right: a dashboard built before canonical state exists produces numbers with no
denominators.

The aircraft is not finished. What exists is a foundation with its invariants
proven against real obligations — which is what the plan asks Stage B to mean.

## 2026-08-29 — the durable shadow runtime

The overnight build of 2026-08-28 produced a semantic foundation and said, in
its own closing lines, that it had not chosen a durable provider and had not
proven durability. This session took the seven dimensions that brief named and
moved each one as far as the repository could actually carry it, in six parallel
workstreams over disjoint files, integrated on one branch, verified once at the
combined head.

### Four declarations that were not mechanisms

The foundation declared more than it enforced, and every one of the four was
found by reading the code against its own comments rather than by a test going
red.

`CompletionContract.acceptableDispositions` declared which dispositions could
close an obligation and **the evaluator never read it**. Three call sites wrote
it; all three wrote `null`, so no outcome anywhere could have differed. It is
enforced now, narrowed to the inherited floor, with the two wider readings
written down beside it and the reason each was rejected — governing every
RouteTask would have punished a scout for honestly disposing an endpoint it
discovered mid-walk, and matching on route id alone would let a floor route
walked against a second host escape the filter entirely.

A disposition could carry **another Attempt's id and cite another Attempt's
artifact**. That is a conclusion about a government resting on bytes the
execution making the claim never retrieved, with the hash chain pointing at a
retrieval that did not happen. Three bindings close it, all mechanical.

`reclaim()` proved almost nothing: any Attempt could reclaim any task, including
a still-open one and a COMPLETED one. And `DENIED_BY_POLICY` — a capability our
own policy engine refused — was swept into the same generic path as a crash,
which is how a fact about us becomes indistinguishable from a fact about a
publisher. It now parks the route in `POLICY_DENIED`: outstanding, never
disposed, recording what must change before a retry.

**A snooze could close an obligation.** `openEscalations(item, now)` hid
escalations snoozed past `now`, and the completion evaluator used it as its
input, so moving a date forward removed a blocking escalation from the
completion test. Queue visibility and blocking truth are now separate questions,
and the blocking one is evaluated **with no clock at all** — there is no moment
the evaluation can be moved to that clears the refusal. An escalation created
without an opinion blocks, because a field nobody set must never be the reason an
obligation closed.

### Evidence that proves its own identity

The vault verified byte *length* and stopped. So bytes that were not the
artifact's were accepted and stored at a key derived from a hash they did not
have — the store manufacturing a false citation at the moment of writing. The
positive control for the fix is deliberately byte-length-identical to the real
page, because otherwise the old guard is what fires and the new one is untested.

The header also claimed a global deduplication the key shape does not provide:
five of its seven segments are scope, so identical bytes for two work items land
on two keys. The claim is corrected to what the code guarantees — immutability
and content identity **within the scoped namespace** — and the header now states
what the duplication buys, which is that per-source takedown stays a prefix rule
rather than a scan and `RESTRICTED_SHORT` expiry stays a storage lifecycle rule
rather than a cron job that eventually stops running.

The in-memory double was a bare `Map.set`. Every test that "proved" immutability
was proving it about a double that did not have the property. A double may be
stricter than production; it may never be looser.

And a real defect surfaced that no amount of reading would have found: Windows
`MoveFileExW` refuses a rename onto a destination another writer is renaming onto
at the same instant, so two workers racing one legitimate retrieval became an
error. The atomic write now takes a mandatory `acceptExisting` predicate — a lost
race succeeds only when what is now present hashes identically, and a rebuilt
manifest passes `null`, because two racing rebuilds genuinely disagree and must
surface.

### Workers can now die

`WorkItem → RouteTask → Attempt` is persisted behind provider-neutral
repositories with an in-memory double and a durable filesystem implementation.
The substrate is the one the repository already governs — committed files, the
same class as `data/workstate/` and `data/method/knowledge.json` — because
control-plane work state is not reader-facing, and adding a Postgres migration
for it would have tripped the schema gate and frozen a release for a reason with
nothing to do with truth.

Two design corrections were forced by building it. Write-then-rename is atomic
for a **replacement**, which is exactly no help when the point is not to replace:
two writers at revision N both rename and both win. Taking revision N+1 is now
winning a race to exclusively create one filename, so compare-and-set is
arbitrated by a single filesystem operation. And `put` compares against revision
1 rather than the latest, because comparing against current state would refuse a
legitimate re-registration of a task that has since been claimed — a guard that
fires on correct behaviour is a guard on its way to being deleted.

The acceptance test is the whole claim in one sequence: worker A claims, writes a
partial artifact, disappears without a terminal disposition; time passes the
lease; **a fresh repository instance over the same root** sees the durable
history; worker B reclaims and completes; exactly one disposition exists; A's
partial is still there and still attributed to A.

What is honestly stated rather than claimed: one process cannot tear another's
write mid-syscall, so no test here demonstrates a torn read. The defences are
structural and the file says so.

### Method learning that cannot overwrite itself or vanish

`runLearnBatch` was an unconditional canonical writer — read, apply, write — so
an invalid route reached `data/method/knowledge.json` and was found later by
`pnpm method:check`. There is one governed write path now; it validates the
prospective store with the canonical validators before writing, and refuses on
any issue. It carries an optimistic-concurrency precondition, so a writer holding
version N cannot overwrite a store at N+1. Six existing ungoverned writers are
named in a ratchet that may shrink and never grow.

A route discovered mid-walk is a candidate: `PROPOSED → VALIDATED → ADMITTED |
REJECTED`, and **a rejection is persisted with its reason**, because a candidate
that simply disappears teaches the next session nothing and will be proposed
again. The `PriorConclusion` corpus the reopening engine had always lacked now
exists, so a conclusion earned under version N is mechanically reopened by a
genuinely new route admitted under N+1.

### The freshness rule, and the premise that turned out to be false

`STALE_HEALTHY` did not freeze anything, so a green reading about an earlier
commit blessed every later one forever. The obvious fix is wrong and was
rejected: a freeze keyed on the **candidate** commit can never be satisfied,
because a post-deploy reading of a commit cannot exist before that commit
deploys. An unsatisfiable gate is the strongest argument anyone will ever have
for the skip flag this repository refuses to have.

So the subject of the question is **what production actually serves**, and the
instrument needs no credential: `/api/build` returns the deployed commit, and
`next.config.ts` puts it there. Served commit equals the reading within a stated
maximum age, the release proceeds; anything else — production moved, the reading
expired, production could not be asked at all — freezes, and cannot be asked is
never a pass.

Building the observer surfaced a defect that would have been silent: adding a
`fetch` to the freeze gate made `process.exit()` abort on Windows and **destroy
the exit code**, so frozen and permitted runs both exited 127. Two verdicts, one
indistinguishable result.

And the session's own premise about production was wrong. NH281 records that
nothing had deployed since `71325247` and that the build log needs the author's
Netlify login. Measured twice, and independently confirmed: production serves
`de61ff5d`, fifteen commits on, and `main`'s tip is docs-only, so production is
CURRENT rather than behind. A fresh post-deploy reading against the served commit
HELD — 23 of 23 migrations. The row is noted, not closed: it cleared on its own
rather than being answered, and closing a Needs Sean row is the author's.

### The proving run

`pnpm shadow:run` carries one real obligation — Pima County's future Board
sittings, the MTG-13 case — through the hardened runtime, over the publisher
bytes already recorded under `tests/fixtures/`, and writes a replayable record.

The floor is **28 routes, not 8**. With no field narrowing the projection offers
122, including PDF extraction and portrait matching; narrowed to the two fields
this obligation owes it is the 8 concrete adapter surfaces plus 20 meeting-bearing
techniques the store holds on UNKNOWN portability. Twenty of those are undisposed,
so **the obligation does not complete — 41 refusals** — and that is the runtime
working rather than failing. A control plane that closed on eight of twenty-eight
known routes would be the exact defect the architecture exists to prevent.

Modelling the crash taught something. The first version had worker A and worker B
retrieve identical bytes, so identical content hashes, so identical artifact ids
— and the append-only log refused the second record for re-pointing A's artifact
at B's Attempt. It was right to. A crashed capture is a **prefix** of what the
server was sending, not the whole of it, and modelling it as a truncated body is
both what actually happens and what makes the attribution honest.

Every measured reader surface is byte-identical before and after, and that
verdict is derived from the two digest maps rather than asserted — with a surface
that could not be hashed counted as moved, because "we could not check it" must
never render as "it did not move".

### What this session did not do

It did not choose a durable workflow driver, so the primitives never run
unattended and the dimension stays PARTIAL. It did not activate `RESTRICTED_RAW`
durability, because the only reachable substrates are a public store and a plain
folder, and weakening the tier to fit them would put a live credential somewhere
readable. It did not promote anything to reader truth. It did not fill the filing
regime registry beyond the four regimes this repository can quote from a primary
source — New Hampshire is left out because the explainer cites a statute quote
that is not in the file it names, and New Jersey because its own notes record the
statute as unread and two hosts refused.

And it did not narrow either campaign-finance completion contract, having found
the reason not to: the Arizona floor is not uniform. Two of its routes can land
on an honest `NOT_APPLICABLE`, so a list right about two routes would refuse
completion on a truthful record.

## 2026-08-29 — the exact-body-identity and answerability session

**The application retrieved the wrong government, and every check downstream
was green.**

A reader asked *"What's on the Pima County Board of Supervisors agenda?"* and
production answered:

> CAP University: Deeper Dive on How Water is Accounted for in the Lower Basin

describing it as the Board's next meeting, and adding that there was no other
upcoming Board meeting in the records. There were fourteen.

The trace read `GROUNDED_CLAUDE`. That is the part worth sitting with. The model
had stayed inside its evidence pack and paraphrased it faithfully. The
substitution guard passed, because the pack's subject was "Pima" and the answer
said "Pima". The temporal guard passed, because the meeting really was in the
future. Every name in the sentence was the right name. **The evidence pack
itself was wrong, and a wrong pack produces fluent, well-sourced, confident
falsehood with every instrument reading green.**

### The mechanism was one line, and the identity to fix it already existed

`lib/ask/inventory.ts` built the Ask body inventory from `meeting.ocdId` — the
DIVISION — and stamped each row `nameClass: "body"`. So the pipeline called a
division a body, and `app/api/ask/grounded` selected meetings with
`m.ocdId === subject.id`. The Pima County division carries 42 meetings: 30 are
the Board's and **12 belong to the Central Arizona Water Conservation
District**, a separate multi-county government recorded against the same
geography. `selectSitting` then correctly chose the next sitting out of the
wrong set.

`lib/sources/types.ts` had said what the fix was since 2026-08-27, in capitals:
`Meeting.bodyId` is *WHICH BODY IS MEETING — the registry id, not the
geography*. `lib/meetings/snapshot.ts` already refuses to serve a snapshot whose
meetings lack it — that guard exists because attributing meetings by geography
once put 364 of 460 meetings on bodies that did not hold them. The identity was
present in the corpus, asserted at the write boundary, and thrown away one layer
above.

**It was never a Pima peculiarity.** Nine divisions in the committed snapshot
carry more than one body, and `az/place:tucson` carries fifteen — Mayor &
Council alongside the Planning Commission, the Design Review Board, the
Commission on Disability Issues and eleven more. Every one of them was an
available wrong answer to a question about the Tucson city council.

### What changed

- **`lib/registry/body-identity.ts` (new).** A synchronous, cached view of the
  canonical registry, keyed on body id. All 78 body ids in the committed
  snapshot resolve in it; 64 carry a sourced name. It reads the registry, it
  never mints identity, and it never writes.
- **The Ask inventory emits one entity per canonical `bodyId`.** The division
  travels alongside as `ocdId` — context for the class tie-break — and cannot be
  mistaken for the identity, because it is a different field with a different
  value. Names come from the registry rather than `meeting.bodyName`, which is
  the meeting's own title carried onto the body: the corpus records Vail's board
  as *"Governing Board Meeting"* and the water district under four names
  including *"CAP University"*.
- **`BindableEntity.level` is TYPED.** `nameClass: "body"` was carrying this and
  could not, because it answers a different question — what KIND of thing a
  reader can name. Retrieval refuses an entity that is not `level: "BODY"`
  rather than falling back to its division; a fallback that fires "only when the
  level is missing" is the same defect with a longer fuse.
- **Evidence records carry `bodyId`, and the validator checks it.** An id
  comparison, not NLP. The name-only check demonstrably could not catch this.
- **`contactsForBody` split from `contactsForDivision`.** *Who represents this
  area* and *who sits on this body* are different questions; they were one
  function because Ask could only name divisions. The division's
  representatives are now offered only for the body that IS that division's
  government, so a Tucson advisory board cannot be given the Mayor and Council
  as its membership — the failure `tests/body-composition.test.ts` already bans
  one layer down, arriving through a different door.

### A quarter of the corpus's bodies could not be named at all

Nineteen of seventy-eight carry a registry name that identifies nothing on its
own: seven called exactly *"Planning Board"*, four *"Budget Committee"*, three
*"Select Board"*, plus *"Zoning Board"*, *"Road Committee"* and Tucson's
*"Planning Commission"*. The binder declines such names on purpose — that
discipline is what stopped a question about Vail binding to a Tucson body called
"Agenda Committee" — so the reader who typed *"the Warner Planning Board"* got
AMBIGUOUS. Honest, and useless, about exactly the hyperlocal sitting this
product exists to surface.

They are now qualified with the division's own sourced label, and **only** where
the body's own name carries no identifying token. Nothing is invented: two
sourced facts are stated together. Qualifying unconditionally would be a
regression, and the corpus holds the case that proves it — the Central Arizona
Water Conservation District is recorded against Pima and is not Pima's, so
prefixing it would demand a word from a reader who would never say it and make
the body unreachable. That control is a test.

### The same class, one surface over: the govern verb

`jurisdictionClaim` took no body id and returned *"Governs: Tucson"* for
anything with a division, while `governVerbMayAttach` in
`lib/registry/body-class-labels.ts` — written to enforce RULING 118 — was never
consulted. Measured over the registry: **248 of 1,998 bodies were making a
governing claim about a division that is not theirs.** They now read "Listed
under". The map's representation note said *"We know this body governs here
because its division exists"*, which is an inference from a division's
existence; both surfaces now read one claim, so neither can carry the verb the
other refuses.

NH270's own code half turned out to have shipped already in PR #215. That was
verified against the extracted pre-fix module rather than assumed, and a
regression test was left behind so it stays fixed.

### Answerability is now measured, and the measurement is unflattering

`lib/answerability/` makes DISCOVERED → ACQUIRED → EXTRACTED → NORMALIZED →
CANONICALLY_LINKED → QUERY_RETRIEVABLE → READER_VERIFIED seven separate stages
with real denominators, and no upstream success may flow into a downstream
numerator. For the Pima County Board of Supervisors:

| question | reach |
| --- | --- |
| what was on the agenda | ACQUIRED 16 of 30, QUERY_RETRIEVABLE 16 |
| what did they decide | **ACQUIRED 0 of 30** |
| how did each member vote | **ACQUIRED 0 of 30** |

The DISCOVERED denominator reads `DENOMINATOR_NOT_ESTABLISHED`: no source
exposes how many sittings the Board actually held, so the 30 may be most of them
or a fraction, and the report says so rather than implying completeness.

`record-class.ts` makes the agenda/outcome distinction structural. An agenda
proves what was NOTICED; items are continued, withdrawn, tabled and pulled from
consent, and none of that changes the agenda. It is now mechanically impossible
to hand an agenda to a question about a decision.

### A speculative method hypothesis is not a known route

`appliesTo` answered one question with a boolean plus a `speculative` side-flag,
so every consumer reading `.applies` got "yes" for a route proven here and a
route merely offered here. Two self-proof bugs were closed: a route that NAMED a
narrowing dimension and left it EMPTY was granted proven status — which is
precisely how a school-district technique becomes a proven county route — and
`STATE_FAMILY` computed a union where it needed an intersection, so a
jurisdiction listing itself in its own family proved every state-family route
applied to it.

The floor is now REQUIRED versus EXPLORATORY, and **the split is not an
excuse**: exploratory routes are still materialized, scheduled, executed and
still refuse the close as `ROUTE_TASK_STILL_OUTSTANDING`. What it forbids is a
hypothesis being refused against as though it were a known API. Before the
split, the Pima run emitted 20 refusals each asserting an applicability nobody
had proven, burying the one real one.

### The permission gap a document URL hides

The detective found that `legistar.granicus.com` serves `Disallow: /` — and it
is the host every Pima and Mesa agenda PDF URL in the snapshot actually resolves
to. Its sibling `pima.granicus.com` was recorded DISALLOWED on 2026-08-28; this
one had never been checked. Two more Highbond tenants are in the same position.
Re-verified independently before recording. The portable rule, and the reason
the gap existed:

> THE HOST IN A DOCUMENT URL IS FREQUENTLY NOT THE HOST OF THE PORTAL THAT
> LISTED IT. Permission must be checked per document host, never per portal.

All three are now recorded DISALLOWED — NOT WALKED. The repo holds 29 documents
with extracted text from them, collected before the permission was read.
**Whether that text stays is not a session's decision**; it is NH286, a Needs
Sean row, and it is stated there with the counter-argument rather than as an
obvious purge.

### What this session did NOT establish

- **READER_VERIFIED is 0 everywhere.** The ladder's last rung is not claimed for
  a single record.
- **`QUERY_RETRIEVABLE` is a structural proxy** — addressable by body and tense,
  with items — not an executed call into the Ask retrieval path.
- **No method route is REQUIRED for Pima today.** The predicate was repaired;
  114 of 116 routes still state zero typed constraints, and populating them is a
  governed store change (NH287).
- **No Pima County campaign-finance dollar figure is held.** The filing index
  was acquired — 138 filers, 680 filings — and the document endpoint answered
  401. Zero money, and a test asserts no amount field exists in the local record.

### Addendum — the instrument that accused eight real people

Landed after the main PR, on `claude/false-absence-verifier`.

Resolving NH216 meant re-reading Vail Unified's board page, and the row's premise
turned out to be false: the five names it said were **absent from the district's
own page** are all on it, at HTTP 200, in bytes a plain node fetch receives.
`pnpm verify:extraction` had produced a false absence — and a false `DISAGREED`
is an accusation against a government's own publication, made by a check that
had not looked where the answer was.

It had two independent causes, and the second was found only because the fix
made the report **not reproducible**.

1. **The page it never read.** `renderedText()` strips `<script>` — right for
   CODE, wrong for the DATA that IS the page on a client-rendered site. Vail
   runs Apptegy; the roster ships in the hydration payload; the reader kept the
   chrome and threw away the page. Now `embeddedDataText()` reads the JSON
   string literals out of `<script>` blocks — string VALUES only, never raw
   script source, because trading a false ABSENT for a false PRESENT is the
   worse bargain.
2. **The wall it read as an emptiness.** The curl rung was `curl -sL` and
   `return stdout.length > 0`. curl prints the body of a refusal exactly as it
   prints the body of a page, so `www.newbury.nh.gov` answering with a hard 403
   became 5,591 bytes of denial HTML, became "the page", and three Newbury
   Selectboard members were accused of not being on their own town's site. The
   rung now asks for the status code; a refusal is `COULD_NOT_READ` and is
   counted in its own column.

```
Vail     BEFORE  0 agreed · 1 partial · 5 DISAGREED
         AFTER   0 agreed · 5 in payload · 0 partial · 1 DISAGREED   (Carruth, correctly — he is staff)
Newbury  BEFORE  0 agreed · 3 DISAGREED
         AFTER   3 agreed · 0 DISAGREED, stable across consecutive runs

Names DISAGREED, corpus-wide        22 -> 13
Rosters where every name agreed     24 of 39 -> 27 of 41
```

Nine false accusations against government pages removed, and the report is
reproducible for the first time.

**A third weakness was found and deliberately NOT fixed.** `judgeName` tests
membership with `String.includes`, so the two-letter given name "Ed" is found
inside "published", "used", "provided" — on any page in the corpus. A short
given name therefore cannot reach `DISAGREED` whatever the page says, which
inflates `PARTIAL`, and is why Ed Buster escaped the false accusation his four
colleagues did not. It is named in the regression test rather than buried:
widening the matcher to word boundaries moves counts in a published report and
deserves its own measured change, not a drive-by.

The lesson generalises past this instrument. **Both faults are the checking
layer committing the exact error the constitution forbids the collection layer
from committing** — asserting an absence it had not established, and rendering a
wall as an emptiness. An instrument is not exempt from the law it enforces, and
RULING 193 already said so.

## 2026-08-29 — the acquisition doctrine, and our gaps stated as ours

**The session was asked to make a doctrine permanent so the author never has to
state it again, and the doctrine turned out to already be violated in two places
nobody was looking.**

### What the author ruled, and how it landed

Five rulings, adopted from an explicit current author directive. The directive's
own instruction was followed literally — *preserve one coherent current
statement of each rule; amend where semantics overlap; add new rulings only for
genuinely new semantic content* — so this is five rulings rather than the five
laws the directive names, and one of those laws got no number at all.

- **RULING 205** — if a public civic record exists, get it. The obligation is a
  durable object that outlives every route disposition taken against it and
  outlives the worker. Three closes and no fourth: acquired and
  reader-answerable, affirmative source-backed evidence about the RECORD ITSELF,
  or human/offline access required with the obligation still open. Extends
  RULING 170 and RULING 184, which say what a session may not CONCLUDE; this
  says what SURVIVES.
- **RULING 206** — the vendor is not the record.
  `GOVERNMENT → RECORD → REPRESENTATION(S) → ROUTE(S)`. Extends RULING 182:
  that one keeps permission and transport apart, this keeps representation and
  record apart, which is the same collapse one level up.
- **RULING 207** — one successful route never collapses the source universe; an
  adapter is a route portfolio, not one fetch function. Extends RULING 178.
- **RULING 208** — an access escalation is a parallel lane. **Amends RULING
  146**, which keeps the SESSION going past a Needs Sean row; this extends that
  to the OBLIGATION the row is about, and gives the row a required content
  shape.
- **RULING 209** — a permission rule binds the next fetch, never possession of
  what was already published. This is the general form of the author's NH286
  decision, and it is what closed that row under RULING 79.

The directive's LAW E was almost entirely RULING 177 and RULING 178 already. Its
one new clause — that a spent portfolio obliges DISCOVERY of the next method
rather than closing the obligation — lives inside 205 and 207, where it has
operative force, rather than in a fifth number that would have restated two
existing rules.

**The doctrine is now in three places and a guard says so.**
`docs/governance/ledger.jsonl` is canonical, `CLAUDE.md` carries it between
the transparency mandate and the cross-cutting rules, and `AGENTS.md` carries
the agent-facing mirror as its first project-owned content.

### The guard exists because nothing else could catch this

`governance:compile` deliberately does NOT re-derive constitutional records
from the live `CLAUDE.md`. That mirror behaviour was a real defect: it silently
deleted the transparency mandate and the ladder the moment the constitution was
shortened, and it was removed for exactly that reason. **The consequence nobody
had written down is that a session can delete law from `CLAUDE.md` and every
governance gate stays green**, because deletion is not duplication and the
ledger is untouched. `AGENTS.md` is worse — it is rewritten by a tool this
repository does not own.

So `tests/acquisition-doctrine.test.ts` reads all three and asserts the
doctrine survives in each, plus a DRIFT check in both directions: a mantra the
mirror states that current law does not is an agent obeying a rule nobody
adopted, and a mantra law states that the mirror omits is an agent never meeting
it. **All five red controls were proved by mutation** — deleting the CLAUDE.md
section, softening one clause, deleting the AGENTS.md block, pushing content
ahead of it, and dropping a mantra from law while the mirror kept it — each
reverted with the tree verified byte-clean afterwards.

### The defect the doctrine was written about, found twice

**In the reader path.** `app/api/ask/grounded/route.ts` reached
`whose: "THEIRS"` and *"No agenda has been published for that … meeting yet"*
from `forMeeting.length === 0`. That condition measures ONE thing and it is a
thing about us: this product holds zero agenda documents keyed to that meeting.
The corpus carries **34 bodies with a future sitting and no document at all**,
and every one of them was being reported to readers as a government that had not
published. `tests/ask-body-agenda.test.ts` regex-pinned the sentence as
correct, so the suite was protecting it.

Live on production before the fix, asked *"What is on the Pima County Board of
Supervisors agenda?"* — the body id resolved correctly, and the answer said
*"The county has not published an agenda for that meeting yet."* After:
`publication: UNKNOWN`, `acquisition: NOT_ACQUIRED`,
`obligationOpen: true`, and *"We have not yet acquired the agenda for that …
meeting. We are still looking for it."*

**In the instrument that measures it.** `lib/answerability/stages.ts` had one
block code in its `BLOCKS_ABOUT_THEM` group — `NO_DOCUMENT_URL_PUBLISHED` —
and assigned it from `!obligation.agendaUrl`, an empty column in our own row.
On the day it was found it was asserting that Pima County published no document
for **14 of 30** Board sittings, on no evidence from Pima County at all. The
doc comment explaining that the two must never print as one sentence was the
thing licensing the collapse. It is now `NO_DOCUMENT_URL_HELD` and OURS, and
the THEM group is reachable only from a first-party publisher observation of
that exact sitting, inside a freshness window.

**Neither of these is a new class.** Both are the render-default rule the
constitution already carried, in code that was written to enforce it.

### The outcome records existed and the reader could not reach them

The Legistar Web API had already been proven to carry Pima's actions and
per-person votes. The harvest lived in a probe script, and reader outcome
answerability was **0 of 30 held sittings**. This session moved it into a
durable store with exact canonical linkage and wired it into the evidence pack.

Measured live and reproduced twice: **20 sittings, 1,360 agenda items, 525 with
a recorded action, 2,083 per-person vote rows, 417 items with a roll call, 108
acted items with no roll call.** Vote values are carried verbatim — **Aye 2,011,
Nay 41, Recused 8, Not Present 23** — and a yes/no mapping would have destroyed
72 real positions. **18 of 20 sittings now answer outcome questions.**

Through the real handler: *"What did the Board decide at its last meeting?"*
returns 58 `MEETING_ACTION` and 285 `MEETING_MEMBER_VOTE` records; *"How did
they vote last time?"* returns 285 member votes and **zero action summaries**,
because the class filter refuses them — the tally lives on the action record and
only there, and one join between them is the difference between a real record
and five fabricated positions.

**And the class-level result is the one that matters.** The same route on Mesa
returns **59 sittings, 874 agenda items, ZERO recorded actions and ZERO vote
rows** — the outcome fields are on the wire and null on every row. *"Legistar is
supported"* is not a safe sentence from one tenant.

### The doctrine changed behaviour the day it was adopted

Pima County's campaign-finance filing BODIES answer HTTP 401 on the one route
anybody knew, and a prior session had recorded that honestly as a wall on a
route rather than a statement about the filing — and stopped. Under RULING 205
that leaves the obligation open, so it was worked: all **59 API routes were
enumerated out of the publisher's own app bundle**, and
`/advancedsearch/contributions/{customerId}` answered **500** rather than 401,
with a stack trace naming `GetSubdomain(url)` throwing on a null URI. The API
has its own anonymous website-user path and needed only the tenant subdomain,
which it reads from the `Origin` header. With it set: **HTTP 200 at 1,090,303
bytes — 900 contribution rows and 584 distribution rows**, no credential, no
login, no bypass. *Citizens of Vail for Education* received \$5,000 from Concord
General Contracting on 2025-12-17.

900 was proved not to be a cap by partitioning against the server (2025:
502 = 502, 2026: 368 = 368), because a truncated result cannot partition
consistently.

**A conflict was correctly refused rather than resolved.** The session brief
asked for federal Schedule B and Schedule E records. `docs/sources.md` records
those as gated behind the PB10/D23 election-law counsel review, and CLAUDE.md's
precedence puts a session brief BELOW current policy. No Schedule B or E was
walked and no live FEC call was made. The brief also assumed a missing API key;
a real `FEC_API_KEY` exists and is wired, and DEMO_KEY would have been worse
than the key rather than a substitute for it.

### Six routes learned, and none of them is about Arizona

Method version **55 → 61**, 116 routes → 122. Streamline's sitemap is a dated
meeting inventory and its market is special districts, the thinnest layer in
every state worked so far. BoardBook returns an entire archive on one
unpaginated page — and its Minutes path is a client-rendered shell that strips
to 757 bytes, so a parser pointed there reports every meeting as having empty
minutes. The apex and `www` forms of a host are different origins: one
answered 403 to four clients while the other served a 267-meeting archive. Two
districts had migrated to `.gov` while an authoritative county GIS layer still
published the dead host. A county has more than one filing officer. And a
refused endpoint is answered by reading the publisher's own bundle.

### What was found and deliberately not fixed

**NH288.** A body's Ask subject name falls back to the bare division label for
**14 of 78** bodies, so a reader is answered about *"that Pima meeting"*. The
obvious fix is to use the corpus's own body name — and the corpus name is
frequently a MEETING TITLE (`GOVERNING BOARD AGENDA SPECIAL MEETING`,
`RTSD Board Meeting`), so substituting naively makes the reader text worse.
The correct fix is registry data, not a heuristic over publisher-supplied
titles.

**NH289.** `release:freeze` was failing before this session started, and
correctly: production serves the post-deploy observer's own data-only commit,
which the workflow argues cannot happen because `data/ops/` is non-shipping.
The classification is right; what is not established is that the cancel TAKES
EFFECT, because every failure path in `scripts/netlify-ignore.mjs` builds by
design. Diagnosing it properly needs the Netlify build log.

**NH287** was re-measured rather than repaired: **114 of 116** method routes
state zero typed applicability dimensions, all of them carry
`portability: UNKNOWN`, and outcome jurisdiction is a free-form string mixing
`az`, `nh`, `pilot-counties` and `az-pima-85641` in one field. The repair
is a change to the method store, which another lane owned while it ran — two
lanes rewriting one canonical store is refused by the parallel-execution rule
rather than permitted by it.


## 2026-08-30 — the served commit was not the application, and the reader finally heard how the Board voted

The handoff opened on a repository that could not ship: PR #227 — four `docs/`
files — stood frozen under a required check whose own scope rule says a
docs-only change is never a production release. This session measured both
defects under that freeze, repaired them as classes, unstranded the PR through
an honest green, and then spent the rest of the day where the product actually
lives: the reader's vote question, the method store's applicability claims, and
the first local campaign-finance records to reach an evidence pack.

### NH290 — the gate that had never read a pull request's diff

Build Check run #463, measured: `release-freeze-gate.mts` diffed against
`origin/main`, a ref a depth-1 `actions/checkout` does not have, so the
changed-path list read COULD NOT BE READ, `classifyDeploy(null)` said
cannot-tell, cannot-tell is production-changing, and the freeze reached the
exact paperwork it is scoped never to reach. The repair is the shape
`db-shipping-gate.mts` proved first: the base comes from the platform —
`pull_request.base.sha` out of the event payload, fetched by sha with a
deepening fetch; a push uses its own added/modified/removed lists. WE MEASURED
NON-SHIPPING and WE COULD NOT MEASURE THE DIFF remain different answers, and
the second still freezes. PR #228's own gates run then printed `changed paths
3 of 5 are production-bearing (git diff fb0c623..HEAD (the pull request's
base, from the event payload))` on the real shallow checkout, and #227 merged
as `45670b06` with no bypass and no skip flag.

### NH289 — a moved commit is not a moved application

The freeze #227 fell into was a second defect. Netlify's own deploy list shows
the class five times running (`589676ae`, `097fca30`, `2be8e854`, `ed0c253d`,
`5169fa32`): the post-deploy observer's `data/ops/`-only commit lands about
sixty seconds after an app-bearing merge, the last-successful-deploy pointer
lags publish by roughly fifteen seconds, so the observer commit rides the
accumulated diff and BUILDS — production then reports the observer's sha while
serving the measured release's application byte for byte, `sameCommit` says
moved, and every next production-changing release freezes. The deploy filter
was correct at every step; cancelling inside the window could strand a
shipping change if the parent build failed, so the wasted build stays the safe
direction and the identity was repaired instead.

The served commit and the application-bearing release are now two identities.
`PRODUCTION_MOVED` consults a PROOF the gate measures from git evidence on
every run: the served commit must descend from the recorded release, and every
path in the range must be non-shipping under `classifyDeploy` — the deploy
filter's own predicate, so a schema file or one app file anywhere in the range
destroys equivalence by construction. `NOT_EQUIVALENT` freezes as a real move;
`CANNOT_TELL` freezes as an unproven one; there is no flag, no trusted sha,
and no allowlist. DEGRADED stays a hard freeze the proof cannot reach, the age
bound still applies after equivalence, and the log states both identities.
The mechanism met its founding scenario live the same afternoon: production
reported `fbcac4ac` (the observer's child of `7fea24af`) and the gate printed
`release permitted … a PROVEN non-shipping descendant … application-bearing
release: 7fea24af`. During the merge train it also refused correctly — a range
carrying #229's real shipping changes froze with `NOT_EQUIVALENT — 4 of 11
path(s) … production-bearing` until the observer recorded the new reading,
which is the freeze doing its job, not failing at it.

### NH288 — the roster held the Board's name for seventeen days

`registry.json` deliberately carries `name: null` on derived bodies, so 14 of
78 bodies rendered as bare division labels, `pack.subject.name` was `"Pima"`,
and the validator's require-a-subject-token rule reduced to *does the prose
contain "pima"* — correct anaphora ("The Board voted 5-0…") was
REJECTED_FELL_BACK and the flagship vote question returned records with no
prose. The fix is in the reading layer: `lib/ask/body-identity.ts` falls back
registry-own-name → `BODY_ROSTERS.bodyName` — sourced, cited, and sitting
unread since 2026-08-13 — → division label. 12 of 14 bodies now serve sourced
names; Mesa and Morris Hills Regional stay at their labels, classified *source
exists, not ingested* (NH293), because nothing is invented. The validator was
redesigned rather than weakened: `subject-not-substituted` now rejects prose
that names a DIFFERENT known body's full name, over the body universe the
route already holds, with the id-level `record-belongs-to-resolved-body` wall
untouched — proven false-first, including the old rule's blind spot (foreign
naming beside the word "Pima" used to pass).

Reader-verified on production with synthetic before/after probes: *"How did
the Pima County Board of Supervisors vote last time?"* moved from
REJECTED_FELL_BACK to GROUNDED_CLAUDE prose naming the August 25 sitting and
its items, subject resolved to the `#governing` body id, denominators
`285 held / 60 in pack` stated. Two warts recorded rather than hidden:
`titleCaseName` prints "Board Of Supervisors" (NH292), and a body-less "how
did the board vote" is UNRESOLVED rather than misbound.

### Which sixty votes (PR #232)

The 60-row vote bound was honest about its size and silent about its choice —
a first-N in store order, so which votes a reader heard about was an accident
of ingestion sequence. Selection is now explainable: an item the question
itself names first (two or more distinct five-plus-character tokens — a false
match would spend the budget answering an unasked question), divided roll
calls next (a 3-2 is what member rows exist for; a unanimous roll is carried
by its action record), store order as the stable tail — and WHOLE ITEMS ONLY,
because three members of a five-member roll reads as an absence for the other
two. The items split is reported beside the rows split
(`rollCallItemsHeldForThatMeeting` / `rollCallItemsInPack`), and the seeded
control asserts whole items exactly against the store's own per-item counts.

### NH287 — the method store stops leaking school districts into counties

Measured at v61: 122 routes, 120 stating zero typed dimensions. Population is
now mechanical or absent (`pnpm method:type-applicability`): states from
YIELDED outcomes only, platforms and publishers from recorded hosts, additive,
idempotent, portability untouched — 58 of 122 typed, and governmentTypes
honestly zero because no OCD id exists anywhere in the store's evidence. The
matcher leak is closed as demote-not-exclude: a mismatch on an evidence
dimension turns PROVEN into OFFERED_UNPROVEN — an AZ school-district technique
is an experiment for an AZ county, never a false REQUIRED floor, and never
withheld. Routes and reasoning disciplines are now a typed `kind`, with 80
routes honestly UNCLASSIFIED rather than guessed. (PR #231.)

### The first local campaign-finance records to reach a reader's evidence pack

The grounded route had no finance evidence provider, so it told readers we
held nothing while `data/campaign-finance/` carried 900 contribution and 584
distribution rows from the Pima EasyVote acquisition. `lib/ask/local-finance.ts`
now links BODY ← OFFICE ← COMMITTEE strictly through the county register's own
`officeName` plus a hand-audited crosswalk committed with its written basis —
never a name match: the PAC "Citizens of Vail for Education" links to no body,
and register-less "ANDRES FOR SUPERVISOR" never reaches the Board of
