## 2026-08-30 · Session A.1 — contract instrumentation repair

Session A shipped four instruments and this session made them real. Every
finding it repairs is the same class: **a contract that appears enforced and is
not.** Nothing here is new architecture; the Session A contracts and schemas
stand and are now mechanically checkable.

### The reader evaluator asks the question now (WI1)

`scripts/reader-suite.mts` evaluated `document.body.innerText` and tested
`includes(expectation.text)`. It never typed a question, never pressed the
button, never waited for an answer, and never looked at one — so a page
carrying the expected words anywhere went green while Ask could have returned a
fallback, the wrong government, or nothing.

It now seeds the ZIP, submits the question through the product's own Ask
interaction (`[data-ask-box]`, Enter, exactly as a reader does), waits for the
answer to SETTLE rather than for a fixed sleep, and evaluates **the answer**.
GREEN requires all of: a rendered answer, a grounded mode from an allowlist
(so a mode added tomorrow is not silently green), a visible source record, and
the expected proposition asserted. The expectation is typed — ENTITY, VALUE,
LIST or VERIFIED_ABSENCE — replacing `DOM_TEXT_INCLUDES`; values are normalised
so `$297.86` and `297.86` agree and `29786` does not. Every RED carries a
failure class from the twelve. New: `lib/health/ask-evaluation.ts`,
`scripts/ask-harness.mts`. `components/ask/ask-box.tsx` gained
`data-ask-sources` (a publisher count, the convention `data-ask-contacts`
already uses) so "is it sourced" is machine-readable.

### The universe check runs, against a denominator that can disagree (WI2)

`checkInstanceUniverse` was never called, and the only body-layer denominator
vocabulary was `PROJECT_REGISTRY` — the store the instances are GENERATED from.
Registry checking registry is a mirror: it agrees over any universe, including
one missing every body the registry omitted. NH232 is the proof that matters —
a regeneration once silently dropped 731 promoted bodies and every green stayed
green.

The denominator now comes from the canonical INPUTS the registry is built from
(`curated-bodies.ts` + `promoted-bodies.json`), under a new source
`PROJECT_BODY_ENUMERATION_EVIDENCE`. RULING 9 is unchanged — it governs source
CLASS, and this is the project's own enumeration evidence.
`assertDenominatorIsIndependent` refuses a `PROJECT_REGISTRY` denominator for
the body layer by name. The check runs BEFORE any scoring, a level with no
independent denominator is NOT_EVALUABLE with the missing evidence named, and a
disagreement produces a typed diagnostic WorkItem. New:
`lib/health/body-denominator.ts`.

### RED creates work, and only a qualifying GREEN closes it (WI3)

`diagnosticWorkItemFor` existed and nothing called it; had it been called it
wrote its completion condition into `why` as prose and attached
`DEFAULT_CONTRACT`, so an item created because a reader could not learn a fact
could be closed by a validator that never asked the question again.

`CompletionContract` gains `instrumentEvidence` — instrument, instance id,
creation SHA, required verdict — and `evaluateCompletion` gains two refusals:
`INSTRUMENT_VERDICT_NOT_EARNED` and `INSTRUMENT_EVIDENCE_UNANCHORED`. Items are
persisted to the durable file-store control plane, deduplicated by derived id,
and closed only by a canonical run on a tree that CONTAINS the failure commit.
A VISUAL_SUITE green cannot close a READER_SUITE obligation. New:
`lib/health/diagnostics.ts`.

### Controls run blind through the real path; visual checks exist (WI4)

The control runner scored a simulated array; with real controls it reported
`score: null`. Each fact is now asked as a reader-shaped question through the
SAME `openAskAt`/`askAndRead` path — blindness holds by construction, because
the transport is a text box with nowhere for control identity to travel. First
real reading: **recall 0.500 (1 of 2), false-absence 0.000, false-presence no
denominator** (no CONFIRMED known_absence row exists to give it one).

`VisualAcceptanceCheck` had a load-bearing evidence-kind rule enforced against
a population of zero. `pnpm visual:suite` loads checks, refuses any whose
evidence cannot certify its property, captures the bound viewport, and
evaluates DECODED PIXELS — clipping from the variance ratio at the boundary,
visibility from luminance variance — never the selector that found the box.
New: `lib/health/control-observation.ts`, `lib/health/visual-evaluation.ts`,
`scripts/visual-suite.mts`.

### pilot:health reads only canonical runs (WI5)

It passed literals: `activeInstances: 0, evaluatedGreen: 0, target: null`, with
a comment promising these came from a run record. Nothing read one. With a
nonempty corpus the red branch tests `evaluatedGreen < activeInstances` — `0 <
0`, false — so READER returned **GREEN over zero evaluated instances**.

It now reads the newest reader and control run records: counts, target, run id,
tested SHA, finish time. `readerContract` refuses a nonempty corpus with zero
active instances unless an independently established zero proves it legitimate,
and a run that is stale or tested on a tree HEAD does not contain reads
NOT_READY. New: `lib/health/latest-runs.ts`.

### Status definition split from status result (WI6)

`lib/ops/status-ledger.ts` held both halves in one hand-typed array —
`lastResult: "suite green in the workstream run that generated this ledger"`,
`proofClass`, `asOf`, `sha` mostly "—" — and `--check` proved the Markdown
matched that array. It proved a document equals its own source. The committed
ledger said HEAD `e62c420` while the release was `096e0469`, every gate green.

Split into `lib/ops/capability-registry.ts` (CURATED: all 23 capabilities
carried across verbatim, `provenBy` a typed union naming instrument and
identity, and **no field in which a result could be typed**) and
`lib/ops/status-result.ts` (DERIVED from gate / walk / reader / observer run
records). `proofClass` is now read off the record rather than declared.
`pnpm gates` writes `data/ops/gate-runs/`; `pnpm walk:all` writes
`data/health/walk-runs/` with a per-check outcome. `--check` is red when the
ledger's recorded HEAD is not the generating HEAD. The old data module is
deleted.

### The standing walk: 1463.4s → 321.2s, same 390 checks (WI7)

**Measured first, and the measurement found the cause.** Per-check wall time is
now recorded on every run with the twenty slowest printed and a canonical
summary written to `data/health/walk-runs/`, so the session reads a record
instead of watching the walk.

The baseline said 61 of 390 checks accounted for **93.3%** of the wall time. The
cause was `appSettled`: it waited for `.coverage-notice` AND
`.state-focus-layer`, and **no element carrying any class containing "coverage"

ran to its full 20s ceiling on every call, and the return value was discarded.
A blind twenty-second pause wearing an outcome wait's name — R49's own defect,
inside R49's own helper. Measured at all four pilot zips: TIMED OUT at 20s,
every time.

Replaced with signals verified to arrive only after the work they stand for
(state focus layer 311–1860ms, who-governs card 451–1955ms, meetings count
196–1737ms) plus NH121's settle. The old 20s ceiling is unchanged — it is a
wall, not a target. **The result is now returned and printed**, so this cannot
silently become a sleep again.

`390 ran + 14 declared COULD NOT RUN, baseline 379, 0 silent` on both runs —
identical coverage. Regressions went 3 → 1; the two that stopped failing had
been read at a fixed 20s that never confirmed readiness and are now read after a
settle that does. This session did not fix them and does not claim to. The one

### Owner intake (WI8)

`defects.md` is retired as an owner surface and kept as a machine-maintained

## 2026-08-30 · Session B — the instruments repaired, the owner's pass swept, and a freshness clock that says when it does not know

Three workstreams. Workstream 1 hardened the instruments so they could not
certify the wrong thing. Workstream 2 swept `feedback/8.30.26/`. Workstream 3
built and shadow-ran the autonomous freshness loop. The orchestration record is
`data/workstate/orchestration/2026-08-30-session-b-instruments-sweep-freshness.json`
and `orchestration:check` reads it TEAM: three workstreams, one independent
pair, every serialization backed by a real handoff.

### Workstream 1 — eight semantic holes, and a ninth found by using the repair

An independent audit of A.1 named eight places where an instrument could
certify the wrong thing. Each was a check that LOOKED enforced — the field
existed, the branch ran, the verdict printed — and was missing a clause.

**WI1.1.** ENTITY expectations checked `answer.subjectId`; VALUE and LIST did
not. A grounded, sourced answer carrying the expected value ABOUT A DIFFERENT
GOVERNMENT went GREEN. Every clause of the reader contract held except the one
that makes the answer true. `expectedSubjectId` now binds both, from the
owner's explicit id or from the instance's own `subjectBodyId`.

**WI1.2.** `LIST.exhaustive` appeared in exactly one place — the failure
message. An answer naming every real member plus an invented sixth passed a
check whose whole purpose was to forbid the sixth. Extras are read off record
lines; prose is deliberately NOT mined for names, and an exhaustive list with
nothing enumerable is NOT_EVALUABLE rather than green.

**WI1.3.** `VERIFIED_ABSENCE.period` existed since A.1 and nothing read it, so
a true sentence about 2025 certified a claim about 2026. The answer's absence
scope must now cover the expectation's, with ranges expanded.

**WI1.4.** An absence fact's `expected_truth` IS the absence, so an answer
correctly stating it matched every salient term and landed in `FACT_STATED` —
which `scoreControls` reads as a FALSE PRESENCE. The product would have told
the truth and the instrument would have recorded it as a lie about a
government. Invisible only because both loaded controls are `known_present`; an
instrument that inverts a verdict on a population of zero still inverts it.

**WI1.5.** The observer adapter expected `sha` and `verdict: HEALTHY|OK`; the
post-deploy observer writes `deployedSha`, `mainSha` and `observed: "HELD"`.
Every field read came back undefined and the row went STALE — and the A.1
report explained the STALE by saying the record "names no SHA". That was a
claim about the DATA that was really a fact about the READER. The record names
`f762a72e` in two fields. The row now renders PROVEN with that SHA.

**WI1.6.** A coverage defect opened a diagnostic under a synthetic id
`coverage:<zip>:<layer>` that `greenInstanceIds` could never contain, so a
repaired denominator left it open forever. `coverageInstanceId` now derives the
id for both directions.

**WI1.7.** `visual_prominence` and `image_level` ran the VISIBILITY test, so
"this element stands out" was certified by "something is painted here" — true
of every element the product renders. Prominence now measures the element
against its surrounding band. Real evaluators for overlap, position, spacing
and reading order; anything without a capable evaluator is NOT_EVALUABLE, never
a red blaming the product for a gap in the harness.

**WI1.8.** Every passing canonical result was labelled
`INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED` — the class `pnpm gates` earns on an unmerged
branch, which RULING 216 excludes by name. The class is now derived from
recorded provenance: a clean tree, already contained by the integration branch
when the run started, and a runner that is not a local session. **16 of 17
ledger entries reclassified to `SESSION_MEASURED`.** The one that did not is
the post-deploy observer row, which is genuinely scheduled — and it moved the
other way, from STALE to PROVEN, because WI1.5 taught the adapter to read it.

**WI1.9.** The universe check is independent of the GENERATED `registry.json`
and NOT of the project's accumulated enumeration knowledge. It catches a
generator regression — NH232, where a rebuild silently dropped 731 promoted
bodies — and cannot catch a body nobody ever discovered, which is absent from
every term of the comparison. That is why the hand-authored adversarial
questions are load-bearing rather than a supplement, and the wording now says
so where the stores are read, where the refusal lives, and in the harness.

**The ninth, found by reloading the workbook after the repair.** The owner has
filled the Adversarial questions tab. Five of the nine kept rows carry edits
that are REQUIREMENTS rather than replacement questions — *"As long as they are
clickable"*, *"Add a small clickable pill…"* — and `questionText: edit || draft`
promoted every one into the Ask box. Five of nine instances would have typed a
product requirement at the product and graded the answer. A replacement must
now END in a question mark or OPEN with an interrogative; merely CONTAINING one
reads the copy inside Q6's own suggested pill. Amendments are kept beside the
question and reported. And the loader now states that **9 of 9 templates carry
no typed expectation**, because a corpus that loads nine and evaluates zero is
a silent zero wearing a number.

**Owner corpus loaded.** Control facts: 3 of 17 rows CONFIRMED — EX, F1, F5 —
EX excluded by id as the workbook's own demonstration row. **2 loaded, both
`known_present`, 0 `known_absence`.** So the negative-control repair remains

### Workstream 3 — the freshness clock

`scheduleAll` returns two lists and the second is the point: an obligation
whose cadence data is broken comes back NAMED, never defaulted. *We have no
signal, so daily* is a decision recorded as `DEFAULT_NO_SIGNAL`; *this row's
data is broken* is a defect, and papering it over would satisfy RULING 212's
invariant by construction while leaving a hole in the clock.

Debt is durable, self-retrying and unnotified, with a capped backoff —
uncapped doubling converges to never checking again, which is
indistinguishable from having dropped it. Incidents aggregate by (cause,
target), so one host refusing 312 obligations is one incident with a size.

Dispatch chooses deterministic code where a graduated method exists, and the
answer is read from the method store rather than a string prefix. That exposed
**NH301**: nothing joins a meetings publisher to a method route, so all 78
resolve UNGRADUATED and the digest reads 0 deterministic, 8 bounded. Correct,
and not the end state — a prefix test would have answered GRADUATED and hidden
it.

**The shadow cycle ran twice.** 78 obligations from the committed corpus, 78
scheduled, 0 unscheduled, 8 due, 8 dispatched, 0 debt. The second cycle
registered 0 and found 78 already durable. The FIRST run crashed and was right
to: `createWorkItem` stamps `createdAt`, the id is a pure function of its
inputs, so cycle two offered one id carrying two values and the store raised
`IdentityCollision`. A standing obligation is registered once and scheduled
forever after.

**FRESHNESS now reports NOT_READY WITH A NUMBER.** That is not a step toward
green — it is what makes the NOT_READY checkable, because *we have not proved
this* and *we have not measured this* are different sentences and until now
only the second was available. `promotedToReaderTruth` is structurally false
and there is no parameter that could make it true.

The Postgres provider is implemented, conformance-tested against the two
providers that exist here, and its cutover proof is **escalated, not faked**:
`WTP_CONTROL_PLANE_DATABASE_URL` is not provisioned, so RULING 220's step 6 —
contention from both machines, crash/reclaim on Postgres, a restore drill — has
not been performed. **NH300** carries it. `pnpm control-plane:gate` reports
NOT_CONFIGURED and says that is not a pass.

`pnpm walk:wait-audit`: 26 waits, 26 satisfiable — the A.1 dead-selector class
is clear. **25 of 26 discard their result** (**NH302**), which is the other
half: a wait nobody reads cannot fail, so an unsatisfiable one costs the
ceiling and reports nothing. Converting 25 call sites to throw would red the
walk on any slow surface, which `until()` was written not to do — so every
timeout is now counted into the walk run record by label. A miss that cannot
fail can at least not be missed.

## 2026-08-31 — Session C, Part A: the write that told nobody, and the street that could not be typed

Session C was directed to deliver Parts A through J. **It delivered Part A**, and
Part H item 4, which turned out to be the same fix. What it did not reach is
listed in `docs/owner-audit/session-c.md` by Part and by item, and the ground it
measured for those Parts is in `docs/frontier.md`.

### The defect was reported four times and survived three fixes

WGH-12 and WGH-15 on 8/28, WGH-22 on 8/30, falsified again by the owner on
production on 8/31. Every previous pass corrected what the panel DERIVED from the
session address. The derivation was right each time.

**Measured first, on production, before anything was changed.** At `0bd520f3`,
typing the owner's own address the way a reader does: the panel did not move at
all. Before and after both `State House District 19`, `State Senate District 19`,
`AZ-6`, every row `UNSETTLED`.

### Two causes, and neither was the one that had been fixed three times

**The write told nobody.** `sessionStorage` fires its change event in every OTHER
tab and never in the tab that performed the write. `hooks/use-resolved-location.ts`
owned a `Set<() => void>` and handed it to `subscribeToStorage`; the two writers
live in `lib/geo/session-address.ts` and could not see it, so **nothing in the
tree ever iterated that set**. The only notification the hook could receive was
the cross-tab event, which by specification never arrives in the tab a reader is
using. The address control re-rendered from its own state — which is why the
banner read District 17 over a panel listing District 19. The listener set now
lives at the store boundary and both writers publish, so a future third writer
gets the notification by construction rather than by remembering.

**The address could not be confirmed on that street at all.** With no house
number the resolver probes a fixed ladder — 1, 50, 200, 800 — against the Census
range. The owner's road is numbered 10701–10899, so every probe missed, the
resolver returned `FAILED`, and the prompt told him it could not place his street
while offering no house-number field and no route to recovery. Telling a reader
their street could not be placed, on the strength of four guesses that missed, is
asserting an absence out of our own empty result. The prompt now ASKS. Both had
to be fixed: with the street unplaceable the panel could not have moved even with
the notification repaired, which is why the frontier's deferral of this as a
separate reader-facing gap could not have held.

### Why the instruments passed while it was live — this is the part worth keeping

1. A unit test whose fixture hand-built a `CoverageSummary` whose `divisions`
   carried 17 while its `seats` did not — a shape `summarizeCoverage` cannot
   emit, because it derives seats BY FILTERING divisions.
2. A sweep row closed against `rq:wgh-22-panel-seats`, which names nothing on
   disk.
3. **The walk block — a real browser, a real build, the real DOM, and still
   wrong.** It wrote the scope into `sessionStorage` and then DISPATCHED A
   SYNTHETIC `storage` EVENT. It measured every step downstream of the
   notification and manufactured the notification itself.

The third is the one to remember: fidelity of the harness is not fidelity of the
measurement. A test that supplies the missing signal proves everything except the
thing that is broken.

### What replaces them

`tests/session-address-publish.test.ts` asserts the publication and **fails
against the previous code** — checked by restoring the old files and running it,
not assumed. Its second test sweeps `hooks/`, `components/` and `lib/` for a
listener set nothing iterates, so the class is refused across the tree.

**The class audit found exactly one instance.** Ten browser-storage subscribers:
seven publish through a local listener set, `lib/ballot/picks.ts` publishes
through its own window event, and `reaction-control` and `shuffled-facts` are
deliberate non-subscribers that say so.

`scripts/walk-all.mts` gains an `SC0831` block that supplies NOTHING: it clicks
the pill a reader clicks, types into the field a reader types into, presses the
button, and reads the panel — same tab, no reload, no seeded storage, no
dispatched event. The expectation still comes from the product's own resolver,
because an answer key is not a supplied answer.

### Found while verifying, and fixed: the walk was destroying its own evidence

`scripts/walk-all.mts` built its run-record filename with a regex written inside
a TEMPLATE LITERAL, so the backslashes were consumed before `RegExp` saw them and
the pattern was `^<day>-(d+).json$` — matching a literal `d` where it meant any
digit. It matched nothing, the sequence stayed 0, and **every walk after the
first on a given day silently overwrote the previous run's record.** This
session's first walk destroyed the record the previous session had committed. It
was a third copy of `lib/health/run-records.ts`, which escapes correctly, and now
uses it (RULING 103). Proven by the repair: the verifying run wrote
`2026-08-31-02.json` and left `-01` intact.

### Verification

Walk on a local production build: **418 checks ran, 0 failures, 0 named
regressions, 0 silent check deaths.** At 85641 the panel moves from District 19
UNSETTLED to District 17 CONFIRMED on the reader's own typing; 07866 moves to
Assembly 25 / Senate 25 / NJ-11; both pass the revisit variant.

### Recorded and not fixed

**At 85701 and 03255 the who-governs card offers no way to settle what it says is
unsettled** — three UNSETTLED rows and no address control at all. WGH-7 made the
could-govern pill the single entry point, and it renders only where a row carries
the mark. The `SC0831` checks DECLARE `COULD NOT RUN` there naming the missing
field, so it is visible on every run rather than silent. Where that door belongs
is the author's call.

**A gate can fail without recording what failed.** Two gate runs recorded
`test FAIL` on a tree whose standalone runs were green five times over; both
failures were inside `handoff --ship`, which regenerates and commits the
digest-registered artifacts and then gates behind its own commit.
`data/ops/gate-runs/*.json` stores only `{id, command, status, seconds}`, so the
failing output is printed and discarded. Both failing records are committed
rather than dropped.

## 2026-08-31 — Session C, Part F: the wall was our own name

New Hampshire campaign finance now renders on the 03255 ballot. Nine candidates
carry filed totals read from the Secretary of State's Campaign Finance System —
Ayotte $5,995,303 raised, Warmington $888,257, Liot Hill $132,104, Harned
$77,861, Innis $36,100, Rogers $12,132, Sargent $1,295, and two sheriffs
reporting expenditures against no receipts. Nineteen more render a sourced,
dated absence. No candidate renders a zero.

### What the record said, and why it was load-bearing

`states/nh/sources.md` recorded the class as walled: HTTP 403 at rungs 2 and 3,
and — decisively — **`robots.txt` itself answered 403**, which left the
permission question UNANSWERED. **RULING 148 refuses a walk on an unanswered
permission question**, so the refusal was not a delay. It closed the fact class,
correctly, on the law's own terms. Tracker `NH40` recorded the one route that
had ever worked as "a procedure and not a script, so nothing in CI can repeat
it."

### Two measurements, and both were different

**THE 403 KEYS ON OUR OWN IDENTIFICATION.**
`https://www.sos.nh.gov/robots.txt` answers **HTTP 200 to a bare client and 403
to the identical request whose User-Agent carries this project's name.** The
file is an ordinary Drupal one: every `Disallow` is a CMS internal — `/core/`,
`/profiles/`, `/admin/`, `/user/login`, `/search/`, README files — and
**nothing in it disallows elections, campaign finance or the lobbyist
registry.** `cfs.sos.nh.gov` publishes no `robots.txt` at all: it returns its
Angular shell for that path byte-identically to a nonsense path, which is an
ABSENCE of published restrictions and is recorded as that rather than as a 200
that grants permission — a SPA catch-all is not a rule.

The existing `identified-agent-refused` route had already measured this across
the `nh.gov` family on 2026-08-26. What had not been done was applying it to the
PERMISSION READ, which is the read that gates every other one.

**CORS BINDS BROWSERS, NOT SERVERS.** The rung-7 route called the API "from the
page's own origin" because a browser must. A server is not subject to CORS at
all, and the same endpoint answers a plain POST with HTTP 200 and JSON. The
visible browser was never the load-bearing part of that procedure — the `Origin`
header was, and a server can simply send it.

### The reusable shapes, which are the part that travels

Both are in the method store (v61 → v63):

- `unanswered-permission-may-be-the-agent-not-the-host`: before recording a
  permission question as UNANSWERABLE, re-read `robots.txt` with the
  identification removed from the User-Agent and carried in `From:` and
  `X-Purpose:`. A 403 on `robots.txt` may be about our name, not the host.
- `ask-what-the-browser-was-for-before-recording-human-only`: when a working
  route requires a live browser, name what the browser SUPPLIED. CORS relief, an
  `Origin` header or a same-origin context can all be sent by a server, and the
  procedure becomes a script. JavaScript rendering, a session or a challenge
  cannot, and the human-only record stands.

**The two-client `robots.txt` read is worth running against any newly walled
host — it costs two requests and it unlocked a state. It is NOT a general
explanation for walls, and that was measured rather than assumed:** eight hosts
carrying a recorded wall or a CANNOT_TELL were re-read the same day with an
identified client and a bare one, and not one showed New Hampshire’s pattern.
`apps.arizona.vote`, `www.pimajted.org`, `services6.arcgis.com`, `asmi.az.gov`
and `azed.gov` refuse both clients equally — a transport wall, CANNOT_TELL under
RULING 182, never a disallow — and `azdor.gov` and `www.pima.gov` serve their
robots.txt to both. The NH route is agent discrimination on one host family, and
the frontier carries the table.

### The join, and the guards on it

The endpoint honours only `filerName`, so every other filter runs locally. Each
row carries the COMMITTEE name and, separately, **the candidate's own name** —
which is what makes it joinable at all. `docs/body-or-intermediary-audit.md`
records NH's hazard exactly: candidates file under legal names and serve under
working names, so a committee-name join fails every committee-style filer.
Matching `Daniel Innis` against the ballot's `Daniel E. Innis` is a
person-to-person comparison, and `judgeMatch` still demands name AND office AND
year.

`officeClassOf` needed New Hampshire's vocabulary, and one of the three gaps was
not an absence but a WRONG ANSWER: **`Executive Council` matched the MUNICIPAL
rule's `council`**, so a statewide executive council classified as a town
council — and a wrong class is the one thing `officesAgree` cannot defend
against, because two wrong classes agree with each other. `state senate` also
did not match `State Senator` (the word boundary fails against the `r`), and
`State Representative` matched nothing at all, which is most of a New Hampshire
ballot. Widened, not loosened: agreement still demands two equal classes.

Two guards were added ON TOP of the shared bar, because `judgeMatch` compares an
office class and never a district: a filer whose `town` names a different county
is refused, and where both sides state a district they must be equal. A row that
is a different person is dropped; a row that IS this person and disagrees is a
LEAD, which never renders; only when nothing survives is the candidate recorded
as a sourced absence.

### What is deliberately not here

Federal contests. A candidate for the United States Senate or the House files
with the FEC, which this product already reads. Asking a state regulator about a
federal seat and recording the silence would manufacture a gap.

Contribution and expenditure DETAIL. Only filer-level totals are taken; the
itemised endpoints are unwalked. Rung 13, the Department's public-records path,
remains unwalked and has been named as a next start since 2026-08-19. And the
lobbyist registry — a source class this product holds nothing of in any state
except Arizona — sits on a host now known to be permitted.

## 2026-08-31 — Session C, Part E: the Arizona route opened, and the obvious answer was refuted

Arizona statewide money is REACHABLE and NO SNAPSHOT WAS BUILT. Both halves of
that sentence are the finding.

**The route.** `seethemoney.az.gov/Reporting/GetNEWTableData` was recorded on
2026-08-24 as live with its parameter shape UNKNOWN — a guessed body answered
200 with two bytes, correctly recorded under RULING 100 as a statement about our
request rather than about Arizona's records. Rung 7 was named as the next rung
and had not been walked.

Walked. It is a server-side **DataTables** action: filters ride in the query
string appended to the path, and the POST body must be the DataTables form
encoding **including its `columns[N][data]` array**, because that array is the
projection the action builds its result from. The three missing filters were
`IsLessActive`, `ShowOfficeHolder` and `ChartName`. With them it returns
`recordsTotal` **370** for the 2025–2026 cycle at `JurisdictionId=0`, each row
carrying `EntityID`, first and last name, `CommitteeName`, `OfficeName`,
`PartyName`, `Income`, `Expense` and `CashBalance`. `EntityID` is the non-name
join key the contract wants. Permission re-confirmed: no `robots.txt`, no terms,
no challenge, no credential.

**The refutation, which is why there is no file.** A candidate returns several
rows sharing one `EntityID` with different amounts and an identical
`CashBalance`. On Jayme Accalia the arithmetic looked like proof: incomes
686.91 + 205 + 1123.97 = 2015.88, expenses 101 + 0 + 466.73 = 567.73, and
2015.88 − 567.73 = **1448.15**, exactly the repeated cash balance.

Checked over all 370 rows in 255 entities, `sum(Income) − sum(Expense) ==
CashBalance` **holds for 134 and breaks for 121** — including for single-row
entities, where there is nothing to sum at all. `CashBalance` carries something
the 2025–2026 window does not, a prior-cycle balance being the obvious
candidate, and Accalia matched because she began from zero.

**The lesson is the one this whole session is about.** A single case agreeing
with a hypothesis is not evidence for the hypothesis, and the check that
refuted it cost one query over the population. Had the snapshot been built on
the seductive version, it would have put a confident wrong number under a named
candidate's photograph — and every instrument downstream would have agreed with
it, because they all read the same file.

**What is owed and where it points.** A source that states a cycle total
independently: `ExportEntityTransactions` (itemised and therefore summable), the
filed reports themselves, or `ftp://ftp.azsos.gov/cfsdata2/`, already recorded
as reachable on 2026-08-26 with 8,828 committees and unwalked for this purpose.
The FTP is the most promising. The obligation is not closed and was never
dispositioned as closed.

## 2026-09-01 — Session C, closeout: the join, the denominator, the rasteriser, and a permission we never checked

Five lanes in parallel, one integration owner, one merge at the end.
`data/workstate/orchestration/2026-09-01-session-c-closeout.json` records the
plan: 5 workstreams, 5 executable, **5 PARALLEL, 0 serialized**, 10 independent
pairs, verdict TEAM.

### Three rulings, adopted through the canonical ledger

**RULING 229 — acquire to the authoritative source universe; project to the
reader.** The author observed the same architecture error independently in three
states, and it was in the code with its own header saying so:

```
  scripts/state-money-az.mts   "FOR THE 85701 AND 85641 BALLOT"
  scripts/state-money-nh.mts   "FOR THE 03255 BALLOT", COUNTY = "Merrimack"
  scripts/state-money-nj.mts   "NJ ELEC FOR THE WHOLE 07866 BALLOT"
```

Each is a correct answer to the wrong question. The Arizona Secretary of State
does not publish a Pima County universe. A collector that asks it only about the
candidates on one page has not been limited by the publisher — **it has limited
itself, and then the limit becomes invisible because every page it was built for
looks full.** The invariant is ZERO REDUNDANT INTERNET HUNT WHEN A NEW ZIP IS
ACTIVATED, and the three layers — acquisition, identity, projection — are kept
apart.

**RULING 230 — one canonical model-switch verdict**, and **RULING 231 — a false
description of a named person is corrected by recorded supersession**, which
answers the `tracker amend` question the frontier had been carrying as *"that
needs a ruling"*.

### Arizona money reached the reader, and nothing was acquired to do it

`state-money-az-2026.json` held Katie Hobbs at **$11,109,719.95** and her card
showed nothing. Certified-lineup cards key on `${contest.id}|${nominee.name}`;
money records key on candidacy ids. **Two correct halves, one seam, and the seam
is the only place it could fail** — which is RULING 228's shape one layer down
from a producer/consumer contract.

The repair is one precomputed, auditable reconciliation over the whole lineup
population, resolving into a **statewide** identity registry:

```
  lineup nominees 30 = uniquely reconciled 27 + ambiguous 1 + unmatched 2
  duplicate target collisions 0 — and a collision REFUSES the write
```

No fuzzy or runtime matching reaches the reader. Published names expand into
exact strings, each labelled with the annotation rule that produced it, compared
by string equality, once, into a committed table. Negative controls are
asserted: `Tom Horne` does not match `Thomas Chalres Horne`, `Katie Hobbs` does
not match `Katherine Hobbs`, and no diminutive is ever inferred.

Measured on rendered DOM, before and after:

```
  85701   4 money sections of 24 cards  ->  24 of 24  (19 filed, 3 our gap, 2 federal)
  85641   4 of 29                       ->  29 of 29  (22 filed, 3 our gap, 4 federal)
```

**One case costs a reader a real number, and it is recorded rather than
resolved.** Teri Ann Hourihan is *No Labels* on Arizona's certified canvass and
*Arizona Independent Party* on the Secretary of State's candidate-filing list.
Two Arizona authorities disagree, the party criterion blocks the mapping, and
her card renders our gap although the corpus holds her filed figure. That is the
rule working — one wrong join puts a candidate's fundraising on their opponent's
card — and both published values are in the reconciliation for the author.

And the denominator moved from a ballot to a publisher: **58 committees chosen
by name-matching the Pima ballot became 716 of 716 chosen by the publisher**,
0 disagreeing, 0 route gaps, over an 860-row / 732-entity cycle universe. No
itemised transaction was persisted — contributor name, occupation, employer,
city and zip were streamed to a sum and discarded, asserted on the committed
bytes.

### The fly-in on a reader with no GPU, and why the first table was unreadable

`--isolate --repeat=3` produced a table where **`no-districts` came back SLOWER
than the fully loaded app**. Removing work made the flight worse, which is not a
finding about districts — it is a load burst wearing one. Arms are BLOCKS in
that mode, and the host sat at 100% during four of them.

A rotated mode fixed the instrument before the instrument was believed: every
arm flown once per round, rotation order advanced each round. 28 flights later
the culprit is **one CSS property** — `.state-focus-scrim`'s `backdrop-filter` is
+13.9 fps of the +14.8 that removing the entire state-focus layer buys, 94% of
that layer's cost. Districts +6.3. SVG art +3.8 on median but nearly all the
residual jank. **Markers +0.6, which is inside their own spread and therefore
names nothing**, reported as naming nothing.

Corroborated independently: **1762 ms of `(program)` self time inside a 2768 ms
flight**, every named JS function under 40 ms. Per-frame raster, never our
JavaScript.

```
  hardware (Intel Iris Xe)   59.9 vs 59.7 = 100.3%, jank 2.0%   PASS, no regression
  software (SwiftShader)     59.9 vs 59.8 = 100.1%, jank 1.5%   PASS, was 28.8%
```

**The intermediate result is the argument for the criterion.** With only the blur
and districts stood down, software reached 89% of bare and still dropped 24.7% of
frames at p95 97.3 ms. The median called that finished; it was not. The software
verdict therefore requires ratio AND jank, and the two populations are never
averaged.

A second instrument defect fell out of it: `no-districts` was **healing
mid-flight** exactly as `bare` did before 2026-08-31, filing a fully loaded
flight under the districts' name. Every run now reads its landing state back and
discards a healed flight — and it fired on the integrated head, declining the
hardware arm rather than passing it.

### A permission we had never checked, on a host we had been calling WIRED

A lane registering a NEW Wikipedia route read `en.wikipedia.org/robots.txt`
before shipping it. Under `User-agent: *`:

```
  Allow: /w/api.php?action=mobileview&
  Allow: /w/load.php?
  Disallow: /w/
```

Two `Allow` lines, neither a content query. **Every Wikipedia call this
repository has ever made ran through `/w/api.php?action=query`** — `lib/hunt/
wikipedia.ts` and `lib/hunt/wiki-graph.ts` — while `docs/sources.md` recorded the
host as Tier A and WIRED. Ten requests reached the disallowed path before the
lane caught its own route.

**The row was never checked against the host's own file.** A permission claim
resting on our own paperwork rather than on the publisher's is not a permission
claim, and this is worse than an unread wall: the host answers `/w/api.php` with
200 all day, so nothing would ever have failed.

It is RULING 206 rather than a wall. `/wiki/<Title>?action=raw` is another
representation of the same record, is not under `Disallow: /w/`, and returns the
same bytes — measured on `Tucson, Arizona`: `200 text/x-wiki`, 183,138 bytes.
Both modules now read it, the redirect the API's `redirects=1` was carrying is
followed explicitly (`Template:NJ Morris County Commissioners` → lowercase
`commissioners`, the case the old doc block named), and
`tests/wikipedia-permission.test.ts` refuses the path repo-wide over what WOULD
BE COMMITTED rather than over what is tracked.

**One thing narrowed and is stated rather than absorbed.** `prop=categories`
returned the categories a page lands in AFTER template expansion;
`[[Category:…]]` in wikitext is only what the article declares itself. Fewer
categories, in the safe direction — a node classified as less certain rather than
as something it is not.

### OWN03 closed through the mechanism, not around it

The author approved nine portraits. RULING 37 reserves a Needs Sean close to
him, and the only mechanism for his close is a keystroke in the workbook — which
a session writing it would be forging. So OWN03 became a **RULING 227
predicate** on a distinction its old card ran together: *the approval is
reserved to him; whether he has GIVEN it is not.* It reads `review.json`,
resolves only when all nine carry APPROVED against that exact image decided by
him, and closes as `predicate` rather than as `sean`.

Its first draft put a false blocker back in front of him — a lost regex escape
keyed `Dale G. Caldwell` to a double-spaced string, and six of nine read
unapproved on the day he approved all nine. A test now runs `registry.mjs`'s own
inlined key TEXT against `lib/photos/person.ts` over every queued subject.

And the promotion refused once, correctly: Wix content-negotiates Kimberly Yee's
portrait on `Accept`, returning a **different 22,544-byte webp** at the same
326×468 where the author approved a 36,019-byte JPEG. Same photograph, different
file. The ask was narrowed to the reviewed format; the guard was not loosened.

### Where the numbers landed

```
  tracker            378 open · 69 Needs Sean, all carded · 477 resolved
  suite              4,562 tests   ← see below; this read 4,555 and 4,555 was
                                     a true count of a SMALLER RUN
  gates              14 of 14
  walk:all           444 passed, 0 regressions, 23 could not run
  governance         268 records, 0 semantic conflicts, 0 structural issues
  governments named  2,641 across AZ (688), NH (552) and NJ (1,401)
```

**The suite count was corrected on 2026-09-01, and the correction is more
interesting than the number.** This line read `4,555` while the close-out for
the same tree reported `4,562`, and the gate record could not adjudicate them
because it never persisted suite totals.

Neither number was wrong. They are the same tree measured two ways:

```
  4,555   this tree, WITHOUT the Postgres lane
  4,562   this tree, WITH it   ← the complete count, and what this line now says
```

The seven-test difference is a lane gated behind an environment variable. The
same test file registers **18** tests when the suite runs without
`--env-file=.env.local` and **25** with it; all seven additions are named
`postgres:`. A bare shell does not load `.env.local`, so a session that ran the
suite directly and a session that loaded the env file counted different
denominators and both reported honestly.

**What made it unresolvable was that nothing recorded which run had happened.**
`scripts/gates.mjs` now persists `suiteTotals` on the SUCCESS path as well as on
failure, records an unreadable total as `read: false` with a reason rather than
as `0`, and records `suiteLaneEnv` — each lane-gating variable's PRESENCE, never
its value. Without that last field, a skipped lane and seven deleted tests look
exactly alike.

## 2026-09-01 — Session C (final directive)

**Three instruments reported clean results while looking at nothing, and a
registry had been calling one county's ballot a state.**

Eleven items, five lanes in isolated worktrees off one base commit, one
integration owner, one merge. `orchestration:check` reports TEAM: 6 workstreams,
12 independent pairs, 0 serialized.

### What a reader can now see that they could not before

**The product has an identity.** A lowercase serif wordmark, two grey dots, one
filled square — *while you were living an ordinary week, decisions got made.*
The map pin is gone from both places it appeared, and it had been wearing two
different wrong colours: `var(--link)`, the accent that means "tappable", in the
welcome overlay; and `var(--accent-local)`, a **tier** colour a reader learns
from the map legend, in the sidebar. The second was not in the brief and nobody
had noticed it.

**The "Where can I vote?" panel has a border again**, and so do its input, its
jurisdiction rule, its site cards and its two refusal blocks. Measured in a
browser: `border-top-style: none` before, `solid` after.

**Ask answers are written by `claude-sonnet-5`**, and on the two hardest
canonical questions a reader gets an answer where they previously got none.

**The site is at `https://meanwhileusa.com`**, and the old host now forwards
instead of serving a parallel copy of the whole application.

**What a reader does NOT see, and it is the largest owed thing:** 211 newly
acquired Arizona candidates. They are `ACQUIRED → EXTRACTED → NORMALIZED →
CANONICALLY_LINKED`, and nothing in `app/` reads them. Under RULING 224 that is
a **defect**, retroactively, not future work.

### The registry had been calling one county's ballot a state

Every candidate registry was built from a pilot ballot document — Pima,
Merrimack, Morris — and labelled statewide. Each individual statement about it
was true and correctly recorded; the LABEL was the defect, and RULING 232 is now
the rule: *"No ZIP in the key" is a property of the key, not of the population.*

Arizona is fixed by acquisition rather than by relabelling: the Secretary of
State's 2026 filing list, vaulted with provenance, **266 candidacies across 76
contests, established twice by independent mechanisms** — positional table
recovery, and filing-date tokens counted out of the text layer — with the
adapter refusing to write when the two disagree. **55 → 266**, zero identities
lost, all 44 committee identities preserved.

New Hampshire and New Jersey are fixed by telling the truth about them. NH's
document is retrieved and hashed and its pages are **rotated**, so the generic
table layer reads each column as a row and returns `ZERO_ROWS`; a prototype
recovered 1,268 rows whose segmentation could not be verified and **was not
shipped**. NJ's Division of Elections files **federal office only** — that
state's universe is the union of that authority and **21 county clerks**, so no
acquisition of those documents alone could ever have earned the word. Both are
`REQUIRES_NEW_ADAPTER` with the wall named; both populations are now
`PILOT_DERIVED`.

### Three instruments that were reporting cleanly while looking at nothing

This is the through-line of the session, and it was three separate discoveries
before it was a pattern.

1. **The model-comparison harness FILTERED incomparable questions out** instead
   of carrying them as unmeasured. `switchVerdict` refuses a run carrying
   `held: null` and refuses an empty set — both correct, and both blind to a
   question that never reached it. So the denominator shrank in silence: the
   effort sweep emitted `SWITCH` over three surviving rows at `xhigh` and over
   **one** at `max`, and the record reported `questions: 1` as though that had
   been the plan.
2. **`--regenerate` read the arm names from today's constants**, which the model
   switch had just swapped. Re-deriving a pre-switch record stamped a real
   measurement with **reversed roles** — rows saying `incumbent: claude-opus-5`
   came back as `incumbentModel: claude-sonnet-5`. Three such records were
   written and **deleted**; the path now refuses a mismatch and prints the
   command that would be correct.
3. **A stylesheet sweep reported ZERO `var()` references across 1,428 rules.**
   Chromium's nested-CSS support gives every ordinary rule an empty-but-truthy
   `cssRules`, so the walker recursed into nothing 1,428 times. The repaired
   sweep walks 1,177 references and is what found a live undeclared-token rule
   the source sweep could not see.

**The open question underneath all three** is on the frontier: this project has
many sweeps, and nothing systematically asks a sweep to prove it looked.

### A stale blocker had been sitting in the owner's queue

`NS12` said there was no Netlify credential on this machine. There is, and
`pnpm deploy:live` answers in full. The row never noticed because it was
**carded** `NOT_MACHINE_VERIFIABLE` — which HOLDS by construction, since the
machine never asks again — while its blocker was "does a credential resolve?",
which a machine can decide perfectly well. That is the exact failure RULING 227
was adopted over, surviving inside the mechanism built to prevent it. It is now
a predicate reading a committed artifact, and `tracker:views` auto-resolved it.

The same sweep found **two decision cards pointing at git refs that no longer
exist**, one of which said in as many words that its branch must not be deleted
unread. The work is not lost — GitHub still serves the tip `33f6f520` by SHA —
and both cards now name the SHA instead of the vanished ref.

### The rulings

**RULING 232** (`R-C9`) labelling · **RULING 233** (`R-C10`) staging-first,
adopted and **not operative until the session after this one** · **RULING 234**
(`R-C11`) the owner's override of the H2 `RETAIN` verdict, for the Sonnet 5
switch only · **RULING 235** a FACT, not a law.

RULING 235 is worth reading for how it came about. Netlify derives a branch
deploy's hostname as `<branch>.<suffix>`, so RULING 233's two halves — branch
`staging`, host `test.meanwhileusa.com` — cannot both hold. The amendment was
drafted, and **the governance validator refused it**: *a LAW_DECISION requires
author provenance.* A session does not legislate. So the measurement is recorded
as a FACT that explicitly declines to amend, RULING 233 stands as the author
wrote it, and `NH304` carries the choice to him with both options.

### SESSION C DOES NOT CLOSE — three items are UNFINISHED

**ITEM A.** Arizona was acquired from the authoritative source universe; **New
Hampshire and New Jersey were not.** Relabelling them `PILOT_DERIVED` /
`REQUIRES_NEW_ADAPTER` satisfies R-C9 honesty and does **not** satisfy Item A,
which requires migration to each state's authoritative candidate-filing
universe. An honestly named wall is not completion.

**ITEM K.** `ASK_SYNTHESIS_MODEL` is `claude-opus-5`. The switch was made,
measured, and reverted the same day under RULING 234's own clause — correctly.
But the directive's acceptance requires production serving `claude-sonnet-5`,
so the item cannot also be called complete. **Readers get `claude-opus-5`.**

**THE RUNNER, and this session broke it.** The shared control-plane database was
migrated to schema v3 from a worktree while the runner executes from the main
checkout on pre-session code declaring v2. That module refuses undeclared tables
by design, so it shut itself down: `control-plane:gate` REFUSED there, cycles
exited NON-ZERO from ~19:56Z, digests read `0 providers, 0 units`. The same gate
PASSES at this head. **Expand-first is only safe when the old code tolerates the
new schema** — true of the additive Drizzle column, false of the control-plane
bootstrap. The repair is this merge; verification can only follow it.

### And the acceptance package did not survive its own audit

Ten skeptics were run against this session's acceptance claims, told to REFUTE
rather than confirm, with every finding handed to a second agent told to show
the first was wrong. **71 agents, 89 claims, 60 raised, 40 CONFIRMED BROKEN.**
Full record: `docs/evidence/session-c-refutation-2026-09-01.json`.

It found, among others: a count printed as `301` where the artifact it cited
says `342`; a "plant-check both ways" with no red arm; an admin self-check whose
`stated` and `rendered` are the same expression, so it can never fail; and an
Item B verification command that produces a SKIP rather than the stated result.

**The pass is itself fallible and was spot-checked rather than believed** — one
CONFIRMED_BROKEN finding is wrong on its facts, and one was stale. The number to
carry is not "40 defects" but that this package asserted things it had not
verified at a rate an independent pass could detect.

## 2026-09-01 — the autonomy-recovery session: the runner could not survive its own backlog

*(One subject, one planned merge, under the SESSION EFFICIENCY LAW adopted this
session as RULING 237. Branch `claude/autonomy-recovery-efficiency-616f07`.)*

### What a reader can now see that they could not before

**Nothing new on the page — and that is the honest lead.** This session touched
no reader surface. A reader loading the ballot sees what they saw yesterday.
What changed is that the machine that keeps civic records fresh can now work
through its own backlog without a person, which is the precondition for
anything reaching a reader unattended.

### What the machine now does unattended, and the defect it had

**The autonomous runner was in a death loop it could not leave.** Diagnosed by
reproduction — one `freshness-shadow` cycle, single process, against the real
control plane, output captured (the runner had been discarding it):

```
AppendOnlyViolation: cp_log_artifacts already contains record ar-0a63a288…
  recorded: attemptId at-b878b386…  recordedAt 2026-09-01T19:45:40Z
  offered:  attemptId at-3ed9ceec…  recordedAt …T03:19:23Z, the next UTC day
  (same artifactId, contentHash, byteLength, canonicalUrl, routeTaskId)
```

A resumed occurrence re-walked a route whose prior observation was already
recorded, retrieved byte-identical content, and offered the SAME
content-addressed artifact under a new Attempt. The append-only log refused the
differing `attemptId`/`recordedAt` as a history rewrite; the throw was
unhandled; the whole cycle exited 1 with no run record; the digest read
"0 providers, 0 units" — indistinguishable from an idle night — and every
crash-restart re-resumed the same occurrence into the same death. Seven hours
of `exit NON-ZERO` digests, `docs/evidence/autonomy-recovery-cycle-pre-fix-2026-09-01.txt`.

**Fixed at the shared code path, four ways:**

1. `recordArtifactMetadata` treats a content-identical re-observation as
   idempotent — the first observation's attribution stands, nothing is
   rewritten — and STILL refuses a different-content collision under one
   content-derived id. `tests/artifact-reobservation.test.ts`, 3 of 3.
2. `runCycle` isolates one obligation's unexpected throw to a FAILED dispatch
   (debt accrues, the obligation stays owed) instead of aborting the cycle and
   stranding every other due occurrence; the occurrence open/resume loop does
   the same and records what it skipped.
3. A crashed cycle writes a legible FAILED run record and prints the
   `run record:` line the runner greps, so the digest says a cycle CRASHED and
   why. Measured on this runtime: a rejected top-level `await` fires
   `uncaughtException`, so both process events are handled.
4. A cycle stops STARTING work at an injected dispatch budget (`--budget-min`,
   default 15 from process start) and ends clean inside the runner's 20-minute
   kill, deferring the rest by name. `tests/cycle-budget.test.ts`, 3 of 3, with
   a moved clock. The runner now surfaces the child's stderr tail and kill
   signal into the digest on a non-zero exit, and the headline says
   "dispatch budget SPENT" when that is why little was dispatched.

**Proof over the real backlog, read back from the durable store, not from the
process under test** (`docs/evidence/autonomy-recovery-readback-before-2026-09-01.txt`
and the after-reading in this section):

| | before | after one post-fix cycle |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| standing obligations, carrying a next-due | 2,996 of 2,996 | 2,996 of 2,996 |
| obligations with at least one occurrence | 1,144 | 1,144 |
| occurrences | 1,447 | 1,452 |
| occurrences closed with a committed disposition | 55 | **77** |
| occurrences whose RouteTask is disposed | 393 | **470** |
| INGESTED dispositions | 69 | **91** |
| REQUIRES_NEW_ADAPTER / BLOCKED_CURRENTLY | 305 / 19 | 359 / 20 |
| debt rows (walls, each with a retry time) | 96 | 149 |

The post-fix cycle: exit 0, 17m00s, dispatched 100 — 22 DISCHARGED, 23 failed
and recorded as debt with backoff, 55 disposed as walls, 2,805 deferred under
the stated ceiling. Zero active obligations have an unknown next-due, before
or after. `docs/evidence/autonomy-recovery-cycle-post-fix-2026-09-01.txt`.

**Cycle time was a second seam, and it is closed by construction.** That
17-minute cycle ran 3 minutes short of the runner's 20-minute kill, on Neon
latency alone — about ten minutes of it opening/resuming 100 occurrences
serially. A kill mid-dispatch leaks open occurrences and repeats. Run through
the real `pilot:run` path with a deliberately tiny 3-minute budget, the
overhead exceeded the budget and the cycle ended CLEAN: exit 0, 2,883 deferred
by name, record written, digest delivered
(`data/health/freshness-shadow-runs/2026-09-01-10.json`).

**Kill-9 recovery, with no manual command.** A cycle (`--max=30`) was started,
allowed to open its occurrences — 30, of which 5 resumed and 25 new — and reach
dispatch, then killed with `Stop-Process -Force` (TerminateProcess: no handler
ran, no run record was written, the wrapper saw exit 127). The next cycle,
started with the same command and nothing else, resumed 28 of those 30 open
occurrences, reclaimed the one lease that had expired with its Attempt closed
LEASE_EXPIRED, dispatched 30 (1 discharged, 13 walls disposed, the rest recorded
as debt with a retry time), wrote 25 staged entries and its run record, and
exited 0 in 10m33s. Nothing was cleared by hand.
`docs/evidence/autonomy-recovery-kill9-victim-2026-09-01.txt` and
`…-kill9-recovery-2026-09-01.txt`.

**Refuted on the exact row that killed the pre-fix cycle**, read back from the
store (`docs/evidence/autonomy-recovery-colliding-row-readback-2026-09-01.txt`):
its RouteTask had been disposed INGESTED at 19:36Z by the attempt that recorded
the artifact, and then carried SEVEN orphan Attempts with no outcome — one per
dead cycle from 20:56Z to the 03:09Z reproduction — because the occurrence was
never closed and every cycle resumed it, re-claimed the settled task, re-walked,
re-recorded and died. The post-fix cycle's attempt on the same row closed
ABORTED (the second disposition was refused by the domain and handled), the
occurrence closed, and the artifact log still holds exactly one record. That is
the fix exercised on the row that needed it, not inferred.

**What is NOT proved here, said plainly.** The Scheduled Task runs from the
MAIN checkout, so the fixed code is not what the task runs until this merge
lands and main is fast-forwarded. The proofs above ran the same child the task
spawns, from the worktree. Whether Windows relaunches a killed PARENT runner
under `RestartCount 999` is unmeasured — task history is disabled on this host
— and both start mechanisms (the task and the older per-user startup entry)
are present, which is the owner's call (tracker `RO08`'s neighbour, carried
from Session C as SC-06).

### The admin login: the expected defect does not reproduce

The directive expected a redirect defect on `admin.meanwhileusa.com`. A full
owner login readback against the LIVE host — `pnpm admin:login-readback`, the
secret read by name and never printed — passed 6 of 6 hops: anonymous
dashboard → `/admin/login?why=NO_COOKIE`; login POST → 303 to `/admin` with the
`__Host-` cookie (Path, Max-Age, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite); dashboard with
the session → 200 rendering "Pilot health"; admin API with the session → not
401; public host with the session → 404; sign-out → 204.
`data/ops/admin-login-readback.json`. Session C's ITEM H shipped this flow on
2026-09-01; the premise was stale. No code changed for it. The 33 seeded
admin checks pass. One observation recorded for later: Netlify scopes the
admin secret and session key to `functions` only.

Runs 33517560447 (2026-09-01) and 33636708298 (2026-09-02) both exited the

before committing"; Commit was skipped, so the prior Commit-step failures

(the clerk's removal, 2026-09-02 only), and the source stamp on

a red suite the failing test files are attributed to sources by reverting one

suite output instead of an API that cannot serve a running job's log.

### Post-merge procedure (the integration owner's, after this head merges)

1. Fast-forward the main checkout; the runner's next cycle spawns the new
   child code; kill the parent once so the window scheduler is live
   (the trigger relaunches it).
2. `pnpm control-plane:bootstrap` with the env loaded (the live control plane
   is already at schema v5 from the shadow window; the v4 runner had been

3. `gh workflow run refresh-daily.yml --repo SeanJ22/we-the-people --field all_sources=true`,
   watch it, read back the bot's commit on `main`, `docs/refresh-run.json`
   (`gate.verdict` GREEN, no `ROUTE_UNREAD`), and the per-source as-of fields
   before/after (`generatedAt`, `curatedAt`, `fetchedAt`, `datasetHash`,
   `source.sha`). The NEXT scheduled run is NH309's closure, not this session's.
4. `pnpm admin:login-readback` reports the Google path NOT_CONFIGURED by name
   until NH310 is done; the shared secret is a break-glass behind
   `WTP_ADMIN_BREAK_GLASS=enabled` only.

## 2026-09-02 — provider transition: preparing the repository for a Codex session

*(Session `codex/provider-transition-2026-09-02`, branch off `origin/main`. The
owner is moving the next engineering session from Claude Code to OpenAI Codex.
This is transition infrastructure, not new product scope. The one planned merge
of the prior session already shipped (PR #263); this change rides its own
next-session branch and is NOT a second merge.)*

### What changed, and why it is mechanical

`AGENTS.md` — the file a coding agent that is not Claude Code reads first — now
carries the whole root constitution, byte-for-byte, as a GENERATED mirror. The
generator is `lib/ops/agents-mirror.mjs`; `pnpm agents:sync` writes it and
`pnpm agents:check` reports staleness by line. It is registered in
`lib/ops/generated-register.ts` as a pure artifact, so
`tests/generated-artifacts.test.ts` regenerates it in place and compares bytes
every gate run (RULING 92, RULING 102); the pre-commit hook and the closeout
checklist run the check too. A stale or hand-edited mirror fails all three
(`tests/agents-parity.test.ts` seeds each way). The mirror preserves the
Next.js-owned `<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->` block verbatim and never
invents it; its notice states that it is NOT an authority, that `CLAUDE.md`
wins over it, and that `docs/governance/ledger.jsonl` wins over `CLAUDE.md`
(RULING 185). Delegated policies under `docs/governance/policies/` are not
copied — they stay where they are.

The invariant, now enforced rather than remembered:

> Everything operative in the root `CLAUDE.md` is supplied to a non-Claude
> coding agent through the root `AGENTS.md`, and a change to one that does not
> update the other fails a gate.

### Session bootstrap and closeout are the same for any provider

Nothing a session needs to resume lives in a provider's transcripts, memory, or
tools; it all lives in committed machinery. A Codex session opens the repo and
runs, in order:

```
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile           node_modules (a worktree has none)
pnpm session:start --check               stale main, clobbered CLAUDE.md, port, hooks
git fetch origin && git rev-parse origin/main    the exact current main SHA
pnpm governance:open --task <domain>     current authority, policy, decisions, snapshot
pnpm workstream:status                   canonical work state and the exact resume cursor
pnpm tracker:open                        what is open, what Needs Sean, the author's notes
pnpm stamp                               every date a session writes
```

The session directive sets the acceptance denominator (RULING 223); the SESSION
EFFICIENCY LAW's bootstrap requirement (RULING 237) turns it into the finite
table. Parallel work runs in isolated checkouts with named file ownership — the
law names no vendor (RULING 190), so `git worktree` or Codex's own mechanism
both satisfy it — and one integration owner merges once (RULING 191). Closeout
is `pnpm gates` (the fourteen CI gates), then `pnpm handoff` (regenerates the
standing views, syncs the Drive mirror, records the exact SHA in
`git-state.txt`), then push and a PR that the ruleset merges only when green
(RULING 1, RULING 155). `pnpm handoff --check` is non-mutating and reports the
whole checklist; `pnpm handoff --ship` is the one-command close and is the ONLY
path that merges.

### What is provider-specific, and what happens to it under Codex

Two closeout steps read Claude Code's own files and DEGRADE harmlessly when
Codex runs them, by design — neither fails the run:

- `pnpm handoff`'s transcript export shells out to
  `~/.claude/export-transcript.mjs`. Absent under Codex, it prints
  `warn transcripts — exporter not found` and the run continues; the mirror's
  `transcripts/` folder simply is not refreshed by that step.
- `pnpm secrets:sweep --transcripts` scans a hard-coded Claude transcript path.
  Under Codex that path is `NOT PRESENT` and is skipped; the repository and the
  Drive mirror are still swept by value, which is the load-bearing part.

The branch-name guard (`scripts/check-branch-names.mjs`) now recognises
`codex/…` branch prefixes as well as `claude/…`, so a Codex branch referenced
in tracker prose is validated rather than invisible.
